title: WAKE-UP STATE 2026-08-12: appearance asymmetry unverified, balanced-links arm interrupted
description:
Machine slept mid-experiment. Exact state:

(1) APPEARANCE ASYMMETRY — UNRESOLVED, and do NOT read the number as a result yet. Budget-preserving sweep of LinkerConfig.appearance_cost (flow-only; births vs deaths priced apart, frontier ships appearance 0.0 / disappearance 1.5 against our symmetric 3). Arm B (appearance 0.0, disappearance 6.0, so the SUM matches the symmetric control's 3+3) measured clamped 0.9353 — IDENTICAL to the control to four decimals. That is the same signature that turned out to be a dead code path twice today (edge_blend never reaching the scorer; the accumulate test comparing two save-best inits). A plumbing check was launched and never read: 'python -m celltrack.eval.proxy_eval --set linker.appearance_cost=60.0' — an absurd charge MUST move the score; if it does not, the knob does not arrive and the 0.9353 means nothing. RUN THAT FIRST on wake.
   Remaining arms if the knob is live: (1.5, 4.5) and the REVERSED (4.5, 1.5). The reversed arm is the falsifier — if the frontier's direction is a real mechanism, reversing it should LOSE. Without it, a win is just knob-moving.

(2) BALANCED-LINKS ARM — killed by the sleep, partial. joint_det_bal.pt, same recipe as joint_det_acc8 plus --balanced-links. Matched init (0.8476, 64 mislinks, P_true 0.191). Only window read: step 400 = sel 0.8516, mislinks 53, P_true 0.167, P_chosen 0.568, inverted 0.91 — against the unbalanced arm's 0.8531 / 52 / 0.161 / 0.560 / 0.94 at the same step. A TIE at one window; the pre-registered falsifier (does P_true stop falling while P_chosen keeps falling?) needs the LATER windows, since the unbalanced arm's P_true collapse only became stark by step 1600. Re-run the full epoch.

(3) BEST OWN-WEIGHTS = joint_det_acc8.pt at 0.9266 faithful / 46 mislinks / node recall 0.9968 held out on the test four. Still below shipped dual-seed 0.9334, so NOT submittable.

(4) v28 (division budget derived, no fork cap) still PENDING on the leaderboard. 2 submission slots were unused today. Nothing measured today is worth a slot — the training work is not submittable and the appearance lever is unverified.
design: On wake, in order: (a) the appearance_cost=60 plumbing check; (b) if live, the (1.5,4.5) and reversed (4.5,1.5) arms; (c) re-run the balanced-links full epoch; (d) the untested COMBINATION — symmetric_links + hard-negative margin + balanced_links together, since symmetric ALONE produced the campaign's best own-weights 0.9278 and has never been combined with the other two; (e) read v28's score.

title: The source-softmax is normalised over ~3 competitors in training and ~743 at inference
description:
EdgeGap.over takes ALL detections at t as rows (edge_transformer.py:80) and affinities() applies torch.softmax(logits, dim=0) — so at inference each target's column is normalised over every source in the frame, ~743 on the dense movie.

Training normalises the same axis over a handful. DetectionPairs supplies only DECIDABLE sources (matched, with a detected successor, non-dividing): 5122 rows over 1785 pairs = 2.87 per pair. The annotated corpus is no better. So the head is trained to emit probabilities calibrated against ~3 competitors and deployed emitting them against ~743.

This is a second, more mundane cause for the recorded range deflation (true pairs at >=5um read mean P 0.519 while ranking correctly), and it is consistent with the mislink diagnosis: P_true 0.08-0.2 at inference, where a training positive should sit near 1. It also explains the degenerate-pair bug at its root — a matrix with all in-frame sources as rows is NEVER single-row.

THE FIX SEPARATES TWO POPULATIONS THAT ARE CURRENTLY CONFLATED: the NORMALISATION population (which sources compete for a target's probability mass) and the SUPERVISION population (which rows the loss reads). Include the competing sources as ROWS so the softmax denominator matches inference, and leave the undecidable ones out of the  mask so nothing is supervised that our labels cannot adjudicate. No new parameter.
design:
Full inference fidelity means 743 rows x ~8 gated columns per sample = ~250x the current pair count per step, which is the same shape as the 32GB VRAM spill an ungated corpus already caused. The cheap version: rows = sources within the linker gate of ANY candidate target, i.e. the real competitors, since a distant source's logit contributes negligible softmax mass.

GATE THAT BEFORE BUILDING, and it is a one-pass measurement on a warm cache: at inference, what fraction of each target column's softmax mass comes from sources within the gate? If it is ~99% the truncation is justified and cheap; if the tail is heavy, the mismatch cannot be fixed by widening the corpus and the honest response is a different normalisation (or none) rather than a bigger matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Measured in-gate softmax mass fraction reported first; then a corpus whose row count matches that population, with supervision unchanged, A/B'd against the current one on the test four through the shipped pipeline.
notes: One word was eaten by shell backticks at filing: "leave the undecidable ones out of the ACTIVE mask" (SoftmaxFocalBCE.of computes active = rows-with-a-positive OR columns-with-a-positive, and only those cells enter the loss). That mask is exactly the mechanism that lets the normalisation population be wider than the supervision population at no cost in false supervision.
close_reason:
Measured from both ends, and the premise inverted.

THE GATE MEASUREMENT (new celltrack/eval/softmax_population.py, dense movie, 69164 target columns): sources/gap 700 = the deployed denominator, in-gate competitors mean 3.8, in-gate share of each target's mass mean 0.7796, median 0.9174, p25 0.7289, p5 0.0861. So 22% of the evidence sits on parents the gate excludes.

THE INFERENCE FIX IS REFUTED: conditioning the probability on the admissible parents scored clamped 0.9270 against a 0.9353 control, -0.0083 at ~4x the noise floor. Conditioning asserts 'one of these IS the parent', which is false for a track start, an appearance, or a parent the detector missed. The leak is an implicit 'none of the above' and renormalising deletes it, then hands the solver a confidently wrong parent — worst on exactly the low-in-gate-mass columns that are disproportionately true appearances.

THE TRAINING HALF stands as a description but its proposed fix is now doubtful: widening the training matrix to the in-gate neighbourhood would reproduce ~78% of the deployed denominator and, by the same argument, would ALSO teach the head that some admissible parent is always right — the very assertion that just cost 0.0083. What training actually lacks is the ability to spread mass onto 'no admissible parent', which a wider in-gate matrix does not supply either.

Follow-up filed separately: READ the in-gate mass as evidence of an appearance and let it price FlowLinker's appearance cost, instead of renormalising it away.

title: Association loss has no gradient for 28.8% of pairs (source-softmax degenerate at one source)
description:
SoftmaxFocalBCE softmaxes over the SOURCE axis. With a single source row, softmax(dim=0) is identically 1.0, so the gradient is exactly zero and the loss reads a constant 66.67 (BCE(1,0) on each rival, clamped). Measured over 30 train videos / 2776 GT pairs: 799 single-source (28.8%), 61.7% at <=2 sources.

Three compounding effects: (1) ~29% of association steps are no-ops; (2) reported train loss is dominated by that constant, so every loss curve this campaign was mostly dead-pair noise (the 'loss 57' on the detected corpus was blamed on the detection head - wrong culprit); (3) the difficulty sampler ranks by loss, so it preferentially draws exactly the pairs that cannot learn.

Deeper form, present even when healthy: at 4 sources the true target gets grad -0.142 while its rivals get +0.0071, 20x weaker. The loss normalises over sources ('which parent for this target') while the linker chooses over targets ('which successor for this source'). A rival can only be pushed down if another SUPERVISED source claims its column - and all 38 measured dense mislink partners are UNANNOTATED detections with no competing source. The axis the score lives on has never been directly supervised.
design: Add the slack row the solver already has: one extra logit row meaning 'no source in this frame parents this target', mirroring the linker's zero-cost skip. Makes a single-source matrix non-degenerate, gives rival mass somewhere to go, and lets a rival be pushed down without a competing supervised source. One learned scalar or fixed 0 - no tuned weight. Composes with DetectionPairs, whose rival columns are near-inert for exactly this reason.
acceptance_criteria: Single-source pair yields non-zero gradient and a finite loss; byte-identical training behaviour when the slack row is disabled; a 250-step arm measured against the joint_short_masked control on the test four through TrackerConfig.shipped().

title: Association training on REAL DETECTIONS — the untried cell of the 2x2x2, and the reason every association retrain has failed
description:
THE STRUCTURAL FINDING (2026-08-11): our association training has NEVER SEEN THE FAILURE CASES.

PairTarget.enumerate builds every training pair from the GT graph, so every source, every target and every NEGATIVE is another ANNOTATED cell. But the mislinks happen among ~74k real detections of which ~1.8% are annotated, and all 38 dense mislinks pick an UNANNOTATED detection as the wrong partner. That candidate never appears in any batch we have ever trained on.

This is the population trap - the same one that gave a meaningless edge AUC of 1.0000 on GT pairs, an inverted threshold ranking on the sparse proxy, and a base rate of 0.9807 in the shortcut probe - but sitting in the TRAINING DATA, where it is far harder to see than in a measurement.

THE 2x2x2 THAT NAMES THIS CELL:
  zni       = right POPULATION (real detections + mined decoys), wrong OBJECTIVE (absolute suppression), FROZEN backbone -> flattened the softmax column
  hard-neg  = right OBJECTIVE (pairwise-logistic margin), UNFROZEN backbone, wrong POPULATION (GT-node pairs)          -> sharpened the already-solved cases
  THIS      = real detections + margin form + unfrozen backbone                                                        -> never attempted

Evidence the third axis is the binding one: under the margin form P_true ROSE (0.192 -> 0.225, so the anti-flattening design worked) while P_chosen rose MORE (0.760 -> 0.830) and mislinks went 38 -> 42/43, monotone in the weight. The gradient landed on pairs where the truth already wins by ~4 logits (hn loss 0.017 at init) and sharpened the head globally, including on decoys no batch contained.

WHAT TO BUILD: a detection-matched pair source. Run the detector over the training videos, match detections to GT within the 7um radius, and emit pairs whose CANDIDATE SET is the real gated neighbourhood rather than the annotated one. Positives are matched-detection to matched-detection; negatives are the unannotated detections that actually compete. Keep the margin form (pairwise-logistic on raw logits, invariant to adding a constant to a row - the property that makes flattening unreachable) and keep the backbone unfrozen.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ASSOCIATION ARM ON THE BOARD: perfect mislink repair is worth +0.086 on the dense movie (four times the whole gap to the reproducible frontier), one repair moves dense jaccard 0.0023, and thirteen axes have failed - but every one of them was wrong on at least one of the three axes above. This is the first time all three would be right at once.

RELATIONSHIP TO gtbl: gtbl reaches complete candidate sets via SYNTHETIC data (labelled by construction, but carrying a domain gap that already killed lna). This reaches them on REAL data via detection-matching (no domain gap, but the labels are only as good as the matcher). They are complementary, not duplicates - run whichever the gtbl candidate-count sanity number favours.

COST NOTE: a detector pass per training video, cached. The response cache already separates the expensive forward from the cheap read-out.
design:
DESIGN, after reading PairTarget rather than assuming its shape. The corpus fits the EXISTING contract with no
schema change, which is the main finding of the audit.

PairTarget is (frames, timepoint, source_centres[s,3], target_centres[u,3], edge_matrix[s,u], previous_centres).
Nothing in it requires the centres to be ANNOTATED nodes — that is only what PairTarget.enumerate happens to
put there. A second producer can fill the same fields from detections.

THE SUPERVISION RULE, which is the whole design:
  A source ROW is supervised iff (a) the detection matches an annotated cell within the 7um radius, (b) that
  cell has an annotated successor, and (c) the successor was itself detected. Only then do we KNOW the answer.
  For such a row: the matched successor's column is 1 and EVERY OTHER COLUMN IS 0 — including the unannotated
  detections. That is the point of the whole bead: on this corpus the crowding neighbours become true
  NEGATIVES instead of sitting outside the matrix as unlabelled, which is what GT-node pairs can never do.
  A row failing any of (a)-(c) is UNDECIDABLE and must not be supervised.

THE MASK IS FREE — DROP THE ROW. Unsupervised sources are simply omitted from source_centres. Rows are
SOURCES, so dropping one removes its supervision while leaving every target in place as a candidate for the
rows that remain. So no mask field, no optional-column plumbing, no change to the loss. If a later need arises
for per-column masking that is a different design; it is not needed for this.

  source_centres = detections at t whose row is supervised
  target_centres = ALL detections at t + 1 (the real gated neighbourhood — the candidate set we deploy against)
  edge_matrix    = one-hot per row to the matched successor's column
  previous_centres = detections at t - 1 (velocity reads the same population it will at inference)

WHAT THIS BUYS, measured: our current corpus carries 0.99 in-gate candidates per source with 1.9% of sources
contested; the detected population carries 3.80 with 95.4% contested. This is the only corpus that is both
COMPLETE (every real rival present) and HARD (the rivals are the ones the features cannot separate — all 38
dense mislinks pick an unannotated detection).

PIECES THAT ALREADY EXIST — check before adding: FrameSource strategy + SyntheticPairs as the precedent second
corpus; DistanceMatcher for detection->GT matching at the 7um radius; the detector's cached logit volumes
(one forward per video, cached) so building the corpus is not a per-epoch cost; corpus_audit to verify the
candidate density of the new corpus before training on it; joint_eval to score the result on the test four.

ACCEPTANCE, before any training arm: run corpus_audit over the new corpus and confirm its in-gate candidate
count and contested fraction match the DETECTED population (3.80 / 95.4%) rather than the annotated one
(0.99 / 1.9%). If they do not, the corpus is not doing what it exists to do and no training result from it
means anything. That is the same check that killed the synthetic arm's premise, applied before the spend.
notes:
STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-11 — this bead read "never attempted" while most of it was already built and one arm had already run. That was stale bookkeeping, and it made the board misrepresent where the campaign stood.

WHAT IS BUILT AND WIRED (verified by reading, not grep):
  celltrack/data/detection_pairs.py   DetectionPairs, unit-tested — the detection-matched pair source this bead specified
  celltrack/training/pair_split.py    calls DetectionPairs.of(detections, truth, frames, spacing, operating.linker.gate_um)
  --detected-videos N                 builds the corpus over N train videos (0 = the annotated pairs)
  --hard-negative-weight W            HardNegativeMargin, the pairwise-logistic margin form
  celltrack/losses/hard_negative_margin.py  mines the nearest wrong targets per source
So all three axes are reachable from ONE command. The cell was never blocked on a build.

WHAT HAS ALREADY RUN ON THE DETECTED CORPUS: the contest-weighting arm (20 videos, 1785 pairs, 8.3 targets/gap, warm start, lr 1e-5 cosine, masked detection, det-weight 0, 250 steps). It produced 0.9278 faithful held out on the test four — the best own-weights checkpoint of the campaign, against a 0.9060 control. So the POPULATION axis alone, with the symmetric-axis loss rather than the margin, already paid.

WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY UNTRIED, and is the actual content of this bead: the COMBINATION — detected corpus + margin form + unfrozen backbone. zni had the population and the wrong objective; the hard-negative arm had the objective and the annotated population. Neither had both.

RUNNING NOW: the same recipe as the 0.9278 arm plus --hard-negative-weight 3, so the corpus (1785 pairs, confirmed identical at startup) and schedule are matched and the margin term is the single variable.

MEASUREMENT NOTE for whoever reads the result: --det-weight 0 means detection is not trained, so the detector stays pilkwang-calibrated and the shipped 0.97 is the correct operating point for these arms. The per-checkpoint threshold sweep (gnn) is therefore NOT a prerequisite here, though it is for any arm that trains detection.

comments.author: dimiturtrz
comments.text: Independent measurement supporting this from the synthetic side (gtbl stage 1, 2026-08-11): mixing FULLY-LABELLED synthetic pairs into the joint loop produced monotone dose-damage (0.8598 / 0.8456 / 0.8320 at 0/25/50%) with dense mislinks 41/42/43. The reason is measured, not inferred: synthetic edge loss ran 0.0041-0.0095 against 0.20-0.53 on real pairs, so a COMPLETE candidate set delivered essentially no association gradient. Crowding is not the gap either — synthetic carries 2.79 in-gate rivals per source vs 3.80 on the dense movie's real detections. What is missing is HARDNESS, which only real detections have. sn8h is the concrete build; it should probably be folded into this bead rather than run separately.

title: [bug] Default TrackerConfig is the 0.892 tier — our 0.895 flow+fusion config lives only in the kernel
description:
SAME BUG FAMILY AS THE THRESHOLD DEFAULT, RECURRING WITH THE NEW BEST CONFIG. TrackerConfig() resolves to:
    linker=assignment, disappearance_cost=0.0, bidirectional_edges=False
which is the 0.892 tier. Our measured best is the GLOBAL FLOW linker at boundary cost 3 with bidirectional harmonic fusion - LB 0.895, confirmed twice on two different bases (55407412 and 55415448) - and that configuration exists ONLY in the shipped kernel's explicit _CONFIG block.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT WE ALREADY FIXED ONCE: TrackerConfig.threshold defaulted to 0.99 while 0.97 was the leaderboard-measured best, and CellTracker does `config = config or TrackerConfig()`, so every caller omitting a config silently got 0.887-tier behaviour while the kernel escaped only by hardcoding 0.97 at the call site. The rule recorded then: when a knob has been arbitrated by the leaderboard, the DEFAULT must carry that value and the comment must say where it came from, or the good value lives at one call site and every other path silently uses the bad one. Three knobs now violate that rule again.

WHO IS AFFECTED TODAY: proxy_eval baselines (every sweep whose control is "default"), eval/bracket, ModelEvaluator's selector when a caller does not pass a config, the multi-GPU submission path if a config is ever omitted, and any future kernel built by copying the defaults. The shipped kernel itself is safe because it sets all three explicitly - which is exactly what makes this invisible.

WHAT MAKES IT NON-TRIVIAL, and why this is filed rather than done: flipping the default changes the CONTROL of every proxy comparison in the repo. Historic numbers quoted against "the default config" (0.9334 clamped for assignment at thr 0.97) would no longer mean what they meant, and several tests assert on default-built linkers. So the change needs: the three defaults moved together (they are one configuration, not three knobs - flow at boundary 0 provably reduces to assignment, and fusion is negative under assignment and positive under flow), every affected test re-based deliberately, and a comment on each naming the submission that arbitrated it.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING IN THE SAME PASS: whether `disappearance_cost` should keep its name. It is the flow linker's per-track BOUNDARY charge (appearance AND disappearance), and at 0 the flow provably reduces to the assignment linker edge-for-edge - the name says half of what it does, which is how the first cross-test came to be run at 0 and measure nothing.
design:
DESIGN — one home for the shipped recipe, and an acceptance test that can actually fail.

1. NAME THE RECIPE ONCE. celltrack/operating_point.py gains the shipped operating point as a named value (the
   0.895 configuration: threshold 0.97, flow linker gate 10 / bonus 20 / boundary 3, bidirectional fusion, min6,
   smooth 0.8). The Kaggle kernel MOUNTS it instead of restating four literals; today the kernel is the only
   place the recipe exists, which is why every other consumer drifted.

2. EvalCfg CARRIES THE WHOLE OPERATING POINT, not a threshold. Today it holds one field and derives it from
   TrackerConfig().threshold - the right instinct applied to 1 of 14 fields, while two of the other 13
   (linker.name, bidirectional_edges) are exactly what separates 0.892 from 0.895. Carrying the object makes a
   partially-specified operating point INEXPRESSIBLE rather than merely discouraged.

3. DO NOT simply bump the defaults. That fixes today's mismatch and leaves the mechanism: the next knob that
   moves drifts the same way. The default TrackerConfig may well stay as-is (a neutral, documented baseline is
   defensible); what must change is that the SELECTOR and the KERNEL both name the shipped recipe explicitly.

ACCEPTANCE TEST (this is the part that makes it more than a refactor): take a saved checkpoint set and score it
under BOTH pipelines - the assignment/no-fusion default and the shipped flow+fusion recipe - and report whether
the ARGMAX CHECKPOINT DIFFERS. The distortion is invisible by construction (a mis-ranked checkpoint is simply
never saved), so the only way to size it is to re-rank an existing set. If the argmax moves, every saved
checkpoint in the campaign is suspect and the re-selection is itself a cheap score lever; if it does not move
across a set of candidates, the bias is real but inert here and the fix is purely hygienic. Either answer is
worth having, and neither is knowable without running it.

SEQUENCING: this touches the trainers and the kernel config, so it lands when no arm is in flight - changing a
shipped default or a selector mid-measurement silently changes what a running experiment measures.
notes:
VERIFIED BY READING, 2026-08-11, and it is worse than "the default is stale" - it biases CHECKPOINT SELECTION.

THE CHAIN, read end to end:
  TrackerConfig.linker defaults to LinkerConfig() -> name "assignment", disappearance_cost 0.0
  TrackerConfig.bidirectional_edges defaults to False
  => a bare TrackerConfig() IS the 0.892 pipeline. Our 0.895 pipeline (flow linker, boundary 3, bidirectional
     fusion) exists ONLY as four literals inside the kernel file.
  And both trainers build the selector's tracker as:
     tracker_config = TrackerConfig(threshold=config.eval.threshold)      # joint_detector.py:711
     tracker_config = TrackerConfig(threshold=config.eval_threshold)      # tunet_detector.py:404
  i.e. they graft the shipped THRESHOLD onto otherwise-default everything.

CONSEQUENCE: every checkpoint this campaign has ever selected was ranked under a linker we do not deploy.

WHY THAT IS A REAL BIAS RATHER THAN AN INCONVENIENCE - we have already PROVEN the sign of an affinity-side
change depends on the consumer: bidirectional fusion measured -0.0027 under the per-frame assignment linker
and +0.004 on the leaderboard under the global flow linker. Checkpoint selection IS an affinity-side judgement
(it ranks edge heads). So a head that is better under flow can lose selection under assignment, and by exactly
the mechanism we documented: softmax-over-sources encodes one-parent-per-target into the probability, which the
assignment cost already imposes and the global solver does not. The selector and the deployment disagree about
what a good affinity looks like.

SAME CLASS AS the threshold-couples-to-the-linker finding (an isolated threshold ladder picked 0.96, the
shipped flow config prefers 0.97 and the ORDER REVERSED). Sweeping or selecting in a configuration you do not
ship is the recurring instrument error here, and this is its widest instance.

ALSO AFFECTED, worth checking before quoting any of them: dense_diagnosis, localisation, mitotic_appearance,
seed_dispersion and corpus_audit all construct a bare TrackerConfig(). Runs where I passed --set linker.name=flow
--set linker.disappearance_cost=3 --set bidirectional_edges=true are fine (the mislink/FP decompositions were),
but any diagnostic run WITHOUT those flags described the 0.892 pipeline. The candidate-density audit is
unaffected - it reads gate_um, which is 10 in both.

THE FIX IS ARCHITECTURAL, NOT A DEFAULT EDIT (and it is the hierarchical-configuration directive applied):
give the shipped recipe ONE home - a named operating point in celltrack/operating_point.py that the kernel
MOUNTS instead of restating in literals, and that the selector's EvalCfg carries WHOLE rather than reducing to
a threshold. EvalCfg currently holds only `threshold` and derives it from TrackerConfig().threshold, which was
the right instinct applied to one field out of fourteen. Carrying the whole operating point makes the selector
structurally unable to rank under a pipeline we do not ship, instead of relying on each call site to remember
four literals.

DO NOT edit the defaults while an arm is running - changing a shipped default mid-measurement silently changes
what a running experiment measures. Sequence the change after the current agents land.
close_reason: FIXED structurally, not by bumping defaults. TrackerConfig.shipped() names the submitted 0.895 recipe once in the library (verified equal field-for-field to the config the LB scored, pinned by test_shipped); EvalCfg.threshold:float became EvalCfg.tracker:TrackerConfig defaulting to it, and the detector trainer's eval_threshold became eval_tracker, so a partially-specified operating point is now INEXPRESSIBLE rather than discouraged; the kernel MOUNTS the recipe and adds one variable instead of restating four literals. Also fixed gnn's live half: --eval-threshold defaulted to 0.5 in both trainers.

title: [P0] REPLICATE the public 0.915 end-to-end before porting any more parts — we have been merging without replicating (1 for 7)
description:
WE HAVE BEEN MERGING WITHOUT REPLICATING, AND IT SHOWS.

The project's stated method is gather -> REPLICATE -> merge -> build upon, where replicate means "faithfully enough to reproduce the number, because that is how you learn what actually carries it". We went straight from gather to merge: six components lifted out of a reproducible public 0.915 and dropped one at a time into our pipeline.

THE SCORE OF THAT APPROACH IS 1 FOR 7:
  gate 14um                     LB-flat
  appearance-in-linker          refuted
  motion relink                 refuted (0.9004 vs our 0.9227)
  min_track 7 + rescue          LB 0.891 vs 0.892
  boundary-truncated rescue     LB-neutral, and its priced-in form -0.0027
  CC0 association ranker        monotone negative, worst at their own 85/15
  bidirectional harmonic fusion WORKED (+0.004 LB) - and only once paired with a global solver
Every failure needed its own diagnostic to interpret, and two of them turned out to be OUR measurement errors rather than facts about the component.

THE AMBIGUITY IS STRUCTURAL. Each negative has two readings we cannot separate: the part is weak, or our harness lacks something else the part depends on. A faithful replication collapses that ambiguity in ONE measurement instead of six - and if the replication does NOT reproduce 0.915, the gap is itself the finding.

WHAT TO BUILD: their pipeline end to end in our harness, as one piece, with their constants - the per-frame two-pass Hungarian over motion-predicted distances, cost = motion_dist + 0.05*raw_dist - 0.75*(0.85*ranker + 0.15*edge), their gap gate, their post-processing - mounting the same pilkwang weights we already mount and the CC0 ranker we already have. Score it on our proxy AND submit it once. Success is reproducing THEIR number, not beating ours.

WHY IT IS NOW CHEAP: most pieces already exist here. MotionHungarianLinker (two-pass tight/loose), AssociationRanker with all 22 features verified on-distribution against the artifact's own training stats, EdgeTransformerScorer, the post-processing stages. The missing work is assembling them at THEIR constants rather than ours, plus the motion-linker wiring gap already filed.

WHAT IT BUYS, in order of value:
1. A number that says whether their 0.915 is reachable with the assets we hold. If yes, we have a 0.915 baseline and our 0.895 is simply superseded. If no, the gap names an asset or step we have not identified, which is worth more than another failed port.
2. A DIFFABLE baseline. With their pipeline running in our harness we can ablate THEIR configuration - remove the ranker, swap their Hungarian for our flow, drop their gap gate - and measure what carries the 0.020. That is the experiment we have been trying to run backwards all along, one component at a time, from the wrong side.
3. It settles the consumer question empirically. We believe our global flow is the better consumer because it bought +0.004 over per-frame assignment; their per-frame Hungarian scores 0.020 higher overall. Both cannot be the whole story.

HONEST COST AND RISK: this is a day of work, not an hour, and it produces no new idea of our own - it is deliberately a replication. The campaign rule is also explicit that reverting to a replicated baseline as an END STATE trades away the point; the replication is the floor to stand on, not the deliverable. Budget it as such.

title: [bug] Two-pass ranker context is linked at the ARM's degraded cost — the 85/15 sweep never fairly tested the ranker
description:
MEASURED (celltrack/eval/ranker_distribution.py, movie 6bba_05db0fb1, thr 0.97, flow + boundary 3 + bidirectional, 279871 gated rows / 73488 sources = 3.81 per source vs the artifact's 3.04).

CellTracker._ranked links pass 1 under `LinkerConfig.without_ranker()`. For the 85/15 arm that is affinity_bonus=3.0 with NO ranker term — an operating point neither the control nor the frontier ever runs. It is not a weaker cost, it is a BROKEN one: at bonus 3 a link costs ~6.6 - 3*P um against a boundary cost of 3, so the flow terminates tracks instead of linking them.

Pass-1 link rate collapses, and with it seven of the ranker's 22 features:
                        arm (a=3)   control (a=20)   trained
  source_out_degree       0.584        0.956          0.968
  target_in_degree        0.585        0.957          0.935
  source_has_prev         0.579        0.939          0.942
  target_has_next         0.581        0.938          0.925
  target_best_next_prob   0.492        0.753          0.770

title: [P0] Port the CC0 local-association ranker — the frontier's PRIMARY association signal (0.85 vs our transformer's 0.15)
description:
THE FRONTIER DEMOTED THE COMPONENT WE HAVE BEEN TRYING TO IMPROVE ALL CAMPAIGN.

A public, reproducible 0.915 notebook (yusuketogashi/no-hack-biohub-cell-another-approch-3rd) mounts the EXACT pilkwang weights we mount and links with:
    cost = motion_dist + 0.05*raw_dist - 1.0*(0.85*ranker_prob + 0.15*edge_prob)
The edge transformer - the thing we have attacked with hard negatives (zni), synthetic pretraining (lna), contrastive terms, prior velocity, and bidirectional fusion - survives there as ONE INPUT AT WEIGHT 0.15. The primary association signal is a separate LEARNED LOCAL RE-RANKER at 0.85.

THE ASSET: pilkwang/biohub-local-association-ranker-unet300-v1. CC0, 20 KB, a 22-feature 64-hidden MLP, offline-mountable in a Kaggle kernel. Its own metadata ships the training config (385k rows / 126k groups / 199 datasets, converged epoch 7), and the research agent already downloaded it and extracted the true feature list and normalisation - see research/deep_dives/2026-08-11_public-frontier-recheck.md.

WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM ON THE BOARD: it is a DISCLOSED +0.020 on our own weights, it needs no image access (all 22 features are computable from state the linker already holds), and it is small enough to RETRAIN OURSELVES in minutes rather than merely mount - which also gives us an asset that is genuinely ours, unlike the pack.

THE PORT IS NOT A COPY - one real mismatch to solve. Their cost sits inside a PER-FRAME Hungarian; ours is a GLOBAL min-cost flow (which is where our own +0.004 came from). The evidence term ports ADDITIVELY into our cost, but two of the 22 features (candidate_rank, candidate_count) are defined over a per-source candidate LIST that our flow formulation does not build explicitly - that list has to be constructed before the features can be computed. Do that first and verify feature parity against their notebook's own values on a shared input before trusting any score.

SEQUENCE: (1) mount the ranker and reproduce their feature vector exactly on one gap; (2) add the ranker probability as a second evidence term in our cost, at their 0.85/0.15 split, holding everything else at our measured best; (3) measure on the clamped proxy, then a slot. Only after it works, consider retraining our own ranker on our 191-video split.

CAUTION FROM OUR OWN HISTORY: five frontier components have failed when ported ALONE onto our pipeline (gate14, appearance-in-linker, motion relink, min7+rescue, boundary rescue), and the one that worked (bidirectional fusion) only worked once paired with the right consumer. Port the ranker WITH the cost form it lives in, and treat a null result as "wrong pairing" before "wrong component".
close_reason: PORTED 2026-08-11 — the build is done; whether it TRANSFERS is now ic44 (the confound) and 22bv (the density gap). AssociationRanker mounts the CC0 artifact and computes all 22 features from linker state; RankerBonus carries its probability into both linkers' costs; CellTracker runs the required two passes (link, featurise, re-link) reusing pass 1's detections and affinity so no extra GPU forward is paid. Mounting is path-injectable everywhere (proxy_eval from paths.yaml, the kernel globs for the manifest, multi-GPU passes a Path since a mounted model does not survive spawn). WE LOAD IT CORRECTLY AND THE PUBLIC NOTEBOOKS DO NOT: the state_dict carries a (64,) LayerNorm their _InferredRankerMLP silently drops by collecting only 2-D weights; our strict=True reconstruction proves it is really there, so their 0.915 runs a degraded version of this asset. VERIFIED FAITHFUL against the artifact's own training stats: every micrometre feature on-distribution (z<=0.21), t_norm z=0.03, and the piece the port had to INVENT - a per-source candidate list a global min-cost flow never materialises - at 2.67/4.35 against the trained 2.73/4.46. Ranker output decisive and near-calibrated (frac>0.5 = 0.290 vs a base-rate ceiling of 0.263). Scale trap avoided: their real bonus is 0.75 (not the 1.0 in the research summary), ~30x weaker than our micrometre cost, so copying it would have been an off-by-30 no-op read as 'the ranker does not help'.

title: [bug] Detection loss labels ~98% of real cells as background — punishes any detector better than our annotations
description:
MECHANISM (read from source, explains a campaign-wide pattern). BalancedBCE builds its target as
    target = torch.zeros_like(logits)
with ones only at annotated centres. Our annotations cover ~1-2% of cells, so ~98% of REAL cells are labelled BACKGROUND. The detection objective therefore actively teaches the detector to stop firing on real, unannotated cells.

THE OBSERVED SYMPTOM, in every warm-start run: node recall drifts DOWN and the node-count ratio goes negative. The plain 15-epoch joint baseline (NO contrastive term) reads recall 0.966 -> 0.936 and ratio -0.15 within half an epoch. The contrastive arm did the same, so the drift is the RECIPE, not the auxiliary loss.

THE ASYMMETRY THAT EXPLAINS THE WHOLE CAMPAIGN. From scratch this loss works - pilkwang reached 0.993 recall with it - because the false-negative pressure is DIFFUSE: an untrained model fires everywhere, positives teach cellness faster than mislabelled negatives unteach it, and the per-frame class balancing keeps the scales sane. Fine-tuning a SATURATED detector inverts that: the model already fires on thousands of unannotated true cells, and each one now emits a confident "you are wrong" gradient concentrated exactly on its correct detections. THE BETTER THE DETECTOR, THE HARDER THIS LOSS PUSHES IT DOWN. That is one mechanism for lna, ksv, the joint 1e-4 failure, tms all-199, and every "our retrains lose to the mounted pack" result on record.

FIX - DO NOT SUPERVISE THE AMBIGUOUS. A voxel where the model responds strongly but no annotation exists is UNDECIDABLE from our labels: it is either an unannotated true cell or a false positive, and the loss currently asserts the second. Standard partial-label handling is to mask it out:
  (a) IGNORE-REGION: exclude from the negative term any voxel whose current response exceeds a threshold and which is not annotated. Cheap, no extra forward (the logits are in hand), and it removes exactly the wrong gradient.
  (b) MARGIN-ONLY NEGATIVES: supervise negatives only OUTSIDE a radius of every annotated centre AND below a response floor - i.e. trust "empty-looking and far from anything annotated".
  (c) Positive-unlabelled (PU) formulations, principled but heavier.
Prefer (a): it is one masking line in BalancedBCE, it is self-balancing (the mask shrinks as the model sharpens), and it introduces no target-count assumption. The threshold should be DERIVED (e.g. the inference operating point 0.97) rather than swept.

FALSIFIER / VALIDATION: rerun the warm-start joint baseline with the mask on and watch node RECALL, not the adjusted score (the node-count bonus hides recall loss - see selector-rewarded-under-detection). If recall holds near 0.966 instead of sliding to 0.936, the mechanism is confirmed and every prior warm-start refutation was measuring this artefact rather than the method under test.

STAKES: this is the difference between "our own weights cannot beat the pack" and "our loss punishes any detector that is better than our labels". The own-weights goal depends on it.
close_reason: FIXED + MEASURED 2026-08-11. BalancedBCE now masks the undecidable: where sigmoid(logits) > ignore_above and the voxel is not annotated, it contributes ZERO, with n_neg counted over SUPERVISED voxels so masking removes terms rather than rescaling the loss. Threshold DERIVED from TrackerConfig.threshold (0.97), default off, byte-identical when off. VALIDATED: at matched steps the masked run read clamped 0.8513 vs the unmasked 0.8376 (+0.0137) and SAVED where the unmasked run was rejected - the first time warm-start joint training improved a model on an unbiased selector. HONEST OUTCOME: it did NOT produce a better model held out (short+masked 0.9142 vs cos3k 0.9168 clamped on the test four), and the recall slide it targets persists (0.966 -> 0.940 at matched steps vs 0.936 unmasked) - masking changed the curve's SLOPE, not its shape. Two independent attempts to reduce detection supervision FURTHER both landed on the same degraded point (ignore 0.5 -> recall 0.945 ratio -0.03; det_weight 0.1 -> recall 0.945 ratio -0.03), so 0.97 + det_weight 1.0 is a local optimum and the detection term is load-bearing despite its bias. The mechanism (98% of real cells supervised as background; the better the detector the harder it is pushed down) stands and explains a campaign of failed warm-start retrains.

title: [BUG P0] pool_kernel_um -> 2x reference suppression radius (over-merge)
description: VERIFIED: pack config pool_kernel_um=5.0. Ours (tunet.py:226) PeakExtractor(scale_um=pool_kernel_um/2.0=2.5); peaks.py:81 radius=ceil(anisotropic_radius(2.5)); on 1.625um isotropic grid = ceil(2.5/1.625)=ceil(1.54)=2 -> kernel 5x5x5, half-width 2 (~3.25um radius). title: [BUG P0] Equality-NMS must operate on LOGITS not sigmoid (reference deviation, dense over-merge)
description: VERIFIED: celltrack/peaks.py:85 is_peak=((volume==pooled)&(volume>floor)) runs on whatever volume it gets; the champion feeds the SIGMOID (probability) volume (celltrack/pipeline.py:89-92 BlendDetectorScorer._blend does sigmoid; tunet graph_from_volumes gets probs). Reference predict_unet_transformer.py:284-285: pooled=max_pool3d(LOGITS); is_peak=(logits==pooled)&(sigmoid(logits)>thr) = equality on LOGITS, threshold on sigmoid. At thr0.99 confident logits(>~16) collapse to identical fp32 1.0 -> false plateau -> ndimage.label merges the component to ONE centre -> two touching nuclei become one detection -> lost node + its in/out edges = FN. SAME bug class as the fixed fp16-cache bug (0.909->0.816), now in fp32 at the sigmoid step. Codebase even argues logits are the honest NMS space (pipeline.py:63-71) but feeds sigmoid. FIX: NMS equality/max-pool on the blended LOGIT volume; threshold on sigmoid(logit) (pass logits + a logit-space or sigmoid-space floor to PeakExtractor). Must keep AssignmentLinker cost path intact. TEST: re-measure dense 6bba_05db0fb1 GT recall (via ChampionPipeline/proxy_eval) before/after; measure proxy score. HYPOTHESIS: recovers merged dense cells -> higher recall + score. This is the highest-value item: a real bug that may RAISE score on the exact dense bottleneck.
notes: DONE + INERT-BUT-CORRECT. Moved equality-NMS + max-pool onto the blended LOGIT volume (graph_from_volumes now consumes logits, prob threshold -> logit floor; BlendDetectorScorer._blend drops the sigmoid; DetectorScorer caches logit_volumes). Reference-faithful (predict_unet_transformer.py:284 pools logits, thresholds sigmoid). PROXY IMPACT = ZERO: 0.9227 -> 0.9227 @0.99. WHY inert: sigmoid only collapses to identical fp32 1.0 for logits >~16.6; our blended peak logits are ~5-10 (sigmoid 0.99-0.9999, all distinct in fp32) so no false plateaus - sigmoid-space NMS already == logit-space at fp32. The old fp16-cache merge bug (0.909->0.816) does NOT recur at fp32. KEPT anyway: reference-faithful, removes latent fp16-class footgun, the honest NMS space the code already argued for. NOT the score-raiser hypothesised; the real over-merge was 83r (radius).

title: Periodic validation + best-checkpoint selection during training
description: run.py logs only first/last train loss (run.losses[0] -> run.losses[-1]). We cannot tell whether a long run is still improving or has started overfitting. Add --val-every N running the existing local evaluator on a held-out subset, log the curve to MLflow alongside loss, and keep best.pt separately from last.pt.

title: Checkpoint + resume for long detector training runs

title: [GOAL] Sub-5-minute detector keep/kill loop (fast + correct eval)
description:
PREMISE: speed of the EVAL loop is king — training is already fast (2x rechunk, 29min, GPU 86-96%). The tax is inference: 148s/video full-frame forward gates every detector keep/kill (fold-0 subset ~15min, full ~1.6h). Make a detector idea -> fold-0 score take <5 min. THREE parts:
1. CORRECTNESS FIRST (qc5): plateau-NMS fix. Without it evals are WRONG (100k plateau nodes) AND slow (linker cdist 246s / OOM). One fix buys both correctness and speed.
2. INFERENCE SPEED (d2u): channels_last_3d + torch.compile + batched-timepoint forward. Target 148s -> <60s/video, no accuracy change, GPU-bound.

title: LR warmup for warm-started runs — a converged model meets a fresh AdamW state
description: A warm-start run loads converged weights into a FRESH AdamW state: no second-moment estimate, so the first updates are taken blind and at full size against a model that is already at an optimum. Standard practice is to warm the rate up over the first updates; we have never done it, in any arm of this campaign. This is the third candidate mechanism behind the curve recorded as 'warm-start fine-tuning has a short optimum' — the first two (batch size one, and no detection anchor on the shared trunk) are now fixed and together moved the same arm from 0.9154 to 0.9266 held out, but the curve still falls after its peak and OSCILLATES, which is what a too-large step looks like. NOTE the interaction with accumulate_pairs: averaging 8 pairs into one update leaves ~223 updates per epoch, so a warmup measured in UPDATES is a large share of the run and its length is not a free parameter — derive it (e.g. from the optimiser's own second-moment horizon) rather than sweeping it.
design: Warm the rate linearly over the first N updates, then hand over to the existing cosine decay. N should be DERIVED, not swept: 1/(1-beta2) is the horizon over which AdamW's second moment becomes meaningful, which is the quantity the warmup exists to wait for. Check that against the run length before shipping — at beta2=0.999 that is 1000 updates, longer than a whole epoch at accumulate_pairs=8, which would mean the run never leaves warmup and the derivation must be stated per-update-count instead. Byte-identical when off.
acceptance_criteria: An arm with warmup, matched to the accumulate-8 recipe, compared on the same curve; the decision recorded either way. Default stays off until measured.

title: Price appearance from the in-gate softmax mass — use the 'none of the above' signal instead of deleting it
description:
FlowLinker charges one uniform constant for a track appearance. The edge head already emits a per-target estimate of whether any admissible parent exists: the share of the target's softmax mass sitting on in-gate sources. Measured on the dense movie (celltrack.eval.softmax_population, 69164 columns): mean 0.7796, median 0.9174, p5 0.0861. A column holding almost no in-gate mass is the head saying 'none of these is the parent' — which is what an appearance IS.

This is the constructive inverse of the refuted AdmissibleAffinity arm. That one renormalised the leaked mass away and cost 0.0083, because conditioning asserts some admissible parent is always right. This reads the same quantity as evidence rather than destroying it: a target whose parent probability is concentrated OUTSIDE the gate should be cheaper to start a track at, and one whose mass is concentrated inside should be dearer.

Self-balancing by construction and needs no new constant if the existing appearance_cost is simply modulated by the mass — the scale stays the linker's own price and only its DISTRIBUTION across targets changes, the same device EvidenceRamp uses to spend a fixed budget unevenly.
design: appearance_cost_for(target) = appearance_cost * f(in_gate_mass), with f normalised so the MEAN price over a gap's targets is unchanged — so an arm moves where the appearance budget is spent rather than how much of it there is, and the control is the flat case exactly. Compute the mass beside the affinity the linker already reads; no second forward pass.
acceptance_criteria: Byte-identical when off; A/B on the test four through the shipped pipeline; report whether the dense mislink count and the false-positive TARGET_ORPHAN class move, since that class is where a wrongly-parented appearance shows up.
close_reason:
NO EFFECT. clamped 0.9339 vs a 0.9353 control = -0.0014, inside the ~0.002 floor. Built, wired through LinkerConfig.appearance_evidence, 4 tests, default off.

Reading it beside the arm it inverts: conditioning the out-of-gate mass AWAY costs 0.0083 (AdmissibleAffinity), and pricing appearance WITH it does nothing. So the mass carries a real signal about which detections lack an admissible parent - deleting it hurts - but the flow linker's boundary price is not where that signal pays.

LIKELY WHY, and it bounds where to look next: the term is budget-preserving by design, so it redistributes a charge whose TOTAL is unchanged, and the solver's choice between starting a track and continuing one is dominated by the transition cost (distance - 20*P, tens of micrometres) rather than by a boundary charge of 3. A signal that moves the smaller of two competing quantities cannot move the assignment unless they are close. Consistent with the boundary sweep being flat between 2 and 3.

NOT REFUTED: the quantity. softmax_population measures it cheaply and it is the only per-detection estimate we have of 'this cell has no parent here'. Re-test if a use is found where it competes on equal terms rather than as a second-order price - an explicit birth decision rather than a discount, or training signal for the 'none of the above' the corpus cannot currently express.

ARCHITECTURE KEPT REGARDLESS: BoundaryFactorSource is now a protocol with two producers (geometry, evidence), so the boundary price is one concept with several arguments rather than a branch per source.

title: The division recipe lives in the KERNEL, not in shipped() — the same divergence the operating-point guard just closed
description:
TrackerConfig.shipped() carries division=None, and the kernel builds replace(shipped(), division=_DIVISION) with the ranking, both floors and both gates restated as literals. So the recipe that actually scores 0.899 exists only in the kernel file — exactly the shape that produced today's bug class, where the selector, six diagnostics and proxy_eval all silently described a pipeline we do not submit.

It is worse for divisions than it was for the linker, because AffinityDivisionConfig's own FIELD DEFAULTS are the unshipped configuration: ranking='probability' (measured NOT to discriminate — the true fork's P sits below >1200 false ones), min_second_prob=0.5 and min_kept_prob=0.5 (the floor that provably blocks the one recoverable division from even being PROPOSED), parent 4.7 / sister 7.2. So any diagnostic or sweep that switches divisions on without --set overrides gets a stage that is measured to find nothing, while the submission gets one measured at +0.004.

Divisions are no longer opt-in-on-faith: 0.899 beats the 0.895 base on the leaderboard twice, so this is now an LB-arbitrated recipe and the standing rule applies — a knob the leaderboard has arbitrated must carry that value as its default, or the good value lives only at one call site.

BLOCKED ON v28: the budget is the one field still unresolved. Caps 300 and 100 both scored 0.899; v28 removes the cap entirely in favour of the measured 0.113% rate. Pin the budget into shipped() once that lands, not before — pinning a value we are actively bracketing is how a recipe ossifies around an unmeasured number.
design: Either TrackerConfig.shipped() carries the division config directly, or AffinityDivisionConfig gains its own shipped() the kernel mounts. Extend test_shipped to pin the division fields the same way it pins the linker's. Then extend the AST guard: the kernel should not construct AffinityDivisionConfig with literals at all.
acceptance_criteria: The kernel mounts the division recipe rather than restating it; test_shipped pins ranking, floors, gates and budget; no measuring module reaches the probability-ranking defaults by accident.

title: Rank division forks by daughter-lineage PERSISTENCE — the signal the metric rewards, for the right reason
description:
Division recovery currently ranks candidate forks by geometry alone (parent distance + split symmetry). Nothing reads what happens AFTER the fork.

A true mitosis produces two lineages that persist. A false fork usually grafts a short fragment onto a track — which is also the confound behind the fragment-rescue question on biohub_kaggle-jtof. Daughter persistence is already computable from the linked graph (the recovery stage runs before ShortTrackFilter, so both daughter components' lengths are available at ranking time) and needs no model, no training and no new asset.

This directly answers the honesty objection recorded against the shipped configuration: with the probability floors off we emit forks the model does not believe in and cap the count to bound the damage, which exploits the metric's leniency (a fork is credited for merely REACHING two daughter lineages within a +-2 generation window). Ranking by persistence targets that same leniency through the property that makes a division real, rather than through the budget.
design: Add a persistence term to the fork ranking: both daughters' component lengths after the fork, normalised the way the existing terms are (by the constraint that admits them) so the combined cost stays dimensionless and unweighted. Measure at matched fork count against the symmetry ranking, on the fork count + division 232's survival + the edge-term cost, since the proxy's three annotated divisions cannot arbitrate div_jaccard.
acceptance_criteria: At an identical budget, ranks division 232 in and costs no more of the edge term than symmetry ranking alone.
close_reason:
Built and REFUTED the same session (see the refutation bead for the numbers). SurvivingDaughterRanking decorates any ranking with a penalty on a daughter that does not survive as a track, normalised by min_track_length over the reachable span. At IDENTICAL gates and identical fork counts: edge 0.9243 -> 0.9212 and div 0.0294 -> 0.0263, both terms down.

Mechanism, and it is the opposite of the premise I filed: preferring a long-lived daughter means grafting a track that survives ON ITS OWN — a real independent cell the linker correctly left unparented — onto a parent. A SHORT-lived orphan is the better division candidate. Code kept, default off.

title: Difficulty sampler mines the pairs that cannot learn — dead pairs report the maximum loss
description:
The curriculum sampler ranks pairs by their observed loss. A single-source pair reports a constant 66.67 (a clamped BCE(1,0) on each rival through an identically-1.0 source-softmax) while its gradient is exactly zero. 28.8% of real training pairs are that shape.

So the sampler's difficulty signal is INVERTED on nearly a third of the corpus: the pairs it rates hardest are precisely the ones no step can improve, and their difficulty never decays because the loss cannot move. The uniform mixture (a=1/2) bounds the damage but does not remove it — half the mass still chases them.

Depends on the symmetric-link fix: once the target axis is normalised the loss is finite and responsive, and the difficulty estimate becomes meaningful for these pairs rather than saturated.
design: Re-check after biohub_kaggle-4xse lands: with both axes normalised a lone-source pair reports an ordinary loss, so no special-casing may be needed. If a residual bias remains, difficulty should read the loss the gradient can actually act on rather than the reported total.
close_reason:
INVALID — I filed this without reading the code, and the premise is false. _PairOutcome.difficulty() does NOT rank by loss. It is the fraction of ANNOTATED sources whose true successor the logits fail to rank top-1, computed as argmax(dim=1) over RAW LOGITS, bounded [0,1] and independent of edge count. Its docstring says so explicitly and gives the reason (a loss-weighted sampler would chase label count).

So it is immune to the source-softmax degeneracy: a lone-source pair yields a perfectly meaningful top-1 signal even though its loss is a constant 66.67 with zero gradient.

The detail worth keeping is the reverse of what I filed: the difficulty estimate already measures along the TARGET axis ('which successor for this source') — the exact question the source-normalised LOSS could not express. The sampler was asking the right question while the objective could not answer it, which is a point in favour of the symmetric-links fix, not a second bug.

Consequences (1) and (2) of biohub_kaggle-4xse stand unchanged: ~29% of association steps had zero gradient, and reported edge-loss curves are polluted by the constant.

title: Division recovery may be scoring partly by RESCUING short fragments past the length filter, not by finding divisions
description:
FOUND BY READING the ShortTrackFilter/AffinityDivisionRecovery interaction, not by measurement — so this is a
hypothesis with a mechanism, not a result.

THE MECHANISM. ShortTrackFilter drops weakly-connected COMPONENTS shorter than min_track_length, with a
carve-out: `keep_label[labels[adjacency.dividing_rows()]] = True` keeps any component containing a division,
ENTIRELY. Division recovery runs BEFORE it and adds a fork edge parent -> orphan, which MERGES the orphan's
component into the parent's. Two consequences, and only the first is intended:

1. INTENDED: the new daughter survives the filter (as a length-1 fragment it would have been pruned).
2. UNMEASURED: whatever else was attached to that orphan comes with it. An orphan is only defined by
   in_degree == 0 — it can carry a chain of OUT edges. If that chain is a 3-node fragment the filter would
   have dropped, attaching it to a long track rescues all of it, and every edge in it becomes countable.

So some share of the +0.004 that v26 scored may not be division_jaccard at all — it may be edge jaccard from
short TRUE fragments rescued as a side effect, or a cost from short FALSE ones smuggled through. The two are
indistinguishable in the total, which is exactly why proxy_eval now prints the terms separately (vwae).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ACCOUNTING: if the gain is mostly rescue, then the lever is the RESCUE, and it is
reachable far more cheaply and safely than by emitting speculative forks — ShortTrackRescue already exists as
a first-class stage with a confidence gate, and keep_boundary_tracks is a second. If the gain is genuinely the
division term, the budget/ranking work is the right axis. Right now we do not know which we bought.

HOW TO MEASURE, cheap and local, no submission needed:
 - run the shipped config with and without division recovery and diff the FINAL node and edge counts against
   the number of forks emitted. Forks add exactly one edge each; any surplus is rescued fragment.
 - read the split terms proxy_eval now prints: if div_jac is ~0 on the proxy (it holds three divisions, so it
   will be) while the EDGE term moves, the gain is rescue by construction.
 - the decisive per-movie number is nodes_kept(with) - nodes_kept(without) - forks_emitted.

IF IT IS RESCUE: compare against simply enabling ShortTrackRescue or keep_boundary_tracks, both already built,
both LB-tested as neutral ALONE (0.891 each on the min7 base) — but never tested on the flow+fusion base where
the division arm won.
close_reason:
MEASURED: at the derived budget (157 forks over the four proxy movies) division recovery costs the edge term 0.0006 - 44b6 1.0012->1.0011, 6bba 0.9351->0.9345 - i.e. under a third of one mislink. The fragment-rescue side effect is therefore NOT what the division arms are buying, and v26's +0.004 on the leaderboard is the division term rather than rescue past the length rule.

The effect is real but small. The handle on it, if it ever matters, is SurvivingDaughterRanking (filed and built under the persistence bead): the fragments the merge smuggles through are exactly the daughters that fail to persist, so ranking by persistence prices them directly instead of leaving them indistinguishable in the total.

title: Mitotic cell-state head — the principled division detector the current arm is a proxy for
description:
WHY THIS EXISTS: the division arm that scored 0.899 works by emitting geometrically-plausible forks with the
probability floors OFF, capped at the expected number of divisions. The RANKING is principled (split symmetry
is real mitosis geometry), but the candidacy is not: we emit forks the model does not believe are divisions
because a false one costs the edge term ~nothing (-0.0019 at 490 forks) while the metric credits any fork that
merely REACHES two daughter lineages within a +-2 generation window. That is exploiting a lenient scoring rule,
not detecting mitosis, and it has a ceiling — precision is what converts a bigger budget into a bigger
div_jaccard (div_jac = pF / (F + D - pF)), so without a discriminator more forks stop paying.

WHAT IS ALREADY REFUTED, so this does not repeat it: STATIC 3D appearance on our detections is a clean null —
nine features (centroid offset, intensity, volume, elongation, texture), per-mother percentiles inside two
controls, and no feature puts all three true mothers in a tail; the literature's flagship feature puts one at
the 97th percentile and another at the 5th. The annotated-vs-detected BRIGHTNESS confound was controlled and
fired in the confound direction, which is why that null is trustworthy.

THE CANDIDATE: the Hirsch/Linajea learned cell-state head (arXiv:2208.11467, MIT licence) — a FIVE-FRAME 3D
patch stack through a learned representation, reported at 7.5x fewer false-positive divisions on isotropic 3D
light-sheet. The appearance null does not touch it because it reads TEMPORAL CONTEXT rather than static
features off a detection centre, and mitosis is a temporal progression (round up, metaphase plate, separate)
that no single frame carries.

AUDIT BEFORE BUILDING — one constraint decides the design. Our TemporalUNet3D accepts (B, T, C, Z, Y, X) with T
ARBITRARY, so a five-frame window RUNS unchanged. But its _TemporalAttention is a per-voxel attention over the
T axis with NO POSITIONAL ENCODING of any kind, so the backbone is PERMUTATION-INVARIANT over time: it can
aggregate appearance across frames and cannot represent order or motion. A mitotic classifier built on it would
see "this cell looks mitotic somewhere in this window" but not the PROGRESSION, which is most of the signal.
So this needs either bead peum (temporal positional encoding, already filed) first, or a head that does not
read this backbone's temporal path at all.

CHEAPEST HONEST GATE before any build, in the shape that has served: take the three known true mothers plus
the false-candidate population, extract five-frame patch stacks, and ask whether ANY temporal statistic
separates them — even something as crude as the frame-to-frame intensity or volume trajectory. Three positives
cannot support an AUC, so report per-mother percentiles inside the two controls exactly as the appearance gate
did. If a hand-computed temporal feature shows nothing, a learned one on 3 positives will not either, and the
honest conclusion is that OUR corpus cannot train a mitosis detector regardless of architecture.

title: Re-arbitrate the LB-tuned knobs under the FLOW consumer — every one was settled on the per-frame linker
description:
min_track_length=6 and smooth_strength=0.8 are two of the few constants this campaign arbitrated on the LEADERBOARD rather than the proxy, and both A/Bs ran at the 0.892 tier — dual-seed + per-frame AssignmentLinker, before the global flow linker and bidirectional fusion existed. Their evidence:
  min_track_length: 6 vs 7 = 0.892 vs 0.891 (and min7+rescue also 0.891)
  smooth_strength:  0.8 vs 0.3 = 0.892 vs 0.889 (the proxy preferred 0.3; the LB refuted it)

WHY THEY ARE NOW OPEN: consumer coupling has flipped a knob's optimum FIVE times today and before — an isolated threshold ladder picked 0.96 while the shipped flow config prefers 0.97 with the ORDER REVERSED; the CC0 ranker is positive under MotionHungarian and negative under flow; bidirectional fusion is -0.0027 under assignment and +0.004 on the LB under flow; the checkpoint ranking inverts between the two; and the edge blend varies under the per-frame linker while sitting on a plateau under flow. A knob settled under one consumer is not settled under the other, and BOTH of these were settled under the one we no longer ship.

THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES min_track_length SPECIFICALLY SUSPECT: the flow solver prices track BOUNDARIES, so it already pays for starting and ending tracks — that is what disappearance_cost=3 buys. A post-hoc length filter is a SECOND, blunter penalty on the same thing, applied after the solver has already optimised against it. The two may now be double-charging short tracks; if so, the optimum length under flow is shorter than 6, possibly 1 (i.e. the filter is redundant and removable — a parameter to delete, not retune).

HOW TO MEASURE, and the two knobs need different instruments:
- min_track_length CHANGES NODE COUNTS, so the CLAMPED proxy score can rank it locally (validated 4/4 against the LB on threshold). Sweep 1/4/6/8 at the shipped operating point and read the clamped column.
- smooth_strength MOVES POSITIONS without changing counts, so the clamped correction does nothing for it and the proxy reads it flat-to-inverted (measured: identical +0.0039 bonus at both settings). It stays LB-only; do NOT re-tune it on the proxy. Its re-test costs a submission slot and should wait for a reason better than "the consumer changed".

The harness is now correct for this: proxy_eval's base and both its swept coordinates derive from TrackerConfig.shipped(), so an unswept run measures what we submit.
close_reason:
CLOSED for min_track_length; smooth_strength stays LB-only and was never in scope for a proxy answer.

MEASURED at the shipped operating point (thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional), clamped column — the one validated 4/4 against the LB for count-changing knobs:
  min 1  faithful 0.9202  clamped 0.9202  bonus +0.0000
  min 4  faithful 0.9340  clamped 0.9332  bonus +0.0008
  min 6  faithful 0.9380  clamped 0.9353  bonus +0.0028   <- shipped
  min 8  faithful 0.9415  clamped 0.9353  bonus +0.0062

BOTH QUESTIONS ANSWERED, and the interesting one is answered against me:
1. NOT REMOVABLE. I argued the flow solver already prices track boundaries (disappearance_cost=3), so a post-hoc length filter would double-charge short tracks and might delete. Refuted: min 1 costs -0.0151 clamped, seven times the noise floor and the largest single-knob effect measured today. The two penalties are not the same object — the solver prices WHETHER TO START/END a track given the affinities, the filter removes SHORT COMPONENTS THAT SURVIVED that pricing.
2. SIX IS STILL RIGHT. min 8's entire faithful gain (+0.0035) is the node-count bonus: clamped is identical to min 6 to four decimals while the bonus more than doubles. That is the exact signature of the knob that anti-transferred before (threshold 0.995: +0.006 proxy, -0.007 LB). Reading the headline column would have spent a submission slot on nothing. min 4 loses 0.0021 and min 7 was already LB-tested worse (0.891 vs 0.892).

WIDER POINT WORTH KEEPING: this is the FIRST knob today whose optimum did NOT move when the consumer changed — five others did (threshold's ladder reversed, the ranker flipped sign, bidirectional fusion flipped sign, the checkpoint ranking inverted, the edge blend went from varying to flat). So consumer coupling is real but NOT universal, and the "re-arbitrate everything under flow" prior this bead was filed on is weaker than stated. Re-arbitrate where a mechanism suggests coupling, not by default.

smooth_strength: unchanged and still LB-only. It moves positions without changing node counts, so the clamped correction does nothing for it and the proxy reads it flat-to-inverted; its re-test costs a slot and needs a better reason than "the consumer changed".

title: Re-test own weights as an ensemble seed under the SHIPPED pipeline — the null that killed it was measured with the wrong instrument
description:
CLOSED ON 2026-08-10 as finetuning-adds-no-ensemble-value: joint_warm_cos3k added nothing to the two-seed blend (0.9315/0.9320 as a third scorer, 0.9325 replacing seed2, against a shipped 0.9334), and the conclusion drawn was that diversity comes from independent training rather than fine-tuning.

WHY IT IS WORTH RE-OPENING, and it is not a hunch: every one of those numbers was measured under a bare TrackerConfig - the per-frame assignment linker with no bidirectional fusion, i.e. the 0.892 pipeline, not the 0.895 one we submit. The re-ranking sweep of 2026-08-11 then showed that instrument INVERTS the ranking of our own checkpoints (cos3k 0.9175 -> 0.9153 while hn_control 0.9141 -> 0.9206), so the ensemble test was run with the same defective instrument AND on what turns out to be the wrong checkpoint.

TWO THINGS CHANGED AT ONCE, which is exactly why the old null does not carry:
1. The CHECKPOINT: joint_hn_control (0.9206 shipped) is our best own-weights model, not cos3k (0.9153). The ensemble was tested with the one that loses under the shipped pipeline.
2. The CONSUMER: a global flow linker prices track boundaries and reads a symmetric fused affinity, where the per-frame matcher wants the directional one. Blending changes the affinity, and we have leaderboard proof that the SIGN of an affinity-side change depends on the consumer (bidirectional fusion: -0.0027 assignment, +0.004 LB under flow).

THE ARMS, all on the test four at the shipped operating point (`--set` nothing; the base is now TrackerConfig.shipped()):
  a. shipped dual-seed control (pilkwang seed1 + seed2) - the 0.9334 anchor, re-measured so the comparison is like-for-like
  b. hn_control REPLACING seed2, at edge_blend 0.5/0.5 and 0.8/0.2
  c. hn_control as a THIRD edge scorer beside both packs
  d. hn_control alone (0.9206, already measured) as the floor

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT SHIPPABLE: beating 0.9334 by more than the 0.01-0.02 transfer floor is unlikely; beating it at all would make it a submission candidate on the transfer law's terms, since a blend change is a DECISION-RULE change of the kind that has transferred for us (greedy->global +0.005, flow+fusion +0.004) even when the proxy could not resolve it.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT PROPERLY: a null measured under the SHIPPED pipeline with the RIGHT checkpoint. That is a real refutation; the current one is an artefact.
design:
AUDIT BEFORE BUILDING (the machinery mostly exists; one constraint decides the design).

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE, so do not add a second mechanism:
- BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer takes N scorers and N weights (not two — arbitrary), blends them in LOGIT space,
  then soft-maxes over sources, and carries `bidirectional` + EdgeBlendOptions. A three-seed blend needs no new
  type at all.
- EdgeTransformerScorer.of(detector, transformer, recipe) binds a transformer to a detector, and
  ModelEvaluator.evaluate_joint already does exactly this for our own checkpoint — mounting it as a ONE-member
  blend, which is the shape a three-member blend generalises.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES THE WORK, stated in the blend's own docstring: "the gap node order (shared detector
nodes) is identical across seeds, so each seed's s×t logit matrix aligns row-for-row". Every scorer in a blend
must therefore score THE SAME DETECTIONS. In the shipped dual-seed blend that holds because both transformers
read their own backbone features at nodes produced by the BLENDED detector.

So the arms are not "our pipeline vs theirs": our checkpoint contributes its TRANSFORMER, reading ITS OWN
backbone features, at the detection nodes the two-pack blended detector produces. Pairing our transformer with
pilkwang's backbone features would be a silent mismatch (a head reading a representation it was never trained
on), and giving our detector its own node set would make the blend undefined rather than merely different.

Which also isolates the question properly: the detector half is held FIXED across every arm, so any movement is
attributable to the association head — the half where the score gap actually lives.

BUILD: an entrypoint that mounts the two packs plus a joint checkpoint and scores the N-way blend through the
shipped tracker. Closest existing shape is ModelEvaluator.evaluate_joint (one-member blend) — extend that path
rather than writing a parallel one, and keep the weights a CLI argument so the arms are config, not code.
notes:
NEW CONTEXT 2026-08-11 that changes what this bead is testing, from the blend re-measurement:

With the edge_blend knob actually connected (it was silently dead — see the with_weights fix), the blend weight
turns out to be CONSUMER-DEPENDENT:
  per-frame point (thr 0.97, boundary 0):  0.8/0.2 = 0.9334   0.5/0.5 = 0.9329   1.0/0.0 = 0.9312
  shipped point (flow b=3 + bidirectional): 0.8/0.2 = 0.9380   0.5/0.5 = 0.9380   0.6/0.4 = 0.9380
So under the pipeline we submit, the mix is flat across 0.5-0.8 while under the per-frame linker it is not.

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE: this bead asks whether OUR head adds to the two-seed blend. If the shipped consumer is
insensitive to how the two published heads are mixed, that is evidence the second seed's edge head is
contributing little THERE — which is exactly the room a third, genuinely differently-trained head would fill.
It also means the arms should not be read as "what weight is best" but as "does a DIFFERENT head move a score
that re-weighting the existing two cannot".

The 1.0/0.0 arm at the shipped point is the decisive prior for this bead and is running: if dropping seed 2's
edge head entirely is ALSO flat, then a whole mounted model is contributing nothing to the submission, which
both frees a slot in the blend and raises the prior that our head can take it. If 1.0/0.0 drops, seed 2 is
load-bearing and our head has to beat it rather than fill a gap.

Also note the ensemble null being re-tested (2026-08-10, joint_warm_cos3k adds nothing) was measured at the
per-frame point, where the mix demonstrably DOES matter — so it was measured in the regime where the existing
two seeds already separate, and against the checkpoint that loses under the shipped pipeline.

title: Print the mean in-gate candidate count at trainer startup — the corpus property that hid a defect for thirteen arms
description:
THE DEFECT IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: our GT-pair training corpus carries 0.99 candidate targets per source inside the shipped 10um linker gate, with only 1.9% of sources contested - against 3.80 and 95.4% on the real detections the tracker chooses among. The association head is trained on uncontested choices and deployed on contested ones. Nothing in the code looks wrong (the thinness is a property of 1.8% annotation density, not of the sampler), no number reads 1.0000 to tip you off, and it went unmeasured through thirteen association arms.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE OF REPORTING, not a mechanism: celltrack/data/candidate_density.py already computes it and celltrack/training/corpus_audit.py already exposes it as a CLI. What is missing is that the trainer does not print it at startup beside the pair count, so it remains a thing you have to think to ask rather than a thing you are told.

WHAT TO PRINT, per corpus, before the first step: pair count, mean in-gate candidates per source, and the fraction of sources with at least one rival - the gate coming from the SHIPPED linker config so the training and deployment questions are compared on the same radius rather than on an arbitrary one.

WHY IT GENERALISES BEYOND THIS CORPUS: the same three numbers are the acceptance test for any NEW pair source (tv3x's detection corpus, or any future synthetic or mined set). A corpus whose contested fraction is far from the deployment figure is training on a different question, and that should be visible at startup rather than inferred from a null result weeks later.

STANDING RULE THIS ENCODES: before training on a corpus, measure what a step actually ASKS. The existing rule (state the population before quoting any model-quality number) was written for measurements; the training-corpus version of the same failure is quieter and lasts longer.

title: Synthetic negatives are COMPLETE but not HARD — mine hard negatives from real detections instead
description:
Follow-on from gtbl's stage-1 null. Measured: on synthetic pairs the edge loss sits at 0.0041-0.0095 while real pairs run 0.20-0.53, at every window of both mixed arms. The warm-started head already solves the fully-labelled pairs, so the complete candidate set contributed almost no association gradient and the mixing was pure dilution (monotone damage 0.8598 -> 0.8456 -> 0.8320 at 0/25/50%).

The candidate-count audit says the geometry is NOT the problem: synthetic GT carries 2.79 in-gate rivals per source (77.8% of sources contested) against 3.80 on the dense movie's real detections (95.4% contested) — same regime. What the real corpus has and synthetic does not is negatives that are HARD, i.e. near-neighbours the current features cannot already separate.

So the property worth chasing is not completeness of labels but hardness of negatives, and the one corpus that has both is our OWN dense movie's DETECTIONS: 744/frame at the shipped operating point, of which all 38 mislinked partners are unannotated. The build is a pair source whose target_centres are the DETECTIONS (matched to GT where a match exists, unlabelled otherwise) with a loss that supervises only the columns adjudication can reach — a masked edge matrix, the association analogue of ignore_ambiguous_above. celltrack/data/frame_source.py + synthetic_pairs.py already give the seam a second corpus plugs into.

Instruments that exist: celltrack.training.corpus_audit (in-gate crowding per corpus), celltrack.eval.joint_eval (dense mislinks + P_true/P_chosen).
close_reason: Duplicate of tv3x - the build spec is folded into that bead so the direction has one home. tv3x is P0 and carries the same conclusion (hard negatives from real detections), plus the candidate-count audit that motivates it.

title: Derive the division fork cap from OUR measured rate, not a published one — the literature over-estimates it 3-10x
description:
MEASURED CORPUS-WIDE (2026-08-11): 151 divisions across 133,318 annotated nodes over 199 videos = 0.1133% per annotated node, 0.76 divisions per video. Our dense movie holds 3 among 1,229 annotated nodes = 0.244%, about 2x the corpus rate. With annotation covering ~1.8% of cells and estimated_node_count 69,800, a full annotation of that movie would hold roughly 79-170 divisions.

OUR RATE SITS BELOW EVERY LITERATURE ANCHOR: developmental 3D reports ~1.1% of cell-instances, 2D nuclei ~0.33%, we measure 0.113%. The likely cause is not biology but OBSERVATION WINDOW - our videos run ~100 frames while a cell cycle is longer, so most cells never divide on screen.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is the whole point of this bead: a division-rate prior imported from a paper would over-estimate our fork budget by 3-10x. The cap must be derived from OUR measured rate (0.11-0.24% of the cell population), not a published one. This is the same scale-mismatch trap that made the frontier's 0.75 evidence bonus an off-by-30 no-op when we ported it - a constant that is correct in its own pipeline and meaningless in ours.

WHY THE CAP IS THE LEVER: measured arms show the CAP, not the gates, drives the cost of the division stage - reachable gates at ~297 forks cost -0.0040 clamped while the same gates at ~50 forks cost -0.0005, under the noise floor. With D true divisions, F forks and precision p, div_jac = pF / (F + D - pF), so more forks pay only if precision holds.

ALSO CORRECTS A CITATION WE CARRIED IN THREE PLACES: the EDA's ~125 divisions in 6bba is an ACQUISITION TOTAL across 128 videos (~1 per video), not a per-movie count. The FP:TP argument survives on the rate-based derivation above, but it survived by luck rather than by care.

FEEDS: 1o18 (the division submission).
close_reason:
IMPLEMENTED and submitted.
