AffinityDivisionRecovery.budget() takes max_added_forks=None to mean the DERIVED budget: round(node_count * 0.00113) from our own corpus measurement (151 divisions / 133,318 annotated nodes / 199 videos), giving 29/36/8/84 forks on the four proxy movies against 1072 at the cap of 300. max_added_fraction was removed outright — it provably could not bind.

The leaderboard then made the derivation the OBVIOUS choice rather than a preference: cap 300 (1072 forks) and cap 100 (~400 forks) both scored 0.899, so the budget axis is flat and a hand-set ceiling that measurably does not bind is a magic number. Kernel v28 ships max_added_forks=None and is pending; it asks only whether the plateau reaches down to the phenomenon's own scale.

Edge-term cost at the derived budget measured separately: 0.0006 for 157 forks across the four movies, under a third of one mislink.

title: Appearance is NOT a division discriminator on our detections (measured 2026-08-11, clean null)
description:
CHEAP GATE, measured 2026-08-11 on 6bba_05db0fb1 at the shipped config (threshold 0.97, flow linker, disappearance_cost 3, bidirectional edges). Tool: `python -m celltrack.eval.mitotic_appearance` (celltrack/eval/mitotic_appearance.py, 26 unit tests).

QUESTION: do our candidate division mothers look mitotic in the RAW image? Motivated by research/deep_dives/2026-08-11_mitosis-detection-precision.md (PMC3278834: 9 static features + weighted SVM separate mitotic from interphase at >90%; Hirsch MICCAI 2022 cell-state head cuts FP divisions 7.5-17x).

ANSWER: NO. Clean null on all seven features, at two candidate floors.

METHOD. Raw full-resolution patches (6.5um half-box, physical masks, spacing z1.625/yx0.40625) around the DETECTION centres of four populations: the 3 annotated mothers + their run-up frames (n=8 frames), the forks AffinityDivisionRecovery.transform actually proposes, 3000 ordinary linked cells, and 1216 detections matched to ANNOTATED non-dividing cells (the annotated-vs-unannotated control the ~1.8% annotation rate demands). Features: intensity mean/sd/max, local contrast, half-max volume, intensity-weighted-centroid offset, second-moment elongation. No AUC computed — 3 positives cannot support one; every number is a per-mother percentile inside a named control.

THE THREE MOTHERS (GT rows are literally 232 / 624 / 771; ids 25000381@t24, 53001011@t52, 63001217@t62). At the split frame, percentile inside the false candidates / inside the annotated control:
  centroid offset  232: 82/73    624:  5/4     771: 97/95
  intensity mean   232: 18/30    624: 75/86    771: 12/22
  volume           232: 36/36    624: 80/89    771: 14/14
  elongation       232: 71/75    624: 41/46    771: 23/22
No feature places all three in a tail; on every feature 624 and 771 sit on OPPOSITE sides. Verdict line reads NONE at floor 0.25 (141 candidates) and floor 0.05 (187 candidates).

ANNOTATED-VS-UNANNOTATED CONTROL FIRES, in the confound direction: the candidate parents are the BRIGHTEST population (median intensity 1544) vs baseline 1388 vs annotated cells 1263. So brightness separates 'is a recovery candidate' from 'is annotated', not 'is mitotic' — exactly the artefact the control was built to catch. Any mothers-vs-candidates intensity story would have been reading that.

CAVEAT THAT DOES NOT RESCUE IT, but bounds what was refuted: the centroid-offset feature is measured from a centre quantised on the (1,4,4) read-out lattice (up to 0.81um per axis in y/x), and the whole feature range across every population is 0.2-1.3um. Mother 232 swings from the 82nd percentile at t-0 to the 5th at t-1. So the offset is refuted AS COMPUTED FROM THE DETECTION CENTRE; a sub-voxel-refined centre is a different (untested) measurement. Size/shape features carry no such caveat and are equally null.

SECONDARY FINDING, relevant to the cap/ranking work: at the SHIPPED gates (parent 4.7um, sister 7.2um, orphan runner-up, kept-child-is-top) the recovery proposes only 141 parents at P>=0.25 and 187 at P>=0.05 — dropping the floor 5x adds 46 candidates. The GATES bind, not the probability floor; the 807-FP figure in dla0's sibling issue comes from a wider geometry, not from this floor.

WHAT THIS CLOSES: a static-appearance discriminator (SVM-on-features, PMC3278834 style) on OUR detections. What it does NOT close: a learned 5-frame patch-stack cell-state head (Hirsch/Linajea) — that reads a temporal stack and a learned representation, neither of which this measures — and it does not close appearance measured from a refined centre or on a segmentation.
notes: Logs: scratchpad mitotic25.log / mitotic05.log. Both arms independently report NONE.
close_reason: RESULT bead - finding recorded in memory + interpretations, nothing left to do.

title: [P1] Curriculum on a COMPLETE candidate set: synthetic pairs + a feedback controller (audit done, plan below)
description:
AUDIT (read, not assumed).
 - celltrack/data/joint_dataset.py: PairTarget carries source_centres (annotated at t), target_centres (annotated at t+1), an s x u edge matrix read straight off the GT graph, and optional previous_centres. THE CANDIDATE SET IS THE ANNOTATED NODES. Every negative in that matrix is another ANNOTATED cell, so the unannotated detections that actually beat us are structurally absent - which is precisely what the hard-negative experiment concluded when its gradient landed on already-solved cases and sharpened the head globally.
 - celltrack/data/difficulty_sampler.py: optimistic init 1.0, draw/observe/coverage/entropy, mixture floor p = (1-a)/n + a*d/sum(d) with a=1/2. Difficulty is stored INSTANTANEOUSLY and used as a DRAW PROBABILITY.
 - No synthetic loader exists anywhere in celltrack/ or core/ - the earlier synthetic work used a throwaway probe.
 - Synthetic corpus, measured: 2174 sequences, each 6 frames of 64^3 with 1352 nodes (225/frame), 1151 edges, 47 divisions, plus voxel_um_pooled. That is ~10,870 fully-labelled consecutive-frame pairs and ~102,000 divisions.

WHY SYNTHETIC IS THE RIGHT ASSET HERE, and it is NOT "more data". Every cell in a synthetic frame is labelled, so target_centres would contain ALL cells including the crowded near-neighbours - the candidate set is COMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION. That is the one property our real corpus can never have (1.8% of cells annotated on the dense movie), and it is exactly the property the association failure needs. The same asset carries ~102k divisions against the THREE our real proxy holds, so it addresses both live objectives with one build.

PLAN, in dependency order.
 1. A SYNTHETIC PAIR SOURCE that emits the SAME PairTarget shape the trainer already consumes, so the loop does not care where a pair came from. Complete candidate sets fall out for free. Note the synthetic nodes are stored on the RAW (64,256,256) grid while volumes are pooled to 64^3 - divide y,x by 4 - a coordinate trap that already cost one wrong run.
 2. A CURRICULUM CONTROLLER, structured as a feedback loop rather than per-sample resampling: read the model's own eval score each window, EMA-smooth it, and drive ONE continuous difficulty knob. The knob is the SYNTHETIC MIXING FRACTION (complete-candidate, hard) against real pairs (sparse, easy). Higher score -> harder, by a scaling factor, exactly the teacher-paced shape.
 3. DIFFICULTY AS A WEIGHT, NOT A SELECTION. The documented SPL failure is starvation, and our own sampler demonstrated it (entropy 0.96 -> 0.235, edge loss exactly 0.0000, held-out recall 0.672 -> 0.201). A per-sample loss weight cannot starve anything and makes the mixture floor unnecessary.
 4. EMA DIFFICULTY, NOT INSTANTANEOUS - the stated mitigation for the oscillation mode, and the thing our sampler lacks. A pair measured at 0.0 once must not become unreachable.
 5. DIFFICULTY-ADJUSTED CHECKPOINT SELECTION, weight the validation metric by (0.5 + 0.5 * current_difficulty), IN THE SAME CHANGE. Without it a curriculum breaks the selector: later windows look worse purely because the data got harder, save-best keeps the easy-window checkpoint, and the experiment measures itself wrong.

THE CONSTRAINT THAT PROVES IT, and score alone will not do: the MISLINK COUNT on the real held-out dense movie must fall. Our floor is ONE mislink (0.0023 of dense jaccard against a ~0.002 noise floor), so a method needs about FIVE repairs to be distinguishable. The evidence-ramp arm already produced a score move with mislinks UNMOVED (38 -> 39), which is the failure this constraint exists to catch. Report mislinks, P_true and P_chosen alongside any score.

RISKS, stated now rather than discovered later.
 - PRIOR REFUTATION: lna trained the edge head on synthetic and measured MONOTONIC DOSE-DAMAGE (baseline pooled 0.9273 -> 0.9105 synth-only -> 0.9058 for a synth->real curriculum). That run had the UNet FROZEN, no masked detection loss, no controller, and its aim was to teach the TASK on synthetic. This differs on all four counts, and the claim here is narrower: synthetic supplies a COMPLETE CANDIDATE SET, not better images.
 - CROWDING MISMATCH: synthetic is 225 cells/frame in 64^3; our dense real movie runs ~743 detections/frame. The synthetic set may simply not contain the crowding that produces our failure, in which case complete candidates buy nothing. Measure the candidate counts per source before drawing conclusions.
 - DIVISION RATE IS INFLATED ~13x: 47/1352 = 3.5% of synthetic nodes divide against a real rate near 0.26%. A model trained on that will over-predict divisions, which on our metric is the expensive direction (false forks). The controller must be able to correct it, and the division head - if one is trained - needs its prior re-calibrated to the real rate.
close_reason: STAGE 1 IS A CLEAN NULL, and it refutes the premise rather than the implementation. Fixed-fraction synthetic mixing (0/25/50%) gave monotone damage 0.8598 -> 0.8456 -> 0.8320 with mislinks 41 -> 42 -> 43, despite differing from the prior lna refutation on all four counts (UNet unfrozen, masked detection loss, mixed rather than synth-only, complete-candidate framing). MECHANISM: synthetic edge loss 0.0041-0.0095 vs 0.20-0.53 on real pairs at every window - the warm-started head already solves the complete-candidate synthetic pairs, so the mixing was pure dilution. Completeness is necessary but NOT sufficient; the negatives must also be HARD. Stage 2 (PacedMixture feedback controller) is BUILT, unit-tested and default-off, correctly NOT run - a controller over a corpus that supplies no gradient measures nothing. It waits for a corpus that does: tv3x. NOT killed: node recall rose 0.9902 -> 0.9959 at 25% synthetic, the detection half's only real movement.

comments.author: dimiturtrz
comments.text: CROWDING RISK MEASURED (celltrack.training.corpus_audit, gate 10um, the shipped linker's own). Mean candidates inside the gate per source: synthetic GT 2.79 (296 sources/frame, 77.8% of sources have a rival) | real GT annotated 0.99 (12.3/frame, 1.9% have a rival) | real DETECTED on 6bba_05db0fb1 3.80 (744/frame, 95.4% have a rival). Reading: the crowding IS present in synthetic (2.79 vs 3.80, same regime) and the training candidate set we use TODAY is the outlier - 0.99 candidates per source means the loop essentially never sees a rival at all. That is the defect, quantified: a 4x gap between what training sees and what inference chooses among.

comments.author: dimiturtrz
comments.text:
STAGE 1 MEASURED (2026-08-11, warm start, lr 1e-5 cosine, masked det 0.97, 1000 steps, eval/250 — the joint_hn_control regime). Arms, fixed synthetic FRACTION, all from the same init (sel 0.8320):
  A 0%   peak clamped 0.8598 | dense 0.8794 / 41 mislinks / node R 0.9902 / P_true 0.203 vs 0.747 | test-four 0.9118 (clamped 0.9112) / 50 mislinks
  B 25%  peak clamped 0.8456 | dense 0.8848 / 42 mislinks / node R 0.9959 / P_true 0.234 vs 0.738 | test-four 0.9124 (clamped 0.9123) / 53
  C 50%  peak clamped 0.8320 = ITS INIT, never improved once | dense 0.8799 / 43 / node R 0.9927 | test-four 0.9100 (clamped 0.9094) / 53
Reference: joint_hn_control re-scored today reproduces the brief EXACTLY (dense 38 mislinks, test-four clamped 0.9136), so the eval is stable and the arms are comparable.

VERDICT: the lna dose-damage REPRODUCES, monotone, under all four differing conditions (UNet unfrozen, masked det loss, mixed not synth-only, complete-candidate framing): 0.8598 -> 0.8456 -> 0.8320. Mislinks move monotonically the WRONG way (41 -> 42 -> 43); every deliverable delta is inside the noise floor, so on the constraint that was supposed to prove it this is a clean null. Do NOT run the controller on this as-is.

MECHANISM, and it is the finding: the synthetic edge loss is 0.0041-0.0095 against 0.20-0.53 on real pairs, at every window of both arms. The warm-started head ALREADY solves the complete-candidate synthetic pairs. So a complete candidate set delivered almost NO association gradient — 25%/50% of the step budget went to an already-solved task, which is pure dilution, exactly matching the monotone damage. Completeness is necessary but NOT sufficient: the negatives must also be HARD, and synthetic near-neighbours are trivially separable even at 2.79 in-gate rivals per source. That is what the corpus does not have and what the next attempt must supply.

NOT KILLED: node recall rose with synthetic (0.9902 -> 0.9959 at 25%), the detection half's only movement, and the pair source is now tracked, tested and off by default.

title: [P1] Curriculum: our sampler is hard mining on the wrong axis — EMA not instantaneous, weight not select, and anti-curriculum is indicated
description:
THE USER'S OBSERVATION IS CORRECT: DifficultySampler IS hard mining, at the PAIR level. It draws each step's pair in proportion to its measured top-1 defect with optimistic initialisation so unseen pairs go first. It failed the way hard mining classically fails - entropy 0.96 -> 0.235, coverage 1.0 at 1.5 epochs, held-out recall 0.672 -> 0.201, train loss 0.0014 with EDGE LOSS EXACTLY 0.0000. We patched it with a mixture floor (p = (1-a)/n + a*d/sum d, a=1/2) and NEVER VALIDATED THE PATCH.

BUT IT MINES THE WRONG AXIS FOR OUR ACTUAL FAILURE. The sampler chooses WHICH ANNOTATED PAIR to show. Our mislinks are lost to UNANNOTATED DETECTIONS - measured: all 38 mislink targets are unannotated, and the trainer's pair corpus is GT-node-only. No pair-level weighting can put the actual competitor in the batch. Pair-level mining makes us see the hardest ANNOTATED example more often; CANDIDATE-level mining is what puts the decoy that beats us in front of the loss.

FOUR DESIGN CORRECTIONS, taken as structure (not code) from a prior curriculum-learning study the user pointed at, and all four are standard SPL literature (Bengio 2009 lineage) rather than anything proprietary:

1. EMA DIFFICULTY, NOT INSTANTANEOUS. The documented SPL failure mode "oscillation - hard examples become easy after one epoch of focus, then the model forgets them" has the mitigation "exponential moving average of difficulty scores, not instantaneous". Our sampler stores the LAST observation, and its docstring claimed staleness self-corrects because an improved model makes an old estimate read too high so the pair is redrawn. That holds only while every pair keeps a NONZERO draw probability - a pair measured at 0.0 is never redrawn, which is exactly the starvation we hit. EMA carries history and decays instead of dropping to zero.

2. WEIGHT, DO NOT SELECT. "Use SPL for weighting, not hard selection. Every sample contributes, but hard ones contribute more." Our sampler makes difficulty a DRAW PROBABILITY, which is what lets a pair vanish. A per-sample LOSS WEIGHT cannot starve anything and needs no mixture floor - strictly better than the patch we shipped.

3. A FEEDBACK LOOP ON A CONTINUOUS DIFFICULTY KNOB, adjusted per epoch from the model's own score, rather than per-sample resampling. Their analogue is a generation parameter (SNR): higher score -> make it harder, by a scaling factor. OUR ANALOGUE is the CANDIDATE POOL's hardness - the number of mined decoys per source, the decoy gate radius, or the fraction of decoys drawn from REAL DETECTIONS rather than annotated nodes. That last one is the axis our failure actually lives on.

4. DIFFICULTY-ADJUSTED CHECKPOINT SELECTION, which we do not have at all: weight the validation metric by (0.5 + 0.5 * current_difficulty) so a model scoring lower on HARD data can beat one scoring higher on easy data. WITHOUT THIS A CURRICULUM BREAKS OUR SELECTOR - later windows look worse purely because the data got harder, and save-best keeps the easy-window checkpoint. Any curriculum we build needs this in the same change or it will measure itself wrong.

ANTI-CURRICULUM IS INDICATED FOR US, NOT EASY-FIRST. The study's condition for hard-first is "when easy examples create shortcuts - if easy examples have spurious correlations, starting easy teaches the shortcut". That is our situation precisely: our easy population is GT-only pairs where the truth wins by ~4 logits (hn loss 0.017 at init), and we measured corr(P, distance) = -0.893 with the head's within-band AUC collapsing to chance at short range because 96% of in-gate candidates ARE the true successor there. Easy-first would train the near=successor shortcut harder.

SO THE BUILD, in dependency order:
 a. A DETECTION-MATCHED PAIR SOURCE - the trainer cannot express real-detection decoys today, and that is the blocker for every version of this.
 b. Candidate difficulty as a FEEDBACK-CONTROLLED knob (decoy count / decoy origin), EMA-smoothed, applied as a WEIGHT.
 c. Difficulty-adjusted selection, in the same change.
 d. Ramp HARD-first or hard-early given the shortcut argument, and measure the mislink count rather than the score - our floor is one mislink (0.0023) and a method needs ~5 repairs to clear it.

title: [P1] Divisions: never LB-tested, our gates exclude the one recoverable case, and the proxy cannot arbitrate the axis
description:
FIVE FACTS THAT COMPOUND, and together they say divisions are the least-tested axis we own.

1. NEVER MEASURED ON THE LEADERBOARD. NOT ONCE. The kernel celltrack-pilktunet-motion-divstlf was written 2026-08-02 with its threshold deliberately pinned at 0.5 "so its LB delta is attributable to divisions alone" - and never pushed. Every division verdict on record is PROXY-ONLY, including tonight's -0.0039.

2. OUR SHIPPED GATES PROVABLY EXCLUDE THE ONE RECOVERABLE DIVISION. The three divisions in the proxy were dissected on 2026-08-03 (interpretations/tracking/2026-08-03_division-recovery-edge-affinity.md):
   232 @t24 - both daughters detected, 2nd is an ORPHAN and the parent's RANK-1 target, edge-P 0.124, parent->2nd 6.08um, SISTER DISTANCE 13.5um. RECOVERABLE.
   771 @t62 - both detected but the 2nd is already linked to another parent (in_degree 1), P 0.0246 at rank 2. Structurally out of reach.
   624 @t52 - one daughter never detected. Unreachable by any linker.
   We ship AffinityDivisionConfig(parent_gate_um=4.7, sister_gate_um=7.2). 232 needs >=6.08 AND >=13.5. BOTH GATES EXCLUDE IT. We are not failing to find it; we are refusing to consider it.

3. TWO GATE DISAGREEMENTS IN OUR OWN DOCS, NEVER RECONCILED.
   PARENT: "the parent gate's optimum is 10.5um, independently reproducing the frontier's constant" (session-handoff 2026-08-02) vs "the faithful frontier port (tight 4.7um parent gate)" (ranked-open-levers 2026-08-03). One day apart, both called "the frontier's". Under the 10.5 reading the one reachable division IS reachable by the faithful port.
   SISTER: "the radius wants to be TIGHT - 7um 0.9980, 15um 0.9960, 25um 0.9902; reaching further only invents divisions" (division-linking 2026-07-23) vs "their 8.0um sister gate is FAR TOO TIGHT here; the plateau starts at 18um" (session-handoff 2026-08-02). Both measured on GT nodes, fold 0, ten days apart, neither citing the other. Possible reconciliation nobody wrote down: one may be the daughter-to-PARENT radius and the other the daughter-to-SISTER radius.
   The current public frontier (source-read 2026-08-11) uses SAFE_DIV_MAX_UM 4.66, SAFE_DIV_SISTER_MAX_UM 8.5, SAFE_DIV_EXISTING_CHILD_MAX_UM 7.65, frame cap 0.0076, global cap 0.00375.

4. THE PROXY CANNOT RANK THIS AXIS - measured 2026-08-11: the four proxy movies hold 3 annotated divisions TOTAL, all in 6bba_05db0fb1; the other three have ZERO. On a movie with no annotated divisions, emitting any fork can only produce false positives. Meanwhile the EDA counted ~125 divisions in 6bba and ~26 in 44b6, so the hidden denser annotation has far more targets. This is the THRESHOLD situation exactly: an axis the local proxy structurally cannot arbitrate, where the leaderboard is the only judge.

5. THE METRIC IS FAR MORE FORGIVING THAN THE CORPUS BELIEVED, and we forfeit the term by construction. Read from core/metrics/divisions.py: each GT division opens a GRANDPARENT-TO-GRANDCHILDREN window and credit is by REACHABILITY - "a predicted fork recovers the division when it sits on the parent side and reaches two of the ground-truth daughter lineages down two DIFFERENT branches of its own". Not exact edges, not the exact frame. The research corpus's "requires strict topology, parent -> 2 daughters" is wrong. AND our shipped FlowLinker splits each detection with a capacity-1 arc, so it emits ZERO forks and div_jaccard is exactly 0 - we give away the whole 0.1x term structurally, not through detection limits.

THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS PRECISION, NOT RECALL. The uncapped affinity run placed the true fork and drowned it: TP 1, FP 807, div_jac 0.0009. Capped runs then evict 232 (bottom of the P ranking) and score div_jac exactly 0.

WHAT TO DO: one submission slot. Gates widened to REACH the known-recoverable geometry (parent >= 6.5, sister >= 14) against a HARD ABSOLUTE cap on forks - not a fraction of node count, which on 74k detections permits ~300 forks for what is locally 3 targets. The proxy will read this as flat-or-negative and that reading carries no information; only the leaderboard can arbitrate it.
BEFORE SPENDING THE SLOT: rebuild the kit (TrackerConfig moved to celltrack/operating_point.py) and verify the fork count actually emitted, because a config that emits zero forks is indistinguishable on the proxy from one that emits three.
notes:
RESOLVED ON THE LEADERBOARD 2026-08-11. This bead's premise was "divisions have never been LB-tested and the
proxy cannot arbitrate the axis". Both halves are now settled:

  v26 (55433641) = 0.899 PUBLIC — NEW BEST, +0.004 over 0.895.
Config: symmetry ranking, probability floors OFF, gates 7.0/14.0, cap 297 (the nominal 300 was silently bound
by the then-existing max_added_fraction — worth stating precisely, since the arm is a data point).

WHAT THE PROXY COULD AND COULD NOT SAY, confirmed by the result: it ranked the arm 0.9434 vs 0.9353, but with
three annotated divisions that number is dominated by an FP:TP ratio 30-50x worse than the hidden set's. The
signals that actually transferred were the FORK COUNT and whether the one recoverable division survived. Do
not read div_jac off this proxy again; read the fork count and the edge-term cost.

STILL OPEN, and it is the whole remaining question: WHERE on the budget axis. v27 (cap 100) is pending and
brackets v26's 297. The budget is now DERIVED rather than guessed — node_count * 0.113% (our measured rate)
gives ~83 for the dense movie — so the pair reads as a test OF that derivation: v26 at ~3.6x it, v27 at ~1.2x.

DECISION DEFERRED DELIBERATELY: TrackerConfig.shipped() still has division=None. It should carry the division
config once the budget axis resolves, per the standing rule that a knob arbitrated by the leaderboard must be
the DEFAULT rather than living at one call site. Changing it now would bake in either an untested cap (the
derived 83) or a cap that no longer exists in the code (297 came from a parameter since removed).
close_reason:
Superseded by results. Divisions are now LB-tested: symmetry ranking = 0.899 twice (new best, from 0.895), and the budget axis is flat between ~400 and ~1072 forks. The gates that excluded the one recoverable case were widened and then DERIVED from the linker's own (a fork is a one-frame step; the sister gate is twice the parent gate by the triangle inequality), so no gate number is chosen any more.

The proxy-cannot-arbitrate point STANDS as a caveat: three annotated divisions, an FP:TP ratio 30-50x worse than the hidden set's, and it read the winning configuration as COSTING 0.009 while the leaderboard paid +0.004. Read the fork count and the edge cost from the proxy; read the division term only from the leaderboard.

title: [P1] celltrack.tracker is a god-module (fan-in 9 x fan-out 13) — move the shared config vocabulary to the package root
description:
BLOCKING: `celltrack.tracker: fan-in 9 x fan-out 13 (both > 8) - god-module`. Tripped when celltrack/eval/localisation.py became the NINTH importer. Fan-out was already 13 (the orchestrator legitimately imports detectors, edges, linkers, postproc, precision); fan-in crossed the line.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX LOOKS BLOCKED, AND IS NOT. The repo rule says "a supplementary type lives BESIDE its producer - never bucket types by KIND", which reads as "TrackerConfig belongs next to CellTracker". But the SAME rule continues: "shared vocabulary several producers speak goes at the PACKAGE ROOT, not a leftovers module". TrackerConfig is exactly that - eval/proxy_eval, eval/dense_diagnosis, eval/localisation, eval/model_evaluator, eval/bracket, training/, both Kaggle kernels and multi_gpu_submission all speak it, and most of them do NOT want CellTracker at all. It is shared vocabulary, not a supplementary type, so a root-level home is what the rule prescribes rather than an exception to it.

PROPOSED: move TrackerConfig (and EdgeBlendOptions if it travels with it) to its own root-level module, leaving celltrack/tracker.py owning the MOUNT and the RUN. Every config-only consumer then imports the config module and not the orchestrator, which is the fan-in the gate is objecting to. Check the number after the move rather than assuming - if fan-in stays above 8 the real split is CellTracker's own responsibilities (it currently mounts packs, holds ephemeral/with_config re-pointing, runs the stage chain, and exposes the two-pass ranked path).

DO NOT "fix" THIS BY RAISING THE THRESHOLD. Thresholds in [tool.structure] are legislated values, never seeded from the repo's current state - that is the whole point of a ratcheting gate. The gate is correct here: a module that nine others import and that itself imports thirteen IS the shape the rule exists to catch, and it got there by accretion, one eval tool at a time.

CONTEXT: found by an agent's verification, not by the pre-commit hook, because the breach arrived via an UNTRACKED file - `git status` showed `?? celltrack/eval/localisation.py`, so nothing staged it and the hook never saw it. Worth noting as a gap: a new module can breach the architecture gate while every commit stays green until it is first added.
close_reason: FIXED 2026-08-11, measured not assumed: celltrack.tracker fan-in 9 -> 5, gate CLEAN. TrackerConfig moved to celltrack/operating_point.py - named for the thing it owns (the tracker's operating point, one cohesive knob vocabulary, one class) rather than a types/config/schema kind-bucket. The repo rule PRESCRIBED this rather than blocking it: 'supplementary type beside its producer' covers types belonging to one producer, while 'shared vocabulary several producers speak goes at the package root' covers this one - four importers (eval/localisation, eval/sweep_tracking, training/tunet_detector, training/joint_detector) only ever wanted the vocabulary and no longer import the tracker at all. No re-export was left behind, which is why the import edge actually disappeared. EdgeBlendOptions did NOT travel (it lives beside its producer already). Thresholds untouched. 706 tests, import-linter 2 kept.

title: [P1] Mislink endpoints sit 2.1x further from their cell — matcher artefact, or detection failures wearing a mislink label?
description:
MEASURED AND UNEXPLAINED: the endpoints of our 38 dense mislinks sit a median 3.495um from their annotated cell, against 1.675um for all 1224 matched detections - 2.1x the population. It is not quantisation (only 27-46% of their per-axis offsets fall inside the grid-explainable half-block, against 74-83% for the population) and it is not crowding (detections with a rival inside the 7um matching radius read 1.675um, IDENTICAL to the population). At the exact nodes where we fail, the peak is genuinely 2-4 voxels off the annotated cell.

THE CONFOUND THAT DECIDES WHAT THIS MEANS, and it must be resolved before anything is built on it: a GT node is "matched" if SOME detection lands within 7um. If the CORRECT detection is missing, the matcher will happily pair the GT node with a NEIGHBOURING cell s detection up to 7um away - and that pairing would produce exactly this elevated offset. In that case the edge is not a MISLINK at all; it is an ENDPOINT_MISSING case wearing a mislink label, and our dense fate decomposition is mis-attributing it.
Note this is NOT already excluded by the classifier having a separate ENDPOINT_MISSING class: that class fires when a GT endpoint matches NOTHING within 7um. A GT node matched to the WRONG detection inside 7um still counts as matched, so it lands in MISLINK.

THE MEASUREMENT, cheap, uses celltrack/eval/localisation.py which already loads everything:
For each of the 38 mislinks, take the TRUE successor s GT node and ask:
 1. distance to the detection the matcher assigned it
 2. distance to the NEAREST detection of any kind
 3. how many detections lie within 7um of it
Then classify:
 - MATCHER SUBOPTIMAL: a detection exists materially closer than the assigned one. That is a MATCHING defect, and it would mean our fate decomposition (and possibly the score) is mis-attributing edges. Check whether DistanceMatcher is greedy or optimal - a greedy nearest-first pass can strand a node onto a far detection when a nearer one was taken first.
 - TRUE DETECTION GENUINELY ABSENT: the nearest detection IS the assigned one and it is 3-4um away, i.e. the cell was detected badly or not at all and a neighbour absorbed the match. Then these are detection failures, the "signal-limited association" reading is partly wrong for these 38, and the fix is on the detection side after all.
 - DETECTION FINE: the assigned detection is close and the 3.5um median comes from a subset. Report the split rather than the median.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE 38: it questions how the campaign has attributed its losses. We concluded "detection is finished" from RECALL (0.988-0.997) and spent everything on association. Recall only asks whether a peak lands within 7um of an annotated cell - it cannot see a peak that lands within 7um of the WRONG cell, and 7um is over four times the median inter-frame step of 1.675um. A matching radius that generous can call a detection correct while handing the linker a position belonging to a different cell.

ALSO WORTH RESOLVING IN THE SAME PASS: 49.8% of ALL matched detections sit a whole 1.625um z-plane or more from the annotated z. z is NOT downsampled, so no read-out refinement addresses it, and because GEFF stores integer voxel indices we cannot tell whether it is our peak or the annotator s rounding. If the z offset is systematic (a consistent sign or a half-plane bias) that is our bug; if it is symmetric it is probably annotation granularity. The signed per-axis medians were 0.000 on all three axes for the population, which argues symmetric - but that was not broken out for the mislink subset.
notes:
MATCHER BRANCH LARGELY PRE-CLOSED by reading core/metrics/matching.py, before the measurement runs. DistanceMatcher._assign builds weights = 1.0/(1.0 + distance) over pairs within max_distance_um and solves min_weight_full_bipartite_matching(maximize=True) - i.e. GLOBALLY OPTIMAL under a weight that is strictly DECREASING in distance, per timepoint. So the greedy-strands-a-node failure mode does not exist here: a GT node cannot be paired with a 6um detection while a 0.4um one is free, because that swap strictly raises the objective. Expect the MATCHER SUBOPTIMAL branch to come back near zero; if it does NOT, that is a bug in the matcher and a much bigger finding than the one this bead is about.
ONE REAL PROPERTY TO KEEP IN MIND, though it is defensible rather than wrong: 1/(1+d) is strongly CONCAVE, so it saturates with distance. Improving a pair from 7um to 6um gains 0.018 of objective while degrading one from 0.4um to 1.4um costs 0.16. The optimum will therefore happily sacrifice a DISTANT node s pairing quality to protect a NEAR one s. That does not mis-pair when a better option is free, but it does mean large offsets are cheap for the objective to tolerate - so a 3.5um pairing survives easily if the alternative assignment would disturb a tight pair elsewhere.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD: weight the two remaining branches accordingly. The live hypothesis is now TRUE DETECTION GENUINELY ABSENT-OR-DISPLACED (the nearest detection IS the assigned one and it is 3-4um out), which would mean these 38 are detection failures wearing a mislink label and the signal-limited reading is partly wrong for them. Measure branch 2 first; branch 1 is a control that should come back empty.

title: [P1] Divisions were closed as detection-limited BEFORE the NMS over-merge fix — the bug merged exactly the cells divisions need
description:
A CONCLUSION COLLECTED UNDER A BUG THAT WAS LATER FIXED, AND NEVER RE-CHECKED.

THE TIMELINE IS THE WHOLE ARGUMENT:
 - 2026-08-02, divisions closed: "div_jac caps 0.0114 vs 0.4468 on GT nodes = DETECTION-LIMITED - most true 2nd-daughters undetected so the fork cannot be placed". Also measured: once ShortTrackFilter(6) prunes short false chains, divisions turn NET-NEGATIVE (0.9090 -> 0.9085).
 - 2026-08-04, the NMS over-merge fix: our peak suppression window was 5^3 where the reference is 3^3, so we were MERGING CELLS 2 VOXELS (3.25um) APART. Fixing it moved the dense movie's RAW edge jaccard 0.849 -> 0.892 (+0.043, bonus-independent) purely by un-merging crowded cells.
SISTER DAUGHTERS IMMEDIATELY AFTER A DIVISION ARE EXACTLY THAT KIND OF PAIR. The frontier's own division gates put sisters at 7.2-8.5um and parent-child at 4.7um, and the EDA measured division edges around 5um against a continuation median of 1.7um - so the two daughters start close together and separate over subsequent frames. A 3.25um merge radius sits right inside that window. The detector that "could not detect second daughters" was running a read-out that merged adjacent cells.

SO THE DETECTION-LIMITED VERDICT IS UNSAFE. It may still be true - the daughters could be genuinely unresolved rather than merged by our window - but the measurement that established it cannot distinguish those two cases, because the bug produced exactly the symptom the conclusion attributes to the data.

WHAT IT IS WORTH IF IT MOVED: score = adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard, and div_jac currently contributes ~0.1 * 0.011 = 0.001, i.e. nothing. The GT-node ceiling of 0.4468 says the DECISION RULE can place forks when the nodes exist. If un-merging recovered even a fraction - div_jac 0.011 -> 0.05 - that is 0.1 * 0.039 = +0.004, above our 0.002 proxy floor and comparable to the flow+fusion gain that is our only leaderboard win. Not a large lever, but a CHEAP one on an axis we stopped looking at, and entirely independent of the association wall that has absorbed the whole campaign.

THE CHEAP GATE, before rebuilding anything:
 1. Re-measure the division ceiling POST-NMS-FIX: how many annotated division events have BOTH daughters detected now, versus at the time of the original measurement? That single count decides it. The original said most second daughters were undetected; if that fraction has moved materially, the conclusion is overturned by construction.
 2. Re-run DivisionRecovery at the corrected gates (parent 4.7, sister 7.2, existing-child 7.8, per-frame 0.8%, global 0.4%) on the CURRENT shipped config (thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional) and report both div_jac and total score against the control. Note the original A/B was run at thr 0.99 with the ASSIGNMENT linker and the 5^3 window - three things have changed since.
 3. Check the STLF interaction specifically, since that is what turned divisions net-negative before: does ShortTrackFilter still prune the recovered daughter chains? A daughter track that is genuinely detected for several frames should now survive min_track_length 6 where a merged-then-split artefact would not.

STANDING LESSON THIS INSTANCES: when a BUG FIX lands, re-audit the conclusions that were measured before it - not just the code paths it touched. The NMS fix was recorded as improving dense raw jaccard, and its effect on the DIVISION conclusion was never considered, because the division work had already been filed as closed. A closed question measured under a since-fixed bug is not closed.
close_reason: RE-TESTED AND STILL NEGATIVE 2026-08-11 - my stale-conclusion hypothesis is refuted. The reasoning was sound in structure (divisions were closed 2026-08-02 as detection-limited; the NMS over-merge fix landed 2026-08-04 and un-merged cells 3.25um apart, which is sister-daughter separation) and wrong in fact. AffinityDivisionConfig at the frontier gates (parent 4.7, sister 7.2, min_second_prob 0.5, min_kept_prob 0.5, max_added_fraction 0.004) on the current shipped config: control clamped 0.9353 vs division 0.9314 = -0.0039, about 2x the noise floor, and WORSE than the +0.0002 the original A/B measured. NOT resolved and worth knowing if anyone revisits: the proxy prints only the TOTAL, and score = adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1*div_jaccard, so whether div_jac rose while the edge term fell further is unknown - print the two terms separately before theorising. Also not matched to the original (0.99+assignment then, 0.97+flow+bidirectional now). Worth the one 5-minute run: the axis is worth up to 0.045 at the GT-node ceiling against the 0.001 we bank.

title: [P1] Detections are quantised to 1.625um voxels — and the median true step is 1.7um. Never measured position accuracy, only recall
description:
OUR DETECTIONS ARE QUANTISED TO THE VOXEL GRID AND THE GRID IS THE SIZE OF THE MOTION.
PeakExtractor returns Int[np.ndarray, "k 3"] everywhere (centres, above_threshold, maxima) - raw argmax voxel indices, no sub-voxel refinement anywhere in the detector. After the (1,4,4) downsample a voxel is 1.625um ISOTROPIC. The median annotated inter-frame displacement is 1.7um. So the position quantisation is the same size as the quantity we are trying to measure.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS A CANDIDATE MECHANISM FOR THE MISLINKS:
 - Each coordinate is rounded to a voxel centre, so per-axis error is up to +-0.8um, and the 3D offset can approach ~1.4um.
 - A STEP is a difference of TWO independently quantised positions, so the measured displacement carries roughly sqrt(2)x that noise.
 - A true step of 1.7um can therefore measure anywhere from near 0 to ~3.5um, while a WRONG neighbour whose true separation is 2.5um can measure as little as ~1um.
That is exactly the observed failure: on the 38 dense mislinks the chosen wrong target is CLOSER than the true successor 87% of the time, and the head - which is fed the pair's relative displacement - is confidently wrong (P_true 0.079 vs P_chosen 0.589). Quantisation noise of this size can invert the ordering of the two candidates by itself, in BOTH the linker's distance term AND the head's input.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN TESTED: the whole campaign measured detection RECALL (0.988-0.997, saturated on every axis, seven refuted detector levers) and never once measured detection POSITION ACCURACY. "The detector is finished" was concluded from recall alone. Recall says the peak is in the right place to within 7um (the matching radius); it says nothing about being right to within 1um, which is what the linker needs.

THE CHEAP GATE - RUN THIS BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING:
For matched detections on the dense movie, measure the offset between the detection's voxel-centre position and the GT node's (float, sub-voxel) position. Report the distribution in um, per axis and in 3D.
 - If the median 3D offset is ~0.7-0.9um, quantisation noise is confirmed at the predicted scale and is roughly HALF the median true step. Build the refinement.
 - If it is much smaller, the peaks already sit near the true centres (possible - a response maximum need not be at the annotated centroid but could be systematically close), and this is closed.
ALSO REPORT, because it is the decisive comparison: the offset distribution restricted to the 38 MISLINK endpoints versus all matched detections. If mislink endpoints carry LARGER localisation error, the mechanism is not just plausible but implicated.

THE FIX IF THE GATE PASSES: sub-voxel peak refinement - a quadratic/parabolic fit to the response in the 3x3x3 neighbourhood of each maximum, or an intensity-weighted centroid over that neighbourhood. Standard, cheap (vectorisable over all peaks at once), no retraining, no new model, and it acts at INFERENCE so our warm-start regime cannot obscure it.

TWO RISKS TO RESPECT, both testable:
 1. THE HEAD WAS TRAINED ON QUANTISED COORDINATES. Feeding it refined sub-voxel `rel` changes its input distribution - the same off-distribution trap that the ranker port had to be checked for. Safer first arm: refine positions for the LINKER'S DISTANCE TERM ONLY and leave the head's input untouched, then test refining both as a second arm.
 2. The node positions we EMIT are also the ones scored. Sub-voxel positions should HELP matching (7um radius, so marginal) but they change the submitted CSV; verify the emitted coordinates round-trip correctly through the submission path.

PRIOR: moderate-to-good. It is physics rather than a knob, it targets the exact failure shape (a near wrong cell beating a far true one), it costs no training, and it is the one axis of detection quality nobody measured because recall looked saturated.
close_reason: REFUTED 2026-08-11 by three independent numbers. (1) In-plane localisation error is a QUARTER of the median step, not half: median |offset| y/x = 0.406um = one full-res voxel, 83% inside the grid-explainable half-block, against a median annotated step of 1.675um. (2) ZERO displacement collisions in 38 mislinks and 1102 correct-edge controls, and it is structurally impossible - the NMS suppression radius IS a cell radius, so two surviving detections can never occupy the same lattice cell. The head always had geometrically distinguishable input. (3) The margin is far too wide to flip: at the mislinks the chosen rival is nearer by a median +6.474um, rival-nearer in 97.4% of cases, with only 7.9% inside sqrt(2)x the measured noise. PREMISE CORRECTION worth keeping: GEFF stores integer voxel indices, so GT is NOT sub-voxel, and z is not downsampled so that axis cannot see sub-voxel error at all. Residue filed as ekyl: mislink endpoints carry 2.1x the population's localisation error and it is NOT quantisation (27-46% grid-explainable vs 74-83%). Tool: celltrack/eval/localisation.py.

title: Two-seed DISAGREEMENT is computed and discarded — does the ensemble know where it fails?
description:
WE COMPUTE A DISAGREEMENT SIGNAL EVERY RUN AND DISCARD IT. BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer mounts two independently-trained edge heads (pilkwang seed1 + seed2), blends their RAW LOGITS 0.8/0.2 and soft-maxes. The blend keeps only the weighted MEAN. The DISPERSION between the two heads - the one thing an ensemble gives you for free that a single model cannot - is thrown away before the linker ever sees it.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A PROBE NOW, and why it is not another affinity retrain: the dense mislinks are SIGNAL-limited, confirmed on seven independent axes. On the 38 mislinks of the shipped config the head is CONFIDENTLY WRONG - 97.4% affinity-inverted, mean P_true 0.079 against P_chosen 0.589. Every fix tried so far tries to make the signal BETTER (retrain on synthetic, on real positives, on hard negatives, contrastive features) or to REWEIGHT it (bonus sweeps, the distance ramp, the ported ranker). All refuted. Disagreement is a different move: it does not try to make the head right, it asks whether the head KNOWS it is unreliable on exactly these pairs.

THE MEASUREMENT, which is cheap and decisive and must come BEFORE any build:
On the dense movie at the shipped config, for every candidate pair, record both seeds' probabilities and a dispersion statistic (|p1 - p2|, and also the logit gap, since we blend in logit space). Then split by the fate the existing dense_diagnosis already assigns:
  - dispersion on CORRECT edges (n~1122)
  - dispersion on the MISLINK pairs - both the WRONG edge we chose and the TRUE edge we missed (n~38 each)
Report the distributions, not just means. The decisive number is the AUC of dispersion at separating mislinked pairs from correct ones - i.e. does disagreement KNOW where we fail?

INTERPRETATION, decided in advance:
 - If dispersion is clearly higher on mislinks: the ensemble carries an uncertainty signal that the mean discards, and there is something to build (downweight high-dispersion edges in the cost, or gate them, or let a global solver route around them). That would be the first NEW information found in this pipeline in a long time - free, already computed, never used.
 - If dispersion is flat across fates: the two heads are confidently wrong TOGETHER, which is itself a strong finding - it means the failure is shared by independently-trained models and is therefore a property of the FEATURES or the RESOLUTION, not of one model's training. That closes the ensemble-uncertainty direction and hardens the signal-limited conclusion considerably.
Either way the probe pays. Do not build the cost term before the measurement.

PRIOR, honest: the two seeds share an architecture, a training recipe and a dataset, differing only in initialisation, so their errors are likely correlated - and the seed-scale measurement already showed their logit distributions are near-identical (std ratio 1.1215, mean gap -0.4335). So flat dispersion is the more likely outcome. It is worth running anyway BECAUSE the flat outcome is informative: "two independent models fail identically on the same 38 pairs" is much stronger evidence for a resolution/feature wall than any single-model result we have.

NOTE A RELATED DEAD END SO IT IS NOT RE-RUN: agreement GATING between the forward and reverse affinity (mutual consistency) was tested in all four linker pairings and is dead - but that is DIRECTIONAL agreement within ONE model, not agreement between two INDEPENDENT models. Different quantity, different claim.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer already holds the per-seed scorers and already computes both logit sets (seed_logit_moments exists and walks them), so the probe needs no new forward pass beyond what a normal affinity run does - and the response cache makes the detection side free.
close_reason: MEASURED null: raw logit gap flat to 3dp across CORRECT/MISLINK/missed-true, AUC 0.522-0.540 = chance. Probability spread looked informative but is bounded by 4P(1-P) - the bound alone outranks it. Seeds fail together = feature/resolution wall.

title: [P1] Half our false positives are unclassified — the mislink diagnostic is GT-edge-centric and FPs outnumber FNs
description:
OUR MISLINK DIAGNOSTIC CANNOT SEE HALF OUR FALSE POSITIVES, and false positives are the LARGER error term.

ARITHMETIC, dense movie 6bba_05db0fb1, post-NMS-fix, thr 0.99 (dense_diagnosis + EdgeCounts):
  TP 1122   FP 75   FN 61   jaccard = 1122/1258 = 0.892
  fate classes over the 1183 GT edges: CORRECT 1122, MISLINK_CONFLICT 26, SKIP 14, ENDPOINT_MISSING 12, MISLINK_FREE 9
The classes account for EVERY false negative (26+14+12+9 = 61, exact). They account for only 35 of the 75 false positives - one wrong edge per mislink. FORTY FALSE POSITIVES ARE UNCLASSIFIED, 53% of the FP term.

WHY THEY ARE INVISIBLE: celltrack/eval/dense_diagnosis.py is GT-EDGE-CENTRIC. It iterates the 1183 TRUE edges and asks what happened to each. A PREDICTED edge that has no GT edge to attach to - both endpoints matched to GT nodes, but GT joins them to nothing or to something else entirely - is never enumerated, because there is no true edge whose fate it is. The instrument answers "what did we lose" and is structurally blind to "what did we invent".

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ANYTHING WE CHASED: jaccard = TP/(TP+FP+FN), so an FP costs exactly as much as an FN. We have spent the campaign on the 61 FNs (mislinks, skips, endpoint-missing) and never once enumerated the 75 FPs. If the 40 unexplained ones were eliminated the dense movie goes 1122/(1122+35+61) = 0.921, i.e. +0.029 on the movie that carries most of the pooled weight - larger than the whole 0.020 gap to the frontier.

WHAT TO BUILD: a PREDICTION-CENTRIC decomposition. Iterate OUR emitted edges whose BOTH endpoints match GT nodes (the only ones the scorer charges us for) and classify each:
  - TRUE          GT joins these two nodes
  - MISLINK       source has a GT successor, we picked a different target (expect ~35, the known set)
  - SOURCE_ENDS   source has NO GT successor at all - the GT track ends here and we linked on anyway
  - TARGET_ORPHAN target has no GT predecessor - we invented a parent for it
  - CROSS_TRACK   both belong to GT tracks, but different lineages
  - SYNTHETIC     the edge involves a DensityGapBridge inserted node
The counts alone decide the next move, and each class has a DIFFERENT fix - SOURCE_ENDS is a boundary-price question, CROSS_TRACK is an affinity question, SYNTHETIC is a post-proc question.

WATCH THE ANNOTATION-SPARSITY CONFOUND, it may explain the whole thing: our annotations cover ~1-2% of cells, so a GT track "ending" usually means THE ANNOTATION STOPPED, not that the cell died. If SOURCE_ENDS dominates, those edges are probably TRUE against the hidden DENSER annotation and our local FP count is an artefact of sparsity - which would ALSO mean this is not a real lever and the honest outcome is a closed question. Note the tension to resolve: sparsity-induced phantom FPs should make the proxy UNDERSHOOT the leaderboard, and ours OVERSHOOTS (0.9334 vs 0.895), so the simple story does not fit and the counts are needed to tell which effect dominates.

CONNECTS TO A MEASUREMENT WE ALREADY HAVE: the flow boundary-cost sweep reads 0=0.9344, 3=0.9351, 6=0.9313, 10=0.9282. Boundary cost is what a track PAYS to end, so a HIGHER cost makes the solver more reluctant to end a track - i.e. more willing to link on past a GT track end. The score falling monotonically above 3 is consistent with over-linking being real and priced. If SOURCE_ENDS is the dominant class, that sweep is the same finding seen from the other side.
close_reason:
ANSWERED 2026-08-11 - they were a DOUBLE-COUNT, not a second lever. Built a prediction-centric decomposition (Charge/ChargeDiagnosis + ChargedLinks, which now owns the metric's repair chain so the decomposition reconciles to TP+FP by construction). Dense movie: TP 1132, FP 71, FN 51, split MISLINK 38 + TARGET_ORPHAN 33, with SOURCE_ENDS, SYNTHETIC and EXTRA_CHILD all exactly ZERO on every movie. All 38 mislink targets are UNANNOTATED and all 33 target-orphans stole a target we had ALREADY lost - so each is the second charge on a false negative we knew about. 71 FPs over 38 mislink EVENTS = 1.87 charges per event.
CONSEQUENCE THAT OUTLIVES THE BEAD: fixing one mislink pays ~2.9 points (-1 FN, -1.87 FP, +1 TP), so association was UNDERPRICED ~3x, and our noise floor is EXACTLY ONE MISLINK (0.0023 vs a ~0.002 floor) - a method needs ~5 repairs to be detectable, and 'a tie at the floor' now means 'fixed at most one'.
IT ALSO KILLED TWO OF MY OWN READINGS: sparse annotation does NOT manufacture phantom FPs (over-linking past a track end is UNCOUNTABLE, hence free, which predicts the overshoot we see - and the FP-vs-density gradient 0/0/11/71 makes FP structure a CROWDING phenomenon); and the boundary-cost sweep is NOT over-linking seen from the other side, since SOURCE_ENDS is zero structurally and a higher disappearance cost MANUFACTURES mislinks by forcing lower-affinity continuations.
A SPEC ERROR NEARLY BURIED IT: I asked for edges with BOTH endpoints matched, but EdgeCounts._countable is an OR - both-matched would have excluded TARGET_ORPHAN, the class that IS the finding. Read the metric's own predicate before commissioning a decomposition of it. Interpretation: interpretations/celltrack/2026-08-11_half-our-errors-were-the-same-error-twice.md

title: Ranker transfer gap that survives a healthy context: our detections are 2.3x denser per frame than its training data
description:
MEASURED (python -m celltrack.eval.ranker_distribution, movie 6bba_05db0fb1, thr 0.97, flow + boundary 3 + bidirectional, pass-1 context at the CONTROL cost).

With the pass-1 context healthy (see the two-pass bug), only 3 of the 22 features stay off-distribution, and two of them are the same fact:

  source_frame_count   ours 747.0 +- 52.4   trained 318.5 +- 219.3   z=1.95  spread=0.24
  target_frame_count   ours 745.7 +- 53.1   trained 318.5 +- 219.6   z=1.95  spread=0.24
  source_density_7um   ours   0.566 +- 0.73 trained   0.251 +- 0.53  z=0.60  spread=1.39
  target_density_7um   ours   0.565 +- 0.73 trained   0.264 +- 0.53  z=0.57  spread=1.38
  motion_gain_um       ours  -0.149 +- 0.78 trained  -0.442 +- 1.75  z=0.17  spread=0.44

frame_count is a RAW per-frame detection count fed straight into the net. At threshold 0.97 we emit 74347 nodes over ~100 frames = 747/frame; the ranker was fitted on datasets averaging 318/frame. The 7um density agrees (0.57 vs 0.26, i.e. ~2.2x), so this is one fact told twice: our detector runs at a much higher-recall operating point than the ranker's training pipeline did. The narrow spread (0.24) is partly a single-movie artefact — pooling movies would widen it — but the LOCATION shift is not.

motion_gain_um is the documented sourcing divergence, now measured: the mean is fine (z=0.17), the SPREAD is 2.3x too small. Our motion_dist_um itself is on-distribution (z=0.21), so the base quantity is right; the residual against raw distance is compressed because the prediction comes from the pass-1 parent rather than from a sequential relink's own just-matched predecessor.

Every geometric feature transfers cleanly (edge_d{z,y,x}, dist, xy, abs_z all z<=0.16, spreads 0.76-0.92), t_norm z=0.03, and — the piece the port had to invent for a global flow — candidate_count 4.35 vs 4.46 and candidate_rank_dist 2.67 vs 2.73. There is NO units error and NO wrong-graph error anywhere in the 22.

OPTIONS, in order of cost: (1) re-run the sweep after the two-pass fix and see whether the residual density shift costs anything at all; (2) retrain the 20 KB MLP on OUR 191-video split and OUR detections, which removes this shift by construction and is minutes of compute (already contemplated in spsl); (3) do nothing and price the ranker as the manifest's own 'constrained local tie-breaker', i.e. a small bonus, never a veto.
close_reason: MOOT 2026-08-11 - the ranker is closed on a stronger axis than density. Filed when the ported CC0 ranker read negative and the residual suspicion was that our detections are ~2.3x denser per frame than its training data (frame_count 747+-52 vs trained 318+-219). Since then the ranker has been refuted in THREE geometries with the pass-1 confound fixed: raw-distance flow (monotone negative, worst at their own 85/15), motion-predicted flow (still monotone negative), and the per-frame motion Hungarian where it IS positive (+0.0032) but unpurchasable because that linker's own ceiling is 0.045 below flow+fusion. Density might still explain WHY, but it cannot rescue the asset in any configuration we can run, so chasing the density gap buys nothing. Reopen only if the whole frontier pipeline is replicated end to end (the P0) and the ranker is being ablated INSIDE it.

title: [bug] Motion linker's tested affinity path is unreachable, and one reader set gates four knobs with different support
description:
TWO COUPLED DEFECTS, found while trying to test the frontier's actual bundle. I attempted the fix by hand, made it worse twice, and reverted — this needs doing carefully, not at the end of a long session.

(1) A TESTED CAPABILITY THE CONFIG CANNOT REACH. `MotionHungarianLinker` has carried `affinity` and `affinity_bonus` since it was written, documented in its docstring ("geometry and learned appearance jointly pick the successor") and exercised by a direct unit test (`a strong affinity for the farther in-gate target overrides the raw-nearest geometry pick`). But its builder row drops them:
    "motion": lambda config, spacing, affinity, parts: MotionHungarianLinker(
        spacing=spacing, tight_gate_um=config.tight_um, loose_gate_um=config.gate_um),
no `affinity=`, no `affinity_bonus=` — and `_AFFINITY_READERS` excludes "motion", so the config would refuse the knob anyway. Built, documented, tested, unreachable: the built-but-unwired anti-pattern the repo has a standing rule against.

(2) ONE READER SET GATES FOUR KNOBS WITH DIFFERENT SUPPORT. `_affinity_knobs_are_readable` checks `affinity_bonus`, `agreement_floor`, `mutual_bonus` and `ranker_bonus` against a single `_AFFINITY_READERS`. But support genuinely differs: motion can honour a bonus and (with a one-line change) a ranker, while it has no agreement gate and no mutual term at all. So the set either STRANDS the capability motion has, or — if widened — SILENTLY ACCEPTS knobs it cannot honour, which is exactly the failure the validator exists to prevent. My revert restores the first, safer failure mode.

THE FIX: per-knob reader sets (`_BONUS_READERS`/`_RANKER_READERS` = {assignment, flow, motion}; `_AGREEMENT_READERS`/`_MUTUAL_READERS` = {assignment, flow}), the builder row passing `affinity=affinity, affinity_bonus=config.effective_bonus, ranker=parts.ranker`, a `ranker` field on MotionHungarianLinker applying `RankerBonus.discount` after the affinity discount, and the refusal message naming the knob's OWN readers. NOTE the existing tests use "motion" as the canonical NON-READER exemplar in four refusal tests — those need a genuinely non-reading linker instead ("nn" is pure geometry), and that re-exemplification is most of the work.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: the ported CC0 ranker measures NEGATIVE in our pipeline at every weight (-0.0019 at b=2, -0.0043 at b=5, -0.0031 at b=10, -0.0229 at their 85/15 split). The frontier runs it inside a per-frame Hungarian over MOTION-PREDICTED distances, and the ranker consumes `motion_dist_um`/`motion_gain_um` AS FEATURES — so motion+ranker is the one pairing where its inputs are in-distribution, and it is precisely the cell this wiring gap blocks. We tested motion+transformer long ago (0.9004 vs assignment 0.9227, refuted) but never motion+ranker.
close_reason: FIXED 2026-08-11. Per-knob reader sets replace the single _AFFINITY_READERS (_BONUS/_RANKER = assignment|flow|motion, _AGREEMENT/_MUTUAL = assignment|flow), each knob refused against its OWN set with the message naming that set; the motion builder row now passes affinity, affinity_bonus and ranker; MotionHungarianLinker gained a ranker field applying RankerBonus.discount after the affinity discount. The four refusal tests were re-exemplified onto 'nn' (pure geometry, no affinity argument exists, so no wiring change could ever make a knob mean something there) with two of them looping (nn, motion) to keep proving motion still refuses agreement_floor and mutual_bonus - that pair IS the content of 'support differs per knob'. It unblocked the experiment it was filed for: motion+ranker measured 0.8964 against our 0.9353 control.

title: Wire AssociationRanker into the tracker + sweep the ranker/affinity evidence split
description:
celltrack/edges/association_ranker.py (CC0 22-feature re-ranker) and celltrack/linkers/ranker_bonus.py (RankerBonus, LinkerConfig.ranker_bonus, default OFF) are built and gated green, but nothing calls them yet.

Remaining:
1. tracker.py: the ranker needs a TWO-PASS run — link once with the shipped cost, hand that graph to AssociationRanker.affinities(spacing, detections, links, affinity, gate_um), then rebuild the linker with ranker= and link again. Gate the second pass on LinkerConfig.ranker_bonus being set (mirror needs_mutual).
2. Mount path: DataRoot.processed('biohub_cell_tracking')/'reference/association_ranker'.
3. Sweep the split at fixed P-budget: affinity_bonus + ranker_bonus = 2*gate_um = 20. The public 85/15 reads as ranker_bonus=17.0 / affinity_bonus=3.0; also probe 10/10 and 20/0 (transformer off). Their absolute weights (0.6375/0.1125 um) do NOT transfer — see the LinkerConfig.ranker_bonus comment.
4. Divergences to keep in mind when reading the result: their motion prediction comes from the relink's own sequential predecessor, ours from the context graph's parent; their candidate lists are per tight/relaxed pass, ours is the single gated list.
close_reason: Wired (tracker two-pass) + swept. REFUTED in all three geometries: raw-distance flow monotone-negative, motion-predicted flow still monotone-negative, positive only inside MotionHungarianLinker which is 0.045 below flow+fusion = unpurchasable. See ranker-sign-flips-with-geometry-2026-08-11.

title: [bug?] We blend two seeds' RAW logits with no scale alignment — is 0.8/0.2 a quality weight or a units fix?
description:
POSSIBLE BIAS IN THE SHIPPED PIPELINE. BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer blends the two seeds' RAW LOGITS with fixed weights (blended_edge_scoring.py:106, `weight * logits` summed, then softmax). Two independently trained networks have no reason to share a logit SCALE, so a fixed weight conflates "how much do I trust this seed" with "how large are its logits".

The reproducible 0.915 frontier config mean/std-ALIGNS the secondary seed's logits (ratio clamped to [0.5, 2]) before blending at 0.475 - i.e. near-even AFTER alignment. Ours blends 0.8/0.2 with no alignment.

TWO COMPETING EXPLANATIONS FOR OUR 0.8/0.2, and they make opposite predictions:
(a) OUR RECORDED BELIEF (memory detector-blend-self-balancing): seed1's edge transformer is genuinely better, so the tilt is quality-weighting - and it is EXPLAINED rather than a bug, since the DETECTOR blend is self-balancing at equal weights while only the EDGE blend is tilted.
(b) THE ALTERNATIVE this config exposes: the seeds' logit scales differ, and the swept 0.8/0.2 is a SCALE CORRECTION wearing quality-weighting's clothes. Under (b), aligning the moments should move the optimum toward ~0.5 AND score at least as well, because the tilt was spending trust to fix a units problem.

WHY (b) IS PLAUSIBLE HERE SPECIFICALLY: the blend happens in LOGIT space and is followed by a softmax over sources. A scale difference is therefore a TEMPERATURE difference - the sharper-scaled seed dominates the softmax regardless of its weight, and down-weighting it is a blunt way to compensate that also discards its ranking information. That is exactly the failure a moment alignment fixes without discarding anything.

TEST, cheap and decisive: (1) measure each seed's per-gap logit mean/std on a proxy movie - if they match within a few percent, (a) stands and this is closed; (2) if they differ, implement mean/std alignment of seed2 onto seed1 (ratio clamped [0.5, 2] as the frontier does) and re-sweep the blend weight on the clamped proxy. Prediction under (b): the optimum moves toward 0.5 and the peak is at least as high.

NOTE the detector blend is a separate question and is already measured self-balancing at equal weights - do not change it on this argument without its own measurement.
close_reason: MEASURED: std ratio 1.1215, mean gap -0.43 over 99 gaps. 12% spread cannot justify a 4x weight - NOT a units fix. Separately, edge_blend is inert (0.8/0.2 == 0.5/0.5 to 4dp), so the constant is fake rather than wrong; removal tracked on duw4.

title: Three disclosed 0.915 mechanisms we have never tried: edge-head log-pool TTA, seed moment-alignment, asymmetric boundary priors
description:
Three further mechanisms disclosed by the reproducible 0.915 config, none of which we have tried. All are cheap and testable on cached responses.

(1) EDGE-HEAD TTA WITH A LOGARITHMIC OPINION POOL. We run 4-fold flip TTA on the DETECTOR and none at all on the edge head. They run four views on the edge head and fuse them with per-view-per-source reliability weights w = 1/(1 + JS / median JS), into a LOGARITHMIC pool (a soft AND) rather than an arithmetic mean (a soft OR). Their own comment says this "avoids the graph inflation caused by a single optimistic spatial view" - i.e. the arithmetic mean lets any one view admit an edge, while the log pool requires agreement. NOTE this is NOT the refuted 8-fold detector TTA (fcd): different stage, different fusion rule. The pooled logits are re-centred onto the identity view's scale, so it drops in without re-tuning our threshold.

(2) MOMENT-ALIGNMENT OF THE SECOND SEED BEFORE BLENDING. They mean/std-align the secondary seed's logits (ratio clamped to [0.5, 2]) before a 0.475 blend. Our 0.8/0.2 blend does not align at all. Two independently trained networks have no reason to share a logit scale, so blending raw logits silently weights whichever net happens to be more confident - a real correction, and it may explain why our blend weight had to be tilted 0.8/0.2 rather than sitting near even.

(3) ASYMMETRIC BOUNDARY PRIORS + DENSITY-ADAPTIVE GAP GATE. They charge appearance 0.0 and disappearance 1.5 - births free, premature endings expensive - against our SYMMETRIC boundary cost of 3. That asymmetry has a mechanism our metric agrees with (a track that ends early loses its remaining edges; one that starts late costs only the edges before it). Note our own position-aware boundary prior measured -0.0027, but it made BOTH ends free by geometry rather than making them ASYMMETRIC by direction - a different claim. Their gap gate SHRINKS with local neighbour density (5.8um base, gain 0.040, cap 0.125um/step, 3 neighbours), the opposite of the 14um widening we refuted, applied conditionally.

ALSO BANKED, two of our refutations CONFIRMED by their config: DeepCenter veto is OFF and short-track rescue is OFF at 0.915. Do not spend effort mounting DeepCenter; our min_track_length 7 + rescue refutation agrees with the frontier.
notes:
TWO OF THE THREE ARE NOW MEASURED 2026-08-11, both dead; the third is still untried.
(1) FOUR-VIEW JS LOG-POOL EDGE TTA - REFUTED, and worse than flat: clamped 0.9304 against a 0.9353 control = -0.0049, over 2x the noise floor, at 3.75x the edge-head cost (affinity wall-clock 120.3s -> 450.8s). Not 'no gain at 4x cost' - WORSE at 4x cost. It reproduces identically with seed alignment on (arms agree to 4dp), so it is the pool and not an interaction, and it did NOT inflate the graph (node counts and the +0.0028 bonus unchanged - the pool sits on the edge head, downstream of detection). MECHANISM, predicted by the same day's shortcut diagnosis: the log pool is a soft AND across four flip views running ON TOP of bidirectional_edges, which is ALREADY a mutual-consistency AND (harmonic fuse of the two directions). Two ANDs stacked suppress TRUE-BUT-ONE-SIDED far successors - exactly the pairs measured at mean P 0.519 on genuinely-true >=5um steps while still ranking at 0.97 within-band. UNTESTED ARM THIS NAMES: log-pool with bidirectional_edges=FALSE, i.e. one AND instead of two.
(2) SEED MOMENT ALIGNMENT - INERT: 0.9352 vs 0.9353, a -0.0001 tie, matching the measured 12% scale mismatch (std ratio 1.1215). AND THE EXTRA PAIR KILLED ITS RATIONALE: the frontier aligns so the blend can move toward even (0.475), but edge_blend 0.5/0.5 scores 0.9353 - IDENTICAL to our shipped 0.8/0.2 - with or without alignment. The blend weight is INERT across that range, so alignment cannot enable a move that was never blocked. See the edge-blend-weight-is-inert memory: the sweep that set 0.8 read +0.0018 over 0.5, below our floor and non-monotone on both sides.
(3) ASYMMETRIC BOUNDARY PRIORS BY DIRECTION - STILL UNTRIED, and now BUILDABLE: FlowLinker's network already charges appearance and disappearance on SEPARATE arcs (source->in, out->sink) and _boundary_costs already returns two arrays; only the config collapsed them. LinkerConfig.appearance_cost (flow-only, None = today's symmetric charge, byte-identical) landed 2026-08-11 with the charges asserted at the graph-builder boundary. Do NOT retire this by association with the REFUTED geometric BoundaryPrior (-0.0027): that varies price by WHERE the boundary sits, this by WHICH DIRECTION it goes. Arms and the direction argument are in the separate appearance_cost bead - and note SOURCE_ENDS = 0 structurally kills my earlier 'cheaper deaths' reasoning, so the frontier's direction (free births, priced deaths) is the one to test.
Both mechanisms are now reachable from proxy_eval --set edge_options.*; neither earns a default-on.

title: [bug] Difficulty sampling collapses — needs a floor on the DISTRIBUTION, not on difficulty
description:
The difficulty sampler's optimistic-init half WORKS (coverage 1.000 by 1.5 epochs vs 0.777 for i.i.d. with replacement) but the difficulty-weighting half COLLAPSES: entropy fell 0.961 -> 0.235, the edge loss reached EXACTLY 0.0000, and held-out recall fell 0.672 -> 0.201 as the model memorised the shrinking set it was still being shown.

THE BUG IS AN ASSUMPTION IN THE ORIGINAL DESIGN, stated explicitly when it was filed: "staleness self-corrects, because an improved model makes an old estimate read too high, so that pair is redrawn and refreshed." That holds only while every pair keeps a NONZERO draw probability. It does not. A pair whose measured difficulty reaches 0 is never redrawn, so its estimate can never refresh, and the mass concentrates permanently on whatever is left - which a1v measured to be the crowd-ambiguous pairs that are NOT separable from these features at this resolution. The sampler therefore spends its whole budget on the unlearnable.

THE FIX IS A FLOOR ON THE SAMPLING DISTRIBUTION, NOT ON DIFFICULTY. A difficulty floor is a tuned constant and re-introduces the knob the design deliberately avoided. Instead mix the difficulty distribution with the uniform one - p = (1-a)*uniform + a*difficulty_normalised - or draw through a bounded transform, so no pair can fall out of rotation and stale estimates keep refreshing. `a` is still a parameter, so prefer a form where it is DERIVED (e.g. the mixture that keeps normalised entropy above a stated floor, adjusted online) over a swept constant. Whatever is chosen, the entropy series must stay the acceptance test.

KEEP AS IS: optimistic initialisation (measurably better coverage than random, no phase switch, no decay) and the normalised-entropy metric, which is the only reason this was diagnosable at all - it was added as a speculative collapse guard and caught the collapse on the first run that could exhibit one.

UNTIL THEN: --difficulty-sampling should stay off. The control (same from-scratch recipe, uniform sampling) is running to separate the sampler's damage from the from-scratch regime itself.
close_reason: FIXED 2026-08-11. p = (1-a)/n + a*(d/sum d) with a = 1/2, so no pair can be starved while difficulty RATIOS are preserved exactly (unlike a difficulty floor). The adaptive form I specified was implemented and REFUTED with measurement: entropy cannot be the controller because the failure is per-pair and entropy is an aggregate - one frozen pair among 18024 moves it by ~1e-4, so it only reacts after thousands have frozen, which is exactly the observed trace; and a=1/2 clears normalised entropy 0.5 for every n and every difficulty vector, making any entropy-targeting solve vacuous. a=1/2 is derived instead from maximum ignorance between two failure modes sharing no unit (i.i.d.-degeneracy vs freeze-out), with the consequence that the coldest pair refreshes about once per two epochs - the timescale the collapse ran on. The entropy floor is now a derived BOUND (worst case 1/2 + ln2/ln n, infimum 1/2, effective support >= sqrt(n)) and stays the acceptance test. Three tests that ASSERTED THE BUG were rewritten. Optimistic init untouched - it independently reached full coverage in about one pass vs i.i.d.'s ~2.8n draws. UNVERIFIED and filed separately: that mixing restores held-out quality past the 1.5-epoch peak.

title: Derive the mutual-agreement floor from true-edge agreement quantiles
description: AgreementGate (celltrack/linkers/agreement_gating.py) ships OFF because no principled floor is measured. Derive it: score fold-0 gaps bidirectionally, split fused probabilities by whether the pair is a TRUE edge in the annotation, and read the low quantile (~5th pct) of the true distribution vs the mislinked near-neighbour distribution the dense diagnosis isolates. Then A/B the floor under both the assignment and flow linkers (flow is where the fusion-as-score won, LB 0.895).
close_reason: MOOT 2026-08-11 - the gate it would calibrate is refuted in all four pairings. The mutual-agreement GATE measured: under the GLOBAL flow linker +0.0004 clamped (floors 0.05/0.15/0.30 = 0.9353/0.9357/0.9356 vs 0.9353 baseline); under the PER-FRAME assignment linker +0.0004 then NEGATIVE (0.15/0.30/0.50 = 0.9299/0.9286/0.9208 vs 0.9295). My pre-registered prediction that the per-frame linker would have room for a gate was REFUTED: the redundancy is with the ASSIGNMENT CONSTRAINT, which a per-frame matcher imposes locally just as the flow program imposes globally, not with globality. Deriving a floor for a mechanism that does not work at any floor would be tuning a null. The standing mechanism, now supported by four cells: mutual consistency helps when it CHANGES WHAT THE SOLVER OPTIMISES (as a score: +0.004 LB) and never when it merely RESTRICTS WHAT THE SOLVER MAY CHOOSE. Gate code kept - default off, byte-identical, composes with both linkers.

title: Likelihood-correct linker cost — removes affinity_bonus AND boundary_cost, both swept constants
description:
TWO TUNED CONSTANTS IN THE LINKER COST SHOULD BE ESTIMATED QUANTITIES, NOT SWEPT ONES.

Our flow/assignment cost is `distance - affinity_bonus * P`, plus a flat `boundary_cost` charged when a track starts or ends. That is dimensionally incoherent - a micrometre distance minus a dimensionless probability scaled by a hand-tuned constant - so the solver is minimising a heuristic score, NOT computing a MAP estimate. Two magic numbers live in it:
  affinity_bonus = 20 (argued as 2*gate, swept, with a broad optimum 20-30)
  boundary_cost  = 2-3 (swept; flat plateau 2-4 under the clamped proxy)

THE FORM IS ALREADY PRINCIPLED - WE JUST INSTANTIATED IT HEURISTICALLY. Min-cost flow over a node-split graph IS the classic MAP formulation for multi-object tracking (Zhang/Li/Nevatia 2008): with every arc costed as a NEGATIVE LOG-LIKELIHOOD, the min-cost flow is the maximum-likelihood set of trajectories. In that reading:
  transition = -log P(i->j)                    <- our calibrated affinity, and affinity_bonus DISAPPEARS
  entrance   = -log P(a track starts here)     <- boundary_cost DISAPPEARS
  exit       = -log P(a track ends here)
Both constants are replaced by quantities we can ESTIMATE FROM THE ANNOTATIONS, which record exactly where and when real tracks start and end.

AND THE ESTIMATED VERSION IS STRICTLY RICHER, not merely tidier. Our boundary cost is a single constant everywhere, but the true prior is not uniform: a cell appearing at the EDGE of the imaged volume, or in the first/last frame, is a plausible birth (it entered the field of view), while one appearing in the INTERIOR mid-movie is almost certainly a broken track or an artefact. We charge both the same. Note this subsumes a thing we already tested and measured NEUTRAL: the boundary-truncated-track RESCUE (LB 0.891 = its base) is a crude post-hoc version of exactly this - it exempts clip-boundary tracks AFTER linking instead of telling the solver they are cheap DURING it. Doing it in the cost lets the solver trade it off against everything else rather than us patching its output.

IMPLEMENT: estimate P(birth | position, time) and P(death | position, time) from the annotated track starts/ends (at minimum: interior vs volume-boundary, and first/last frame vs mid-movie), calibrate the affinity so -log P is on the same scale, and drop both constants.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING BEYOND ELEGANCE: this is the class of change that TRANSFERS. Every leaderboard gain this campaign has produced came from altering HOW THE LINKER DECIDES (greedy -> global +0.005; global + symmetric affinity +0.003), while every recall-side tweak died. A likelihood-correct cost is a decision-rule change of exactly that kind, and it removes two swept constants rather than adding any.

RISK: calibration. `-log P` assumes the affinity is a probability, and ours is a softmax over sources whose sharpness was never calibrated - a badly calibrated P makes the log blow up on confident-wrong edges. Check calibration (reliability curve on annotated edges) BEFORE trusting the log form, and keep the heuristic cost available as the shipped default until the likelihood version beats it on the clamped proxy.
notes:
CONSTANT AUDIT — CORRECTED 2026-08-11 (the earlier note on this bead called edge_blend a proven-fake constant; that was withdrawn and is now re-measured).

The claim "0.8/0.2 and 0.5/0.5 are identical, so the constant is fake" was produced through a BROKEN KNOB:
CellTracker.with_config carried the scorer's options and fusion flag but not its WEIGHTS, so every arm of that
sweep scored the mount's original mix. Two identical numbers were the signature of the bug. Fixed
(BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer.with_weights) and re-measured, four movies:

  SHIPPED point (thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional): 0.8/0.2 = 0.9380 | 0.6/0.4 = 0.9380 |
                                                            0.5/0.5 = 0.9380 | 1.0/0.0 = 0.9336
  PER-FRAME point (boundary 0):                             0.8/0.2 = 0.9334 | 0.5/0.5 = 0.9329 |
                                                            1.0/0.0 = 0.9312

SO: the MIX RATIO sits on a broad plateau (0.5-0.8 identical) under the shipped consumer and varies slightly
under the per-frame one; the SECOND SEED is load-bearing either way (-0.0044 to remove it). edge_blend is
therefore a REAL knob on a plateau, not a fake constant — it needs no defence, but it is not evidence of
anything being removable, and 0.8/0.2 stays shipped because it is what the leaderboard scored 0.895 with.

WHAT THIS BEAD SHOULD STILL REMOVE, unchanged: affinity_bonus and boundary_cost, if a likelihood-correct cost
can price them. The argued-vs-swept test in the earlier note stands; only the edge_blend example was wrong.

THE GATE ON THE COST REWRITE ITSELF also stands and is the hard part: -log P blows up exactly where we fail.
On the 38 dense mislinks the affinity is 97.4% inverted with mean P_true 0.079 vs P_chosen 0.589, so a log cost
takes a SMALL penalty on the confidently-wrong edge and a LARGE one on the true edge — worse than the current
linear cost. Recalibrate on REAL DETECTIONS before the log form is safe.

title: Re-rank every 'proxy-blind' recall knob under the clamped score — smooth and min_track have LB ground truth
description:
The clamped proxy reproduced the leaderboard's THRESHOLD ordering exactly (0.97 > 0.98 > 0.99 > 0.995, all four, where the faithful proxy was inverted).
