Every other recall-side knob this campaign wrote off as "proxy-blind" or "proxy-anti-informative" was dismissed using the BIASED instrument, so each deserves re-ranking under the clamped score - and two of them have LEADERBOARD GROUND TRUTH already paid for, which makes them free validation points for the instrument itself.

RE-RANK THESE, each against its known LB answer:
1. SMOOTH_STRENGTH. Faithful proxy strongly preferred 0.3 (sweep 0.0/0.3/0.4/0.8/1.0 = 0.9417/0.9426/0.9426/0.9344/0.9340, and the dense movie's raw jaccard rose 0.892 -> 0.906 at 0.3). The LB said the opposite: v13 smooth0.8 = 0.892 vs v14 smooth0.3 = 0.889. We shipped 0.3, regressed, and reverted. PREDICTION IF THE INSTRUMENT IS SOUND: clamped should rank 0.8 at or above 0.3. Note the mechanism differs from threshold's - smoothing moves node POSITIONS rather than counts, so the node-count factor may not be the confound here and clamped may NOT fix it. That makes this the sharper test of the two.
2. MIN_TRACK_LENGTH. Faithful proxy was monotone-increasing in length (favouring aggressive cuts); the LB preferred 6 over 7 (0.892 vs 0.891 with rescue). Dropping short components REMOVES nodes, so the bonus should be implicated exactly as it is for threshold. PREDICTION: clamped should flatten or invert the monotone preference toward 6.
3. NMS window / peak radius, and the short-track RESCUE (proxy read -0.0005, "proxy-anti-informative" - re-read it clamped).

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the campaign's standing conclusion is that recall-side gains never transfer and only decision-rule changes do. That law was derived entirely from the biased instrument. If clamped re-ranking predicts the LB on smooth and min_track as it did on threshold, the law needs rewriting: it was not "recall-side changes do not transfer", it was "our proxy could not measure them". That would re-open every recall lever previously closed - a large set - and turn a 5-per-day leaderboard resource into local sweeps.

HONEST BOUND: threshold validation was RANK-only on four points of ONE axis (clamped 0.9295 vs LB 0.892 differ in level). Do not treat the clamped score as an LB predictor; treat it as an ordering instrument, and re-verify per axis before trusting it on a knob of a different kind. Smooth is the case most likely to break it, which is why it should be run first.
close_reason: ANSWERED 2026-08-10, with the scope it turned out to have. THRESHOLD: clamped reproduces the LB order EXACTLY (0.97 > 0.98 > 0.99 > 0.995 vs LB 0.892/0.891/0.887/0.880) where faithful is inverted and picks the config that lost 0.005 - this OVERTURNS 'threshold is irreducibly LB-only'. SMOOTH: predicted null and confirmed null - the bonus is IDENTICAL (+0.0039) at 0.3 and 0.8 because smoothing moves POSITIONS at constant count, so the ordering cannot change and the clamped proxy still disagrees with the LB. MIN_TRACK: predicted a flip toward 6, got only a halving (faithful favours 7 by +0.0043, clamped by +0.0022) - partial, and the LB truth there is 0.892 vs 0.891, at LB resolution. SCOPE ESTABLISHED: the clamp corrects COUNT-changing knobs and does nothing for POSITION-moving ones. Ask which kind a knob is before trusting a local sweep on it.

title: [bug] Checkpoint selection rewards UNDER-detection — the one component proven to anti-transfer
description:
THE BIAS. ModelEvaluator._scored returns EvalResult(SplitScore.of(metrics).score, recall, ratio) and the joint trainer SELECTS its best checkpoint on that score. That score is the competition metric, adjusted = jaccard * (1 - 0.1 * ratio), which pays a BONUS for undershooting the estimated node count. So a checkpoint that simply DETECTS FEWER CELLS can win selection.

THIS IS THE ONE COMPONENT KNOWN TO ANTI-TRANSFER. Threshold 0.995 vs 0.99 was a matched A/B differing only in trimming: proxy +0.006, LB -0.007. Mechanism (threshold-recall-mechanism-CLOSED): our proxy's annotations are SPARSE, so trimmed true cells are mostly unannotated locally and cost no jaccard while paying the bonus; the hidden set annotates the same movies DENSELY, so those same trimmed cells ARE annotated there and cost real jaccard. The bonus is therefore systematically over-rewarded on our proxy relative to the leaderboard.

OBSERVED TODAY, in the contrastive run. Node recall fell 0.966 -> 0.867 while the adjusted proxy only fell 0.8414 -> 0.7292, because ratio went to -0.22 and the bonus paid for the under-detection. The score understated a tenth of the detector's recall. No checkpoint was wrongly saved in THAT run (nothing beat the init), but the same masking applies to every future run that touches detection - which now includes the kinematics and contrastive-placement arms.

FIX - CLAMP THE REWARD, DO NOT REMOVE THE METRIC. Keep the reported score faithful; add a SELECTION score whose count factor is min(1.0, 1 - 0.1*ratio): overshooting is still penalised exactly as the competition penalises it, undershooting simply earns nothing. That removes the farming incentive while leaving the metric's shape and the honest number intact. It is not a tuned knob - 1.0 is the neutral point of the factor, i.e. "no adjustment", so nothing is introduced that has to be swept.

SHAPE: name the clamped variant beside its faithful sibling on VideoMetrics (form-named method, one home), have SplitScore expose both, and carry both on EvalResult so logs can show the honest score AND what selection used. The trainer selects on the clamped one. Do NOT add a boolean flag to the existing method (FBT / keyword-only-bools rule, and a flag would let a caller silently pick the farming variant).

VALIDATION, cheap and available: re-rank the checkpoints we already have (joint_warm_cos3k, joint_seed2_cos3k, joint_nce_15ep, and the published packs) under both scores. If the ranking is identical the bias has not bitten yet and the change is insurance; if it differs, we have been selecting on the wrong axis and the difference is measurable immediately.
close_reason: FIXED + VALIDATED 2026-08-10. VideoMetrics.clamped_edge_jaccard uses min(1.0, 1-0.1*ratio): over-detection penalised exactly as the competition penalises it, under-detection earns nothing. 1.0 is the factor's neutral point so no tunable constant enters; the faithful metric is untouched and pinned by a test. Both trainers select and early-stop on the clamped score and log both. CAUGHT FIRING LIVE, which is why this was not insurance: a run saved a checkpoint whose recall had fallen 0.966->0.938, scored as an improvement purely by the bonus; restarted on the fixed selector, the same window was correctly REJECTED. Concrete inversion: candidate A (jaccard 0.88, ratio 0.00) = 0.8800 vs candidate B (jaccard 0.86, ratio -0.30) = 0.8858 faithful / 0.8600 clamped - the faithful metric prefers the model that found 30% fewer cells. HONEST FOLLOW-UP: the fix did NOT produce a better model held out (cos3k 0.9168 clamped vs short+masked 0.9142) - the bias was a risk that had not materialised in the run that made our best model.

title: Kinematics: the model has pairwise displacement but NO history — feed prior velocity, don't re-add a motion cost
description:
AUDIT FIRST - WE ALREADY HAVE MOTION IN TWO PLACES, AND THE MODEL IS NOT GEOMETRY-BLIND.

(1) HAND-CODED, IN THE LINKER, REFUTED. MotionHungarianLinker predicts each cell's successor from a DAMPED constant-velocity estimate (half a step ahead, because full extrapolation overshoots), propagating velocity along its own links, two-pass tight/loose gating. Measured on the dense movie it LOSES: 0.82-0.84 vs the plain assignment linker's 0.868. Velocity as a cost term HURTS in crowding. Also present: gap_closer's motion-synthetic insertion, LinefitSmoother's line fit, topology_repair.

(2) ALREADY IN THE MODEL - PAIRWISE DISPLACEMENT. external simple_node_transformer.py's pair head computes
      rel = (coords_t.unsqueeze(2) - coords_t1.unsqueeze(1)) / 100.0
      logits = pair_mlp(cat([q_expanded, k_expanded, rel], dim=-1))
so the RELATIVE DISPLACEMENT of every candidate pair is ALREADY an input to the edge head. Adding "displacement features" would be duplicating what exists. (Note the /100.0 - an undocumented scale constant, worth a look under the no-magic-numbers rule.)

THE ACTUAL GAP IS HISTORY, NOT GEOMETRY. The model sees the candidate pair's displacement (t -> t+1) but never the cell's PRIOR displacement (t-1 -> t). Velocity requires the previous step. Without it the model cannot ask the question that disambiguates our documented failure - a fast mover whose true successor lands FAR while a slower neighbour sits NEAR: "is this candidate consistent with where this cell was already heading?" Distance alone cannot separate those two; distance PLUS prior heading can.

WHY THE OLD REFUTATION DOES NOT COVER THIS. MotionHungarianLinker HAD history and spent it as a fixed analytic cost. Our corrective research (2026-08-10) independently supports that failing: OC-SORT notes that at high frame rate displacement noise is comparable to true displacement (our regime - median step 1.7um), and LEARNED motion beats constant-velocity Kalman only in the dense/non-linear case (DanceTrack 52.1 vs 47.8 HOTA; the MOT17 advantage vanishes). So: hand-coded velocity refuted twice over, LEARNED velocity never tried.

THE CHICKEN-AND-EGG, AND THE THREE WAYS ROUND IT. Prior displacement needs prior LINKS, and links need affinities.
  (a) TWO-PASS: link once without velocity, derive each node's incoming displacement from that result, re-score with it, re-link. Cheap, uses what we have, but conditions on hard first-pass decisions (and inherits their mistakes exactly where they are worst - crowding).
  (b) SOFT/EXPECTED displacement: use the affinity-weighted mean incoming displacement from the previous gap rather than a hard link. Differentiable, no hard decision, available at train time, degrades gracefully when the previous gap is ambiguous. Preferred.
  (c) T=3 WINDOW WITH TEMPORAL POSITIONAL ENCODING: give the backbone (t-1, t, t+1) so velocity is learnable in the FEATURES rather than hand-fed. This subsumes (a)/(b) and matches Trackastra's verified mechanism (RoPE carrying relative spatial AND temporal offsets in every attention layer). BLOCKED until the backbone can represent order at all - our _TemporalAttention has no positional encoding and is permutation-invariant over time.

PLAN, cheapest falsifier first: implement (b) as an extra per-source node feature (3 numbers: the expected incoming displacement, in the same um space as rel), train, and read the dense mislink inversion rate - the metric that says whether the affinity now ranks the true far successor above the near decoy. If it moves, (c) is justified as the general version. If it does not, the fast-mover story is wrong and that is worth knowing before building RoPE.

HONEST RISK: our corrective research found NO source quantifying motion-feature contribution in 3D developmental light-sheet crowding - every verified motion ablation is 2D pedestrian/dance/CTC-2D. This is the best-evidenced lever we have, not a proven one.
notes: BUILT, RUN, NULL 2026-08-11 - and the null may be untestable in this regime rather than a refutation. PriorVelocity.expected_incoming (soft, affinity-weighted, unnormalised so an ambiguous previous gap SHRINKS the velocity rather than guessing a direction) is wired through training AND inference, with train/inference agreement pinned by exact torch.equal and feature use detected from proj.in_features rather than a flag. HELD OUT on the test four: velocity 0.9143 clamped vs its own control 0.9142 = +0.0001, identical. On validation it led by +0.0029 but the curve swung 0.8332 -> 0.8627 between ADJACENT windows, so that edge was noise. THE CAVEAT THAT MAY INVALIDATE THE TEST: the velocity columns are ZERO-INITIALISED (that is what preserves the warm start bitwise), so the model starts with the feature contributing nothing and must LEARN to use it - inside a recipe that peaks at 250-750 steps and degrades after. We may be asking a warm-started model to learn a brand-new input in a window shorter than it takes to learn one. If revisited: from-scratch with the feature present from step 0, or a long run with detection frozen so only the head learns to consume it. Cost measured: 2.5x per step (extra frame decode is IO-bound), worse than the +33% estimate.

title: Config should speak in EPOCHS — steps/patience units hid that every joint run was <1 epoch
description:
JointTrainConfig expresses steps, eval_every and patience in RAW STEPS and EVAL WINDOWS. Nothing in the config knows what an EPOCH is, and that hid a real error: 18024 GT pairs at one pair per step means one epoch = ~18000 steps, so every joint run this campaign has done was a FRACTION of one epoch (3000 steps = 17%), while the published pack trained 50 epochs. I read "3000 steps" as a training run and it was a sixth of a first pass.

The same units gap made "patience 5" ambiguous. It counts EVAL WINDOWS, so its meaning silently depends on eval_every - patience 5 at eval_every 500 is 2500 steps (14% of an epoch), and at eval_every 9000 it is 5 epochs. Same number, two orders of magnitude apart. The user asked for "patience 5 epochs", which the config cannot currently express.

CHANGE: make the epoch the unit the config speaks in. The trainer already knows the pair count (it logs "18024 train pairs"), so it can derive steps_per_epoch itself - nothing needs to be supplied.
  epochs: float          -> steps = round(epochs * steps_per_epoch)
  evals_per_epoch: int   -> eval_every = steps_per_epoch // evals_per_epoch
  patience_epochs: float -> patience windows = round(patience_epochs * evals_per_epoch)
Raw steps/eval_every/patience stay available for the short probe runs that genuinely think in steps, but the epoch fields should be what the CLI offers by default, and the run log should state BOTH ("epoch 3.5/15, step 63000") so a curve is never again read at the wrong scale.

SELF-BALANCING ANGLE (repo directive: remove parameters that should be derivable): steps_per_epoch is DERIVED, never configured - it is a property of the dataset, and any hand-set value would be a magic number that silently rots when the split changes. Likewise cosine T_max should follow from epochs rather than being passed separately.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: every early-stop decision, every "it plateaued" claim, and the cosine schedule's shape all depend on this scale. Reading a dip at step 1000 as convergence (which happened twice) is a units error as much as a patience error.
close_reason: DONE 2026-08-10. --epochs / --evals-per-epoch / --patience-epochs resolve against steps_per_epoch DERIVED from the pair count the trainer already logs (never a field or constant - a hand-set value rots when the split changes). Resolution happens as the first statement of train(), the earliest point the corpus exists, so the cosine horizon, window bound, EarlyStop, ETA and tracked params all read resolved values; a test pins T_max against the resolved count. Raw --steps/--eval-every/--patience still work for probes, an epoch field wins over its raw twin and the run LOGS which value it overrode. Window line prints both scales. En route: --eval-every had never been exposed at all, which is WHY patience was meaningless (it counts eval windows). CAVEAT worth carrying: the units finding was real but the inference I drew from it - that we had never trained properly and needed full epochs - was REFUTED held out; the optimum is ~250 steps.

title: Difficulty-weighted pair sampling — optimistic init unifies visibility and difficulty
description:
USER'S IDEA (their own prior scheme, adapted): give each training sample a VISIBILITY and a DIFFICULTY. Unseen samples get used first; once all are seen, difficult ones get used more.

CORRECTION TO MY EARLIER FRAMING: I claimed 3000 steps over 18024 pairs = "17% of an epoch" and treated that as a defect. It is not, by itself - a random subset per epoch is fine. What matters is COVERAGE plus HARD-EXAMPLE EMPHASIS, which is exactly what this scheme buys.

DESIGN - THE TWO METRICS COLLAPSE INTO ONE VIA OPTIMISTIC INITIALISATION. Do not implement visibility and difficulty as separate fields with a phase switch ("have all been seen yet?"). Initialise difficulty at its MAXIMUM (1.0) and an unseen sample automatically outranks every seen one; on its first visit the value drops to what was measured. One array, one rule, no branch, no phase flag:
  difficulty[i] = 1.0 at init      -> unseen sorts first for free
  sample i with probability proportional to difficulty[i]
  update difficulty[i] on every visit
STALENESS IS ALSO SELF-CORRECTING: as the model improves, an old estimate reads too HIGH, so that sample is resampled and refreshed. No decay constant, no recency window - both would be knobs this design does not need (repo directive: remove parameters that should be self-balancing).

DIFFICULTY MUST NOT BE RAW LOSS. Our annotations are ~1-2% dense, so per-pair loss scales with HOW MANY annotated edges the pair happens to carry, not with how hard it is - loss-weighted sampling would chase label count and annotation noise. Use instead the fraction of annotated sources whose TRUE successor is not ranked top-1 by the edge logits: bounded [0,1], independent of edge count, and it IS the measured defect this campaign is chasing (the dense mislinks are 100% affinity-inverted, P_true 0.134 vs P_chosen 0.686). It is free - the edge logits are already computed in the step.

COST: one float array of 18024 entries updated on a pair already forwarded. No extra passes, no extra memory of consequence.

WHY IT SHOULD HELP HERE SPECIFICALLY: the association head is the undertrained half AND the one carrying the score gap, while the detector is warm-started at recall 0.992 and needs little. Uniform pair sampling spends the same budget on both. Difficulty-weighted sampling spends it where the model is wrong, which is the crowded pairs - the exact population the mislinks live in.

RISK TO WATCH: difficulty-weighted sampling can over-concentrate on genuinely UNLEARNABLE pairs (crowd-ambiguous cases at the resolution wall, which a1v measured as not separable from the features). If the sampler collapses onto a small hard core the model cannot fit, effective data diversity drops. The optimistic-init + refresh dynamic partly guards this (a sample the model cannot improve keeps its high score but so do others), but the honest check is to log the sampling distribution's entropy and compare a run against uniform.

PRIOR ART CONSULTED (user's own private work repo D:/work/ai, for inspiration only, NOT copied): data/processed/data_selection/dataset_sampler.py is a composable filter -> diversify -> select pipeline with preset modes - a static SUBSET-SELECTION pattern, not per-step online sampling; data/analysis/learnability/dataset_learnability.py measures learnability per DATASET by retraining on each in turn - difficulty as an offline measured property. Neither is the online per-sample scheme; the composable-pipeline shape is the transferable idea.
notes:
BUILT 2026-08-10, NOT YET RUN. DifficultySampler ships with optimistic init (1.0 = unseen outranks every seen pair, no separate visibility field and no phase switch), difficulty = fraction of annotated sources whose true successor is not ranked top-1 (NOT loss - at 1-2% density a per-pair loss chases label count), and normalised sampling entropy logged as the collapse guard. No decay, no recency window, no temperature, no floor: the all-zero case falls back to uniform, which is the LIMIT of the proportional rule rather than an epsilon.
THE PROBLEM IT SOLVES IS BIGGER THAN ASSUMED: the existing sampler draws i.i.d. WITH REPLACEMENT over 18024 pairs, so expected coverage after a nominal epoch is 1-e^-1 = 63% and ~37% of pairs are never seen while others are drawn three or four times. Coverage was a lottery.
RISK CHECKED AND CLEARED: a pair with no annotated source rows would report difficulty None forever and sit at optimistic 1.0 as a permanent max-weight attractor. Measured over 40 train videos / 3678 pairs: ZERO all-zero edge matrices (and 99.0% of annotated source rows carry a link). Structurally reachable, does not occur here.
DEFERRED, HONESTLY: the training optimum turned out to be ~250 steps, so a sampler that improves COVERAGE over an epoch has little room to matter at that horizon. It should be tested on a from-scratch or long run, not on a warm-start fine-tune.
close_reason: Built + run. Unmixed sampler COLLAPSED (entropy 0.961->0.235, recall 0.672->0.201); fixed with a uniform mixture a=1/2 on the distribution. Follow-up verification is vjm0.

title: [design] One synthesized pipeline: contrastive embedding + ordered time + global solver
description:
GOAL: one coherent pipeline trained end to end with every decision this campaign has MEASURED, plus the new ideas the measurements point at - not an ensemble, not a pile of options.

THE SYNERGY THAT MAKES IT ONE DESIGN. Today's LB win (0.895) came from a GLOBAL solver wanting a SYMMETRIC affinity. Our model emits ASYMMETRIC logits that we softmax over sources, so we manufacture symmetry by running the model twice and fusing (2x cost, and the backbone cannot even distinguish the frames). A CONTRASTIVE EMBEDDING produces a symmetric calibrated similarity NATIVELY - cosine similarity is symmetric. So the association model the accuracy gap demands is exactly the affinity form our best consumer wants. Two independent findings converge on one architecture.

DECISIONS, each with its evidence:
- BACKBONE: TemporalUNet3D at T=2 PLUS temporal positional encoding (NEW). It currently has none, so its attention is permutation-invariant and cannot represent order - no velocity, which is what separates a fast mover's far-true successor from a near-false one. Also the precondition for T>2 meaning anything.
- LOSSES (decoupled, summed, logged separately - the structure already exists): BalancedBCE on both frames (detection) + SoftmaxFocalBCE (association ranking) + InfoNCE on APPEARANCE channels only (NEW - discrimination as an explicit objective; contrast on the full vector would be satisfiable via position, the exact failure being fixed) + optionally hard negatives, whose zni collapse mechanism required a FROZEN backbone and may not apply now.
- TRAINING: warm-start at lr 1e-5 (1e-4 walks off a converged optimum - measured), cosine over a long horizon (the curve dips and recovers, so patience must survive a dip), 191 videos, selection through the SHIPPED pipeline on the 4 DENSE held-out movies. Never fold-0 (leaked, and it misranks 0.837 vs 0.893 for the same weights).
- INFERENCE: DUPLICATED-frame detection read-out (measured 0.9334 vs 0.9280 for real pairs - a moved cell's features leak into voxels where it is not yet), fp16 not bf16 (inference wants mantissa, not gradient range; and fp16 is Turing's only fast half), multi-GPU dispatch (score-neutral, proven on the hidden set).
- LINKING: GLOBAL flow solver at boundary cost 1-3 (broad plateau: 0 -> 0.9334, 1 -> 0.9355, 3 -> 0.9353) with a symmetric affinity. +0.004 on the LB.
- POST: min_track_length 6 (min7+rescue measured 0.891 vs 0.892), smooth 0.8 (LB-arbitrated over the proxy's 0.3), density gap bridge.

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN ASSEMBLING WINNERS - three knobs stop being independent:
1. contrastive training -> symmetric similarity -> what the global solver wants, natively, without the 2x fusion hack;
2. positional encoding -> order -> velocity -> the information an unordered pair provably lacks (bidirectional fusion failed BECAUSE the answer is not in the pair);
3. discriminative features -> mutual agreement becomes MEANINGFUL, where today "both directions agree" is weak evidence precisely because the features cannot tell the cells apart.

SEQUENCING (cheapest falsifier first, per the campaign's own rule): (a) contrastive term into the existing joint trainer, gated on whether it separates the 35 known inverted mislinks the current features cannot; (b) hard negatives unfrozen; (c) temporal positional encoding, which requires a retrain and only then makes T>2 worth trying; (d) drop the bidirectional fusion hack once the embedding is natively symmetric - it exists only to manufacture what the embedding would give for free.

HONEST RISK: this forfeits the pretrained head start. Our best from-scratch detector sits ~0.04 below the shipped pipeline - but it was trained under the OLD broken harness (leaked fold-0 selection with a motion linker, no LB-aligned selector, no schedule, 158 videos). We have never trained from scratch with a working harness, so that number is not evidence about this design.
notes:
RESEARCH-BACKED UPGRADES (re-read research/deep_dives/2026-08-03_dense-association-training.md, status "settled", 12 citations). Our own prior research already prescribed most of this design, and two items sharpen it:

(1) BIDIRECTIONAL CONSISTENCY BELONGS IN TRAINING, NOT INFERENCE. The doc says verbatim: "train the association net with both directions, not just forward-only. Cost is ~2x compute, benefit is robustness to crowding." We implemented it as an INFERENCE-TIME fusion of a forward-only-trained model - asking for mutual consistency the model was never trained to have, then averaging two passes of a backbone that cannot even distinguish the frames. That is a materially weaker thing, and it explains why the fusion measured -0.0027 alone. ADD a consistency loss term (forward and reverse predictions must agree) and DROP the 2x inference fusion once the model is natively consistent - it exists only to manufacture what training would give for free.

(2) MOTION/VELOCITY IS LISTED SOTA AND WE CANNOT REPRESENT IT. The doc: "cells move with consistent velocity; motion model eliminates kinematically-implausible links" - which is exactly our documented failure (a fast mover whose true successor lands FAR while a slower neighbour sits closer). Our backbone attention has NO positional encoding over time, so it cannot infer velocity at all. Temporal positional encoding therefore stops being speculative: it is the ENABLER for the motion cue the research says matters most in crowding, and the precondition for T>2 meaning anything.

ALSO CONFIRMED BY THE RESEARCH, already in the design: hard-negative mining ("the core technique for crowding" - our zni failed only because the backbone was FROZEN); softmax-over-sources parental constraint (we have it, and it is precisely the asymmetry that made the inference-time fusion hurt the per-frame linker); triplet/metric learning for identity margins (the InfoNCE term just built); appearance embeddings beyond distance ("two neighbouring cells have different morphology - embeddings separate even when locations are close"), which is our measured 22.9% defect stated from the other side.

BENCHMARK CONTEXT from the same doc: linking-before-segmentation dominates CTC; transformer association nets (Trackastra, Cell-TRACTR) rank top; integer programming is theoretically optimal but costly and learned association nets match or exceed it in practice - consistent with our own finding that the GLOBAL solver helped (+0.004) but the signal is where the remaining gap lives.

title: Consumer-side follow-ups: two-term cost, agreement gate, flow boundary sweep
description:
Today's LB win (0.895) came from the CONSUMER side - same weights, same probabilities, a global solver plus a symmetric affinity. That side is barely sampled. Two cheap follow-ups, both proxy-testable in minutes with no training.

(1) TWO-TERM COST. Directional P (softmax over sources) says WHO PREFERS WHOM; harmonic P says WHO AGREES. We currently discard one to use the other. Try cost = distance - a*P_forward - b*P_harmonic so the solver gets preference AND agreement as separate evidence. The forward term restores the competitive dilution that the assignment cost fed on (two sources contending for a target dilute each other, so ambiguity reaches the solver), which pure harmonic destroys.

(2) AGREEMENT AS A GATE (the sharper hypothesis). Keep directional P in the cost, but ADMIT an edge only where harmonic agreement clears a floor. Mutual consistency becomes a filter rather than a score. This targets the documented failure directly: our dense mislinks are 100% affinity-inverted - a wrong NEAR neighbour that wins forward, and which typically fails mutual agreement because that near cell has its own better parent. A gate removes exactly those candidates without blunting the directional sharpness everywhere else.

(3) FLOW BOUNDARY SWEEP. FlowLinker's boundary cost is sampled only at 0 (where it provably reduces to AssignmentLinker edge-for-edge) and 3 (its measured peak, and the winning submission). Sweep 1/2/3/4/6 - the optimum was never located, only bracketed, and it is now a load-bearing parameter of our best configuration.

WHY THIS AXIS DESERVES THE ATTENTION: the transfer law says DECISION-RULE changes transfer even when the proxy cannot resolve them (greedy->global +0.005 on the LB; today flow+fusion read +0.0019 on the proxy - under its noise floor - and transferred as +0.004), while every recall-side proxy gain has died. These are all decision-rule changes.

title: Contrastive term in the joint loss — make the shared representation discriminative
description:
THE MEASURED DEFICIENCY: on the dense mislinks, the backbone features rank the true successor above the wrong NEAR neighbour only 22.9% of the time, and a bilinear probe on them generalises at 0.574 (chance). Detection trains the shared representation toward INVARIANCE (every cell should look like a cell); association needs DISCRIMINATION (this cell must differ from the one 3um away). Nothing in the current objective asks for discrimination - the edge loss only asks the HEAD to rank pairs, given whatever features it is handed.

WHY IT IS NOW CHEAP (this was mis-scoped earlier as an architecture rewrite): it is a LOSS TERM, not a new model.
- The three failed retrains (lna x2, zni) all FROZE the backbone, so the features could not become discriminative - only the head could re-weight what was already there.
- Joint training unfreezes them and is the one thing that worked (+0.0075 held out, via association).
- celltrack/models/joint_model.py ALREADY computes feat_source and feat_target (lines 83-84); they are simply not returned. Expose them and the loss has its inputs.
- The losses are already decoupled, form-named and summed in the trainer with separate logging (BalancedBCE, SoftmaxFocalBCE) - a third term is the shape the code was built for.

DESIGN: an InfoNCE / NT-Xent term over each source's candidate targets. For source i with true successor j+, loss = -log( exp(sim(i,j+)/T) / sum_j exp(sim(i,j)/T) ), summed over sources that HAVE an annotated successor, with the GT edge matrix supplying positives. Cosine similarity, temperature T as the one knob.

CRITICAL DETAIL - CONTRAST ON APPEARANCE ONLY. node_features returns concat(sampled UNet features, sinusoidal position embedding). Contrasting the FULL vector lets the objective be satisfied through POSITION - nearby cells get similar embeddings - which is exactly the wrong lesson and precisely the failure being fixed. Slice the appearance channels (the first out_channels dims) before computing similarity.

SECOND, EQUALLY CHEAP RETRY that the same insight unlocks: zni's HARD-NEGATIVE MINING with the backbone UNFROZEN. It failed before because deflating a wrong-near-neighbour's probability dragged the true edge down with it (the head could only move a shared fixed representation, so the whole softmax column flattened: correct edges 1122 -> 948). With features free to move, that specific mechanism may not apply. Same mining code, same data, one flag different.

PRE-GATE before either full run: does the contrastive objective separate the 35 known inverted mislinks on the dense movie that the current features cannot? Same cheap-gate discipline that killed synthetic-pretrain in an hour instead of a week.
notes:
BUILT + MEASURED 2026-08-10, verdict is PLACEMENT not patience. InfoNCE lands as a third form-named loss contrasting APPEARANCE CHANNELS ONLY (contrasting the full vector is satisfiable through position - the exact failure being fixed); the layout was verified empirically and pinned by a regression test. Default weight 0.0, computed anyway as a free diagnostic.
MEASURED at weight 0.1 over a FULL epoch: proxy 0.8414 -> 0.7430 (half epoch) -> 0.7292, node recall 0.966 -> 0.887 -> 0.867. The deciding evidence is that the contrastive term CONVERGES over the same span (nce 0.877 -> 0.428, edge 0.248 -> 0.161) while recall falls: a warm-up dip recovers as the new term settles, this one settles and keeps costing. It is a TRADE - the model buys discrimination and pays in detection, exactly as predicted when both heads read one representation.
PARTLY CONFOUNDED, in our favour and against: the plain baseline WITHOUT contrastive slides the same way (recall 0.966 -> 0.936), because the detection loss supervises ~98% of real cells as background. The contrastive arm slid FASTER (0.867 vs 0.936), so the trade is probably real, but a clean rerun needs the masked loss in place.
UNTRIED VARIANTS, in prior order: (a) a SEPARATE embedding head so the contrastive gradient never reshapes detection features; (b) stop-gradient into the shared trunk; (c) a magnitude-matched weight (<=0.01) chosen by matching the term to the edge loss rather than guessed. PROCESS NOTE: I killed this run at step 2500 of 18000 and called it refuted, having already recorded a memory saying not to stop on a dip; the withdrawal and rerun are what produced the real answer.

title: BUG: both logging paths failed silently in the first real joint run
description:
The joint warm-start run (3000 steps) trained fine and saved joint_warm_v1.pt + .resume.pt, but produced NO window summaries and NO recorded metrics. Two independent SILENT failures in one run.

(1) __main__ LOGGER HOLE - general, hits every python -m entrypoint. Modules log via logging.getLogger(__name__). Run as a module, that file executes as __main__, so its logger is named __main__ - NOT a child of celltrack - and Obs.setup, which configures the celltrack logger with propagate=False, never sees it. Imported modules were fine (celltrack.tracker lines appeared throughout), which is exactly why it looked like the loop had never run. Every trainer and CLI in the repo has this hole.
FIX: Obs.setup attaches its handlers to the __main__ logger as well as celltrack (one home, general), OR entrypoints log through the logger Obs.setup returns instead of a module-level getLogger(__name__).

(2) MLFLOW RECORDED NOTHING, SILENTLY. mlflow.db is on an out-of-date schema - found version 6f8d9c3b2a1e, expected b7e4c1a90f23; needs mlflow db upgrade sqlite:///mlflow.db. Tracker wraps every call in contextlib.suppress so tracking must never break a run - correct as a principle, but it also means it never RECORDS one and says nothing about it.
FIX: upgrade the db, and make the suppression VISIBLE - log a one-time WARNING on the first suppressed failure, still never raising, so a silently-inert tracker is detectable in seconds rather than after a run.

DESIGN LESSON: a component whose contract is never break the caller must still be LOUD about being broken, or it converts a hard failure into an invisible one. Both of today's failures had exactly that shape.

COST: the first real joint run produced a checkpoint with an UNKNOWN score. It must be re-scored offline against the proxy to recover the number.
close_reason: FIXED 2026-08-10. Both paths were silently dead in the first real joint run. (1) mlflow had been INERT since the day it was wired: enable_system_metrics_logging() sets a global flag and every later start_run() then RAISED because psutil was absent, which the never-break-a-run guard swallowed - a whole 3000-step run recorded nothing. Now gated on importlib.util.find_spec('psutil'), and Tracker._disabled logs one warning instead of vanishing, so a broken tracker is distinguishable from a working one. (2) Console summaries went to a __main__ logger sitting OUTSIDE the celltrack tree the handlers configure, so every 'python -m' entrypoint logged into the void while imported modules kept printing; Obs.setup now configures both. Generalisable lesson recorded: a component whose contract is 'never break the caller' must still be LOUD about being broken, or it converts a hard failure into an invisible one.

title: Bidirectional harmonic probability: fuse forward and reverse edge affinities
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 via notebook provenance: the pipeline at public 0.915 uses "bidirectional harmonic-probability association fusion", transcribed from yusuketogashi/no-hack-biohub-cell-another-approch-3rd v18 ("Biohub 145 | Bidirectional Harmonic Probability").

THE METHOD: score each frame gap in BOTH temporal directions - forward P(source@t -> target@t+1) and reverse P(target@t+1 -> source@t), the latter by running the association with the pair swapped so the model sees time reversed - then fuse the two matrices with a HARMONIC mean. The harmonic mean is dominated by the SMALLER of the two, so a pair only scores high when BOTH directions agree: it demands mutual consistency rather than one-sided preference.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE THING WE ALREADY REFUTED: bead e9b tested affinity RE-NORMALISATION (softmax over sources 0.8680 / over targets 0.8683 / raw 0.8692 / "bidir" 0.8686 = all noise) - but that was re-normalising the SAME forward logit matrix. This is a SECOND forward pass with the temporal pair swapped, which is a different computation the model has never been asked for. Our current scorer only softmaxes over sources (the "one parent per target" constraint).

WHY THE MECHANISM FITS OUR DOCUMENTED FAILURE: dense mislinks are 100% affinity-inverted (MislinkSignal: P_true 0.134 vs P_chosen 0.686) - a confident WRONG NEAR neighbour beating the true far successor. A wrong near neighbour often wins FORWARD while failing in REVERSE (the near cell has its own better parent), so mutual agreement is exactly the signal that separates them. And unlike lna/zni this needs NO retraining - it is an inference-time fusion, so the three refuted retrain results do not apply.

COST: 2x the affinity forward per gap. Affinity is ~33% of inference, but we just restored fp16 (~2x) and have 2x T4 dispatch, so it is affordable. IMPLEMENT in celltrack/models/edge_transformer.py (a reverse _gap_logits + a fusion), A/B on the proxy, then LB.
notes:
CONSUMER-COUPLING CROSS-TEST (2026-08-10). Same affinity change, two different linkers, @thr0.97:
  assignment (per-frame):        forward 0.9334 -> bidirectional 0.9307  (-0.0027)
  flow (global, boundary=3):     forward 0.9349 -> bidirectional 0.9353  (+0.0004)
The SIGN FLIPS. Neither cell clears the 0.01-0.02 noise floor, so this is NOT a claim that bidirectional helps the flow linker - the meaningful quantity is the DIFFERENTIAL (~0.0031) between consumers for an identical affinity.

WHY IT MATTERS: the coupling hypothesis made a falsifiable prediction - the fusion should stop hurting once the consumer imposes one-parent/one-child GLOBALLY (as a constrained solver does) instead of through the affinity normalisation itself (softmax-over-sources, which AssignmentLinker cost distance-bonus*P is built around). It survived a test that could have killed it: had bidirectional hurt flow equally, "shaped for a different consumer" would be dead. Weak supporting evidence, not proof.

METHOD NOTE that nearly wasted a run: FlowLinker at disappearance_cost=0 reduces to AssignmentLinker EDGE-FOR-EDGE, and the first cross-test was run there - it reproduced the assignment numbers exactly (0.9334/0.9307) and tested nothing. A control must be verified to actually vary the thing it controls for. The real test needs boundary_cost > 0 (used 3, the measured peak).

CONSEQUENCE: port the 0.915 bundle AS A BUNDLE (bead 73g: ILP-global + bidirectional fusion + their repairs together), not cherry-picked. Our last three frontier cherry-picks (gate14, appearance-in-linker, motion relink) each failed alone while their bundle scored.
close_reason: Shipped inside the 0.895 config. Sign-flip prediction confirmed on the LB (+0.004 under flow, -0.0027 under assignment).

title: Boundary-truncated track rescue: min_track_length penalises tracks flush against frame 0 or T-1
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 in public notebook maulikgajera/biohub-cell-tracking-truncated-track-rescue-patch (patch on a pipeline at public 0.915). THE BIAS (we share it): ShortTrackFilter drops any linked component shorter than min_track_length (we ship 6, currently probing 7). But a component flush against the FIRST or LAST observed frame of the video is structurally INCAPABLE of reaching that length - a track that starts at frame 96 of 100 can be at most 5 frames long no matter how real it is. We delete it as if it were a spurious fragment. The hidden annotation still scores its edges, so every such deletion is pure lost recall.

THE FIX: exempt a component from the length filter when it touches frame 0 or frame T-1 (i.e. it is truncated by the clip boundary rather than by being spurious). The notebook ships it opt-in/default-off as BIOHUB_OUTPUT_BOUNDARY_TRACK_RESCUE and is explicit that it is a hypothesis to A/B, not a guaranteed win.

WHY THE PRIOR IS GOOD FOR US SPECIFICALLY: this is a RECALL lever of the DECISION-RULE kind, not the admission-widening kind - it changes which components we DELETE, and per our transfer law the levers that transferred were decision-rule changes (AssignmentLinker global +0.005) while recall-side/admission tweaks were flat. Also it composes with, and is distinct from, the confidence-based ShortTrackRescue we already built (that one rescues short components with high mean edge prob; this one rescues them for a purely structural reason). Cells enter and leave the field of view constantly, so the affected set is not tiny.

IMPLEMENT: add the exemption to celltrack/postproc/short_track_filter.py as a config flag beside the existing rescue, A/B on the proxy, then LB. Cheap - pure post-processing, needs no forward pass, testable off cached responses.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + PROXY A/B (2026-08-10). ShortTrackFilter.keep_boundary (TrackerConfig.keep_boundary_tracks, default off) exempts components touching the first or last observed frame. Sharpened beyond the notebook framing: a short component STRICTLY INSIDE the clip appeared and vanished mid-movie (the genuinely suspicious case) while one flush against a boundary extends past what was filmed - the test asserts that asymmetry (a 2-node component at the last frame survives, an identical one mid-clip is still dropped). PROXY @thr0.97: baseline 0.9334 -> boundary 0.9329 = -0.0005 = a TIE under our 0.01-0.02 noise floor. EXPECTED and NOT a refutation: this is a RECALL lever and the sparse proxy structurally cannot see its payoff - our annotation mostly lacks the boundary tracks the hidden denser annotation scores. The informative part is that it did NOT hurt, i.e. the re-added components are almost all free or true rather than false positives (a sloppy rescue would have tanked it). Same signature as the confidence ShortTrackRescue (proxy -0.0005, shipped as an LB probe). NEXT: LB arm on top of the v21 base (min7+rescue), single variable flipped, so the two submissions are directly comparable when both land.
close_reason: MEASURED AND NEUTRAL 2026-08-10. Implemented (ShortTrackFilter.keep_boundary + TrackerConfig.keep_boundary_tracks, default off) with the asymmetry sharpened beyond the source notebook: a short component strictly INSIDE the clip appeared and vanished mid-movie (suspicious), one touching a boundary extends past what was filmed (truncated) - the test asserts exactly that. PROXY -0.0005; LB 55406248 = 0.891, identical to its base 55405539. So it neither helps nor hurts: the re-added components are true or free rather than false positives, but the hidden denser annotation does not reward them. Fifth frontier component to fail alone on our pipeline. Kept opt-in.

title: BIAS: selector evaluates at threshold 0.5 while we ship 0.97 (and the fix removes the parameter)
description: FOUND 2026-08-10. Both trainers default eval_threshold=0.5 (TUNetTrainConfig line ~79, JointTrainConfig same) and ModelEvaluator mounts TrackerConfig(threshold=config.eval_threshold). The SHIPPED kernel runs _THRESHOLD=0.97. So checkpoints are RANKED at an operating point we never deploy. Threshold is not a minor knob here - it is THE lever the LB responds to (public 0.99/0.98/0.97 = 0.887/0.891/0.892) and it drives the node-count penalty, so 'best at 0.5' does not imply 'best at 0.97'. SUBTLETY (why the naive fix is also wrong): the right threshold is MODEL-DEPENDENT - the from-scratch detector peaked at 0.999, not 0.97 (cdg-honest-4movie), because its calibration differs from pilkwang's. So hard-coding 0.97 in the selector would just move the bias, not remove it. PROPER FIX (removes the magic parameter, self-balancing per the standing directive): score each checkpoint at ITS OWN BEST operating point - sweep a few thresholds at eval and select on the max. This is CHEAP by construction because the architecture already splits the expensive half from the replayable half: logit_volumes (forward, expensive) vs graph_from_volumes (read-out, cheap) and CellTracker.with_config exists precisely to 'reuse the cache across a sweep'. ModelEvaluator currently uses EphemeralResponseStore (drops the volumes), so the sweep needs a per-eval caching store: forward ONCE, then read out + link at N thresholds (linking is only ~11% of a video). Then eval_threshold DISAPPEARS as a config field and the logged score carries its own best threshold - which is also the number to ship for that checkpoint. INTERACTS WITH: the eval_tta mismatch (selector runs tta=False, kernel ships tta=True) - same class, milder, decide together.
notes:
COST MODEL CORRECTED 2026-08-11, and it changes what the fix must be. The design assumed detection is the expensive half (from the submission audit: detect 55% / affinity 33% / link 11%). That split is for the DUAL-SEED 4-fold-TTA submission. The SELECTOR is single-seed with tta=False, and its measured split is the other way round: 44b6_341df25f detect 3.4s | affinity 26.7s | link+post 3.0s. AFFINITY IS 80% OF THE SELECTOR EVAL.

So the planned fix - a caching store so the forward runs once and N read-outs replay - buys almost NOTHING here (it amortises the 10% that is cheap). Affinity is recomputed per threshold because it is scored at the DETECTED NODES, which the threshold chooses.

WHAT MAKES A SWEEP CHEAP INSTEAD: the node sets are EXACTLY NESTED in the threshold, so one affinity computation at the lowest threshold serves every higher one by SLICING its rows and columns. Proof: _local_maxima marks volume == max_pool(volume); two adjacent marked voxels lie inside each other's pooling kernel, so each is >= the other, so every connected plateau component is CONSTANT-valued. A floor keeps or drops a component whole and can never split one. Pinned by test_maxima_nest_in_the_floor (tests/unit/celltrack/detectors/peaks.py). PRECONDITION: suppression radius >= 1 voxel on every axis - true on the isotropic (1,4,4) read-out grid, NOT guaranteed for anisotropic spacing where a zero-radius axis leaves neighbours uncompared. PeakExtractor.maxima already exists for exactly this and its sweep use is currently unwired.

PRIORITY LOWERED, with the reason: the threshold's model-dependence only bites when a run TRAINS DETECTION. Our association arms run --det-weight 0, so the detector stays pilkwang-calibrated and the shipped 0.97 is already their correct operating point. This is on the critical path for detection/from-scratch runs (where our own detector peaked at 0.999), not for the association work that is currently the P0.

title: BIAS: ModelEvaluator selects checkpoints on the 4 proxy movies, which are IN the training split
description: FOUND 2026-08-10 by direct check: AcquisitionFolds().split(root.videos('train'),0).train contains ALL FOUR TEST_MOVIES (44b6_0113de3b, 44b6_0b24845f, 6bba_05b6850b, 6bba_05db0fb1) among its 158 videos. The new celltrack/eval/model_evaluator.py ModelEvaluator scores the trained detector on exactly those 4 movies (TestMovieProxy) and the trainers use that score for EarlyStop + save-best. So CHECKPOINT SELECTION IS LEAKED: the selector cannot see overfitting on the movies it judges by; it will prefer the most-memorised checkpoint. WHY IT MATTERS (not merely academic): the hidden LB is a DENSER annotation of these SAME movies, while our local labels are the sparse subset - so a checkpoint that memorises our sparse labels can score better locally and generalise WORSE to the dense hidden set. That is the proxy->LB anti-transfer pattern the campaign has hit repeatedly (node-count farming, smooth0.3, min7). Note training ON them is legitimate (they live in train/ and tms showed memorising them buys nothing); the defect is SELECTING on them. FIX: exclude TEST_MOVIES from the training targets in both trainers' main() (celltrack/training/tunet_detector.py + joint_detector.py) - 158 -> 154 videos, a 2.5% data cost - so the selector measures generalisation. Do it in ONE general place (a filter both trainers call), not copy-pasted. THEN any own-weights run is honestly selected. BLOCKS meaningful joint/detector runs.
close_reason: FIXED 2026-08-10 by the honest split. Selection ran on fold-0, a k-fold split built before we knew the competition's test set is four specific movies living INSIDE train/ - leaked for anything pilkwang-based (they trained on 180 of 199, covering ~93% of fold-0's validation) and it MISRANKED (the same weights score 0.837 through the fold-0 motion-linker eval and 0.893 through the real pipeline). Replaced with 191 train / 4 validation (the DENSELY annotated movies, selected on) / 4 test (the competition movies, untouched) - which gained data rather than costing it. Selecting on densely-annotated held-out videos points the pressure at labels shaped like the ones that score us, instead of our sparse annotations of the test four. Calibration figure that fell out and is worth keeping: the SAME untrained weights score 0.8474 on the dense validation four and 0.9100 on the sparse test four against a true LB of 0.892 - the sparse set flatters through the node-count bonus.

title: Joint trainer (T=2, detection+association) — the competitive own-weights path

title: Multi-frame temporal context (T>2) — trajectory disambiguation for dense mislinks
description: NEW un-refuted dense-mislink axis. All prior attacks (e9b/lna/zni/tf5) were PAIRWISE (single t,t+1 view). Mislinks are per-frame-ambiguous by construction: fast-mover true successor lands FAR, slow neighbor lands NEAR, indistinguishable from 2 frames (distance AND pairwise affinity both prefer near-wrong). Over t-1,t,t+1,t+2 the TRAJECTORY (velocity/accel) disambiguates -> the far successor is consistent with motion. Approaches: (a) T>2 window in the temporal backbone + edge transformer (needs JOINT retrain, temporal attn is built for T=2); (b) a trajectory-aware LINKER using multi-frame velocity prediction (cheaper, no retrain). Cost ~T/2x compute+memory (pairs with gradient checkpointing). ASSOCIATION lever -> lives in the joint/edge model, NOT the detection-only trainer. Physics: cell motion ~1.7um/frame, ~8.5um over 5 frames = enough trajectory signal. HIGH interest - first genuinely new dense-mislink lever since the pairwise refutations.

title: LB-recall submission ladder — map the LB recall curve with daily slots (proxy is threshold-blind)

Candidates in recall order: thr0.98 (more nodes than 0.99 champion), thr0.985, +DeepCenter-union (slw), +TTA (fcd). Submit the champion-config kernel at each, one per slot, record LB. Builds the LB recall curve -> finds the true operating point. Kernel = celltrack-dualseed-assign-affinity-stlf6 variants. Best public so far 0.887 @thr0.99. Do NOT bonus-farm (higher thr) - that anti-transfers.
notes:
PREMISE PARTLY SUPERSEDED 2026-08-10. This bead's rationale is 'the proxy is threshold-blind, so map the recall curve with daily LB slots'. That was the right observation with the wrong cause attributed: the proxy was not blind because our annotations are SPARSE, it was blind because the NODE-COUNT BONUS rewards the trimming sparse annotation hides. Clamping the bonus at 1.0 (VideoMetrics.clamped_edge_jaccard) makes the SAME sparse proxy reproduce the leaderboard's threshold ordering on all four points we have ground truth for:
  thr    faithful  clamped   bonus     LB
  0.995  0.9326    0.9203    +0.0123   0.880
  0.99   0.9348    0.9264    +0.0083   0.887
  0.98   0.9344    0.9291    +0.0053   0.891
  0.97   0.9334    0.9295    +0.0039   0.892
The faithful score picks 0.99 - the config that LOST 0.005 on the leaderboard. So threshold is LOCALLY TESTABLE now and does not need slots.
WHAT REMAINS TRUE, and why this is 'partly': the correction is scoped to knobs that change COUNTS. Position-moving knobs (smooth_strength, linefit) stay genuinely proxy-blind for a DIFFERENT reason - a matching-radius effect, not a count effect - and min_track_length was predicted to flip under the clamp and did NOT (it halved the bias without flipping it). So a recall LADDER is still LB-only for those, but the threshold axis itself is done: the ladder was already run (0.995/0.99/0.98/0.97 = 0.880/0.887/0.891/0.892) and 0.97 is settled and shipped, with the clamped sweep flattening below it.
CONSEQUENCE: do NOT spend a slot on threshold. If this bead is kept it should be re-scoped to the position-moving knobs only, which are the ones no local instrument can rank.

title: Background/random-negative crops to fix detector over-firing
description: Training crops are always anchored on an annotated cell (+jitter), so the model never sees large empty background. At full-frame inference it over-fires there: w64 detector emits 528k nodes at thr=0.5 on a 71-truth-node video, score 0.0, uncalibrated (needs 0.99+). Fix: sample a fraction of crops from uniformly-random locations (mostly empty tissue) so the model learns to be confidently-negative on background. The DetectionTarget mask still excludes ambiguous bright regions, so unannotated cells in a random crop carry no gradient (safe). Expected: calibrated detector operating near 0.5, far fewer false nodes to link (also speeds the linker). CropSampler gets background_fraction; run.py a flag; retrain w64 and re-eval on fold-0 val.
close_reason: INVESTIGATED, lesson recorded: bg-crops (0.3) HELP sparse (44b6 0.269->0.380, confident zeros = less smearing) but TANK dense (6bba 0.513->0.228). Value: bg-negatives are density-conditional, not a global good. Constrains 80e recipe -> apply bg-crops only where sparse, or per-crop positive-count normalize.

Two cheap runs that bound the problem before any model is trained.

nearest-neighbour linker - expected near 0.98 given that 2.1% of true links exceed 7 um.

(b) FLOOR: a classical detector (LoG/DoG on the quantile-normalised volume, anisotropy-aware sigma)
plus the same linker, scored end to end.

DONE WHEN: both numbers are in an interpretations/ note with the gap between them named. That gap is
the budget the learned detector has to win, and it decides whether effort goes into detection or
linking.

that unmatched predicted nodes generate no FP, adjusted edge jaccard against the GEFF

subsequent keep/kill decision noise.
