title: [epic] GOAL: Epic 1 - architecture + first scored baseline
description:
Two strands, deliberately split. The BASELINE strand exists to produce a real leaderboard number
fast, using methods we already trust; the ARCHITECTURE strand builds the model that is meant to beat
it. They meet at the operating-point sweep.

The gate between them: nothing in the architecture strand is worth tuning until the evaluator is
verified and a trivial baseline has a number. Deadline 2026-09-29; top LB 0.929 as of 2026-07-23.

Score = adj_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard, with
adj_edge_jaccard = max(0, J * (1 - 0.1 * (N_pred - N_total)/N_total)).
See docs/PLAN.md and interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_dataset-survey.md.

title: Should TrackerConfig's field defaults simply BE the shipped recipe? — two operating points is what made today's bug class possible
description:
TrackerConfig now carries TWO operating points: its FIELD DEFAULTS (per-frame assignment linker, no fusion — the 0.892 tier) and TrackerConfig.shipped() (flow boundary 3 + bidirectional — the 0.895 recipe we submit). Today four separate defects were all instances of "something constructed the first when it meant the second": the checkpoint selector in both trainers, six diagnostics, CellTracker._mounted itself, and proxy_eval's config_at plus its two swept-coordinate defaults at two layers each.

Every one is now fixed at the call site. The question this bead asks is whether the SHAPE should change so the class cannot recur: make the field defaults BE the shipped values, and `shipped()` becomes redundant.

FOR: `TrackerConfig()` would then mean "what we submit", so the failure mode is unconstructible rather than merely discouraged — which is the standard this repo already applied when it moved the threshold default from 0.99 to the LB-measured 0.97 ("a knob arbitrated by the leaderboard must carry that value as its DEFAULT, otherwise the good value lives only at one call site").

AGAINST, and these are not weak:
1. `LinkerConfig()` alone still defaults to `assignment`, so `TrackerConfig(linker=LinkerConfig())` stays unshipped. Merging gives PARTIAL protection and may read as total — arguably worse than an explicit `shipped()` a reader must ask for.
2. A default that means "our current best" CHANGES MEANING as the recipe improves, so a test or a note written against `TrackerConfig()` silently re-points. The named method makes the recipe's identity explicit and greppable; `test_shipped` pins it precisely because it is named.
3. The neutral defaults are a legitimate documented baseline — the per-frame linker is a real, tested strategy, and several unit tests use `TrackerConfig()` purely as an arbitrary base for override parsing where the values are irrelevant.

MEASURED CONTEXT that makes this non-cosmetic: the two operating points are not interchangeable. Re-ranking saved checkpoints under both INVERTS which one wins (0.9175/0.9141 becomes 0.9153/0.9206), the threshold ladder reverses order, and the edge blend varies under one while sitting on a plateau under the other. So "which default" is a question about which pipeline every unannotated measurement describes.

DECIDE, do not drift: either merge them and delete `shipped()`, or keep both and make the neutral one HARDER to reach by accident (e.g. require the linker to be named explicitly). What must not happen is two silently-different operating points with no rule about which a caller gets.

title: proxy_eval prints only the TOTAL score — the edge and division terms must be reported separately
description:
score = adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard, and the proxy prints only the sum. So a division arm that RAISES div_jac while costing more edge jaccard is indistinguishable from one that does nothing - which is exactly the ambiguity that left the 2026-08-11 division re-test (-0.0039) with an unresolved mechanism after it had already been measured.

FIX: report both terms, and the fork COUNT, on every run. All three are already computed inside the metric; only the reporting drops them.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND DIVISIONS: our proxy holds THREE annotated divisions, so div_jac cannot rank division arms at all. The fork count and whether the one reachable division (232) survives are the readable signals - and neither is printed today. An instrument that reports a sum when it holds the parts is hiding evidence it already has.
close_reason: Done: proxy_eval now logs 'proxy score=X (clamped Y, bonus Z) = edge A + 0.1 * div B'. Both terms were already on SplitScore; only the reporting dropped them. It immediately earned itself — the division arms are read on the fork count and the edge-term cost, and without the split those two are indistinguishable from a division-term change.

title: Flow prices births and deaths identically — the graph already separates them, the config does not
description:
THE PLUMBING ALREADY DISTINGUISHES BIRTH FROM DEATH; THE CONFIG COLLAPSES THEM. FlowLinker builds the circulation with two separate arcs and two separate arrays -
    appearance, disappearance = self._boundary_costs(positions_um, timepoints)
    graph.add_edge(_SOURCE, ("in", row), weight=appearance[row])
    graph.add_edge(("out", row), _SINK, weight=disappearance[row])
- but `_boundary_costs` derives BOTH from a single `boundary_cost` scalar. So the solver can already price a track START differently from a track END, and we have never asked it to. Fourth instance of a capability that exists and is unreachable (after the motion linker's affinity, the relative-position transformer, and EdgeBlendOptions).

WHY ASYMMETRY IS PHYSICALLY MOTIVATED, not just an extra knob: appearances and disappearances are NOT symmetric events in this data. A track can begin mid-movie for several ordinary reasons - a cell enters the imaged volume, a division produces a new daughter, or the annotation simply starts - whereas a track ENDING mid-movie is rarer and more suspicious. Charging the same price for both forces the solver to treat "a new cell showed up" and "a cell vanished" as equally implausible, which the biology does not support.

THE FRONTIER USES EXACTLY THIS AND WE HAVE NEVER PORTED IT. The disclosed LB897 config sets ILP appearance = 0.0 with disappearance = 1.575 - free to start a track, expensive to end one. Note this is a DIFFERENT claim from the geometric boundary prior we already REFUTED (BoundaryPrior, free at the volume face and clip ends, full cost in the interior, measured -0.0027): that one varies the price by WHERE the boundary is, this varies it by WHICH DIRECTION the boundary goes. Do not retire this by association with that.

WHAT TO BUILD: split the single knob into appearance and disappearance components on LinkerConfig, defaulting so that today's behaviour is byte-identical (both equal to the current `disappearance_cost`), reachable via --set, with the identity asserted through the CONFIG path. `_boundary_costs` already returns two arrays, so the change is in how they are FILLED, not in the graph.

ARMS, on the shipped control (thr 0.97, flow, bidirectional, current boundary 3 -> clamped 0.9353):
  appearance 3, disappearance 3   control, must reproduce 0.9353 exactly
  appearance 0, disappearance 3   the frontier's direction - free births, priced deaths
  appearance 3, disappearance 0   the opposite, as the control for the DIRECTION claim
  appearance 0, disappearance 6   free births, doubly-priced deaths
The third arm matters: without it a gain from arm 2 cannot be separated from "the total boundary budget changed".

THE DIRECTION IS AN OPEN QUESTION AND THE FP WORK MAY DECIDE IT. Higher disappearance = more reluctant to end a track = MORE willing to link on past a true track end. Our boundary sweep already reads 0=0.9344, 3=0.9351, 6=0.9313, 10=0.9282, i.e. declining above 3, which is consistent with over-linking already being priced too weakly against. If the prediction-centric FP decomposition finds SOURCE_ENDS dominating the 40 unclassified false positives, then we are over-linking past track ends and the useful asymmetry may be the OPPOSITE of the frontier's - cheaper deaths, not dearer ones. Run this AFTER that decomposition reports, and let its counts pick the expected direction before measuring.

title: Unify the per-pair cost terms behind one CostTerm protocol — two already share an exact signature, a third is filed
description:
Tonight added four objects that modify how a linker decides, and two of them already share an EXACT signature:
    MutualBonus.discount(timepoint, cost) -> cost
    RankerBonus.discount(timepoint, cost) -> cost
The filed forward-acceleration lookahead would be a third with the same shape, and each new one currently costs: a field on BOTH AssignmentLinker and FlowLinker, an `if self.x is not None:` branch in each `_gated_cost`, a slot in LinkerParts, a knob on LinkerConfig, a per-knob reader set, and a builder-row argument. That is six places per term, and the repo rules ask for low ifs, strategy pattern, and maximum unification.

THE UNIFICATION: a `CostTerm` protocol with `discount(timepoint, cost) -> cost`, and each linker folding an ORDERED TUPLE of them:
    for term in self.cost_terms: cost = term.discount(timepoint, cost)
MutualBonus and RankerBonus become implementations; the lookahead becomes a third with no linker change at all. The branch disappears (an empty tuple is the default and is exactly today's behaviour), and LinkerParts collapses toward one sequence.

SCOPE IT HONESTLY — DO NOT FORCE THE OTHER TWO IN. AgreementGate.narrow(timepoint, within_gate) operates on ADMISSION (which pairs the solver may consider), and BoundaryPrior.factors() prices PER-NODE track boundaries and applies only to the flow linker's source/sink arcs. Those are different operations on different objects; bending them into a cost-discount protocol would be the "one interface to rule them all" mistake that makes the abstraction lie. Three concepts, not one: admission, per-pair cost, per-node boundary price.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING NOW RATHER THAN LATER: we have exactly the evidence that says more terms are coming (the lookahead is filed; the ranker may return in a motion-predicted cost; a likelihood-form cost is filed). Unifying at three implementations is cheap; at six it is a refactor nobody wants to start. And the ORDER of application becomes explicit and testable, which it currently is not - today the sequence is whatever the two `if` blocks happen to be written in.

CONSTRAINTS: the linker layer must not import celltrack/edges/ (import-linter), so terms keep arriving as EdgeAffinity-backed objects built outside and handed in, exactly as they do now. Default must be byte-identical - an empty tuple, asserted by a test. And keep the per-knob reader sets: which linkers can honour which term is a real distinction that a uniform protocol must not erase, since a knob accepted and silently dropped is the failure the validator exists to prevent.

title: Forward acceleration lookahead — the velocity idea as a COST term, sidestepping the zero-init learning problem
description:
DISCLOSED MECHANISM from the reproducible 0.915 lineage (research/deep_dives/2026-08-11_public-frontier-recheck.md, F5, full source read):

    current_velocity = target_pos - source_pos
    residual = min over next_id in frame t+2 of norm of ((next_pos - target_pos) - current_velocity)
               considering only continuations within 10um of the target
    support  = max of 0 and (1 - residual / 4.0)
    cost -= 0.20 * support

An edge is rewarded when SOME continuation into t+2 keeps its velocity constant - a constant-acceleration prior evaluated one frame beyond the edge being scored.

TAKE THE MECHANISM SERIOUSLY, NOT THE CLAIMED GAIN. It is the only change between their 0.915 and their 0.916, and the author's own target is +0.001 - below our 0.01-0.02 transfer floor and near our ~0.0008-per-edge proxy floor. Do not expect it to show up cleanly.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH BUILDING, and this is what makes it more than a knob: it is the VELOCITY idea expressed as a COST rather than as a model feature, and that sidesteps exactly what made our prior-velocity arm untestable. That arm added zero-initialised input columns (to preserve the warm start bitwise), so the model had to LEARN to use a brand-new input inside a recipe that peaks at 250-750 steps and degrades after - we may have been asking it to learn a feature in a window shorter than learning one takes. A cost term needs no learning, no retraining and no warm-start compromise: it either helps at inference or it does not, and one proxy run says which.

IT IS ALSO GENUINELY NEW INFORMATION FOR US. Everything our linker sees today is the pair under consideration plus, optionally, the previous gap. Nothing looks FORWARD. A t+2 continuation is information no current term has access to, which is a different claim from re-weighting what we already see - and the transfer law says decision-rule changes carrying new information are the class that has actually moved our leaderboard score.

DISTINCT FROM THE REFUTED MOTION RELINK: that re-decided links from a damped constant-velocity prediction and lost (0.82-0.84 vs 0.868 on the dense movie). This does not re-decide anything; it only shades the cost of the link already under consideration, and the geometry it uses is MEASURED (the actual t+2 detections) rather than extrapolated.

CONSTANTS TO DERIVE, NOT COPY: their 10um continuation gate is our gate_um (the argued maximum single-frame travel), so reuse it rather than adding a second radius. The 4.0um residual scale and the 0.20 bonus sit in THEIR cost scale, which is roughly 30x weaker than ours - the same trap that made the ranker's 0.75 an off-by-30 no-op we would have misread as "it does not help". Express the bonus as a fraction of our P-budget of 20, and argue the residual scale against something measured, or the arm measures the translation rather than the mechanism.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE: the linker already receives per-frame detections, so t+2 positions are in hand; no extra detection or affinity pass is needed. It composes as another discount alongside MutualBonus and RankerBonus, which already establish that shape.

title: Verify the sampler mixture restores held-out quality — entropy ~0.57 is the read, not the score
description:
The collapse is fixed structurally (no pair can be starved: p = (1-a)/n + a*d/sum(d), a=1/2), but the MECHANISM CLAIM is untested: that mixing actually restores held-out quality past the point the unmixed sampler peaked.

WHAT TO RUN: the same from-scratch recipe (8 epochs, lr 3e-4 cosine, masked detection loss, thr 0.97 selector) with --difficulty-sampling ON, against the uniform-sampling control already measured.

THE READ TO WATCH IS ENTROPY, NOT THE SCORE. Under the even mixture normalised entropy should sit near 0.57 on an 18024-pair corpus and STAY there; the failing run fell 0.961 -> 0.378 -> 0.235. If entropy holds and recall still degrades past 1.5 epochs, the sampler was never the cause and the from-scratch regime itself is the problem - which the uniform control decides independently.

THREE OUTCOMES, all informative:
(a) entropy holds AND recall keeps climbing past 1.5 epochs -> the mixture fixed it, difficulty weighting earns its place.
(b) entropy holds AND recall still peaks early -> the collapse was a symptom, not the cause; difficulty weighting is neutral and the honest default is uniform (keep optimistic init alone, which independently reached full coverage in about one pass vs i.i.d.'s ~2.8n draws).
(c) entropy falls anyway -> the mixture is insufficient and the analysis is wrong; do not add a knob to rescue it, re-derive.

DO NOT tune `a` on this run. It is derived (maximum ignorance between i.i.d.-degeneracy and freeze-out, two failure modes sharing no unit) and sweeping it would convert a derived quantity back into the magic number the design exists to avoid. If the mixture is wrong, the fix is a different argument, not a different value.

CONTEXT: entropy was added as a speculative collapse guard and is the only reason the original failure was diagnosable at all - but it was also shown NOT to work as a controller (one frozen pair among 18024 moves it by ~1e-4), so it stays an acceptance test.

title: Consolidate core/hparams.py RunConfig with the joint config hierarchy
description: joint_config.py now carries the validated nested hierarchy for the joint trainer (Field bounds + JSON round-trip via pydantic). core/hparams.py::RunConfig survives because (a) celltrack/training/tracked_run.py::TrackedRun types on it (optim.epochs/patience/es_min_delta, eval.every), and (b) it uniquely provides dotted --set overrides (apply_overrides), to_json/from_json path helpers, and fields the joint trainer has no analogue for (data.window_size, data.pool_kernel_um, aug.*, optim.batch, optim.precision, name, out_dir). Its DEFAULTS are the published recipe and several are refuted by our measurements (lr 1e-3, det_loss_weight 10.0, eval.threshold 0.99 vs the LB-best 0.97) - anything wired to it must not inherit them. Decide: rewire TrackedRun onto the concern-grouped config and delete hparams, or port the epoch-native/override capabilities across.

title: Merge JointTrainConfig into a nested validated hierarchy — adopt hparams.RunConfig's shape, keep our measured defaults
description:
JointTrainConfig is a FLAT dataclass of ~25 fields spanning six unrelated concerns: data (downsample, out_channels, layers), optimisation (lr, grad_clip, cosine_lr, epochs/steps), losses (neg_weight, det_weight, contrastive_weight, temperature, ignore_ambiguous_above), eval/selection (eval_every, eval_threshold, eval_tta, patience, es_min_delta, evals_per_epoch, patience_epochs), runtime (device, compile_backbone, seed), and warm-start (warm_pack, difficulty_sampling, prior_velocity). The repo rule is "config objects over long arg lists" and the standing directive is hierarchical configuration; TrackerConfig already models this correctly with nested LinkerConfig / BridgeConfig / ShortTrackRescueConfig.

THE SHAPE ALREADY EXISTS AND WAS DELIBERATELY KEPT. core/hparams.py RunConfig is a validated pydantic hierarchy - DataCfg / AugCfg / OptimCfg / EvalCfg nested under RunConfig, with real Field constraints (ge/gt/lt) and JSON round-trip against the config.json files already written under the data root. It was deleted once for being unimported and RESTORED under the consolidate-before-deleting rule, precisely because it is the better design left unwired. Its groups map almost one-to-one onto JointTrainConfig's implicit ones.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT - ADOPT THE STRUCTURE, NOT THE NUMBERS. RunConfig's defaults encode the PUBLISHED recipe, not our measurements: lr 1e-3 (ours is 1e-5 for warm-start), det_loss_weight 10.0 (ours 1.0), threshold 0.99 (LB-refuted; 0.97 measured best), epochs 50, precision bf16 (inference wants fp16, training bf16 - check per site). Importing those wholesale would silently ship defaults the leaderboard has already refuted, which is exactly the bug fixed today under "a default you did not choose is not a decision you made". Every default in the merged config must carry OUR measured value and a comment saying which instrument arbitrated it.

ALSO MISSING FROM RunConfig, and required: the epoch-native fields (epochs / evals_per_epoch / patience_epochs) resolved against a DERIVED steps_per_epoch, ignore_ambiguous_above, difficulty_sampling, prior_velocity, contrastive_weight/temperature, warm_pack.

DO: merge into one nested, validated hierarchy - pydantic like its TrackerConfig siblings, groups named for the concern not the consumer. Keep the CLI flat (argparse flags are the user interface; the nesting is the model) and keep behaviour byte-identical, asserted by a test that trains twice and compares checkpoint bytes. Delete core/hparams.py only once every capability it has is present in the merged config - the JSON round-trip and the Field constraints are the two to preserve deliberately.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING WITHOUT A SCORE ATTACHED: the flat config is how the units bug hid (steps/eval_every/patience with no epoch anywhere), how the selector bias survived (no group owned "what are we selecting on"), and how RunConfig came to be written twice. Grouping makes each of those a visible question rather than a field lost among twenty-five.

title: RESULT: mutual-agreement gate is null under the global solver (+0.0004 clamped)
description:
STAGE RUN, NULL, with a mechanism and a caveat. The mutual-agreement GATE (admit an edge only where forward and reverse agree; keep the sharp directional probability in the cost) measured on the best consumer config (flow boundary 3 + bidirectional fusion, thr 0.97):
  no floor    faithful 0.9380  clamped 0.9353  bonus +0.0028
  floor 0.05  faithful 0.9381  clamped 0.9353  bonus +0.0028
  floor 0.15  faithful 0.9387  clamped 0.9357  bonus +0.0030
  floor 0.30  faithful 0.9396  clamped 0.9356  bonus +0.0039
Best is +0.0004 clamped = half an edge on ~1200. NULL.

THE CLAMPED SCORE EARNED ITS KEEP HERE. The FAITHFUL score rises monotonically with the floor (0.9380 -> 0.9396) and reads as "+0.0016, ship it". It is the bonus: the gate removes edges, fewer tracks survive min_track_length, node count falls, and the node-count factor pays for it (+0.0028 -> +0.0039). Without the clamp this would have been shipped as a win and would very likely have LOST on the leaderboard, exactly as node-count farming did (-0.007).

WHY IT IS NULL, and why that is consistent rather than disappointing: under a GLOBAL solver, mutual consistency as a GATE is largely redundant - the flow program already imposes one-parent/one-child and rejects those candidates through its own constraints. The same quantity worked as a SCORE (+0.004 LB) because it changes the affinity the solver OPTIMISES; a gate only removes candidates the solver would mostly have declined anyway. This is the affinity-form/consumer coupling showing up a third time.

NOT TESTED, and the honest next step if revisited: the gate under the PER-FRAME assignment linker, where the solver does NOT impose global structure and the redundancy argument does not apply. That is the pairing the coupling story predicts could work, and it is one proxy run.

ALSO WORTH KEEPING: the implementation discarded a cheaper in-linker derivation of the reverse direction (row-normalising the forward matrix) after proving it monotone in the forward probability - it could never prefer a lower-forward candidate, i.e. could not express the mechanism at all, and would have gated out the true successor on our own numbers. Any future "cheap agreement" shortcut must clear that same check.
close_reason: RESULT bead - finding recorded in memory + interpretations, nothing left to do.

title: Model soup: weight-average the fine-tune with its parent — the merge our ensemble failure argues FOR
description:
Motivated by TODAY'S NEGATIVE RESULT, not by novelty. We measured (from BOTH parents) that ensembling our joint fine-tune with pilkwang gains nothing: adding it as a third edge scorer read 0.9315-0.9320 and replacing seed2 with it read 0.9325-0.9334, against the shipped 0.9334. Diagnosis: ensembles pay for DISAGREEMENT, and a fine-tune agrees with the model it came from.

But that same property is the precondition for the OTHER merge. Output ensembling wants independent basins; WEIGHT-SPACE AVERAGING (model soup) wants the opposite - models in the SAME basin, separated by a small displacement. A fine-tune is in its parent's basin by construction. So the technique our failure rules out and the technique it argues FOR are different techniques.

EXPERIMENT (cheap: one state-dict average, one proxy run): score average(pilkwang_seed1, joint_warm_cos3k) - and the same for the seed2 pair - against both parents alone and against the shipped blend. Try a few interpolation weights (0.25/0.5/0.75), since the optimum is rarely the midpoint when one endpoint is better trained.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT WORK: our fine-tune measured +0.0075 over its parent on the untouched test four (association, recall unchanged) but showed signs of drift - the training curve dipped hard at some windows (0.8646 peak, 0.8332 by step 3000). If the run bought association quality while wandering slightly off the parent's optimum, the average could keep the gain and shed the drift. That is precisely the regime soups are for.

WHAT WOULD KILL IT: if the two heads' improvements are not linearly connected to the parent (a real risk for a transformer head trained 3000 steps), the average is worse than both endpoints. That is a clean, cheap read either way.

NOTE the joint checkpoint holds BOTH heads (detector + transformer), so a soup can be taken per-head - averaging only the transformer while keeping the parent's detector is a legitimate arm, and matches where the measured gain came from (association, not detection).

title: One architecture: per-voxel instance embedding instead of dense-backbone + sparse-point head
description:
Raised by the user: why is the joint model two architectures rather than one? Strictly it is one backbone with two heads, but there is a real structural discontinuity and it is a candidate root cause for the association wall that four experiments have now hit.

THE BOTTLENECK. The U-Net produces a DENSE per-voxel feature grid (C=32). The edge transformer reads it at SPARSE points - the detected centres - so everything association knows about a cell is 32 numbers sampled at ONE voxel, plus a 32-dim sinusoidal position embed. The cell's extent, shape, local context and raw intensity never reach the association head. For a task that is precisely "which of these near-identical blobs is which", that is a severe compression.

THE OBJECTIVE CONFLICT (the sharper half). Detection wants INVARIANCE - every cell should look maximally like "a cell". Association wants DISCRIMINATION - this cell must look different from the one 3um away. They share one representation and pull it in opposite directions. That predicts exactly what a1v measured on the frozen features: the true successor ranked above the wrong near neighbour only 22.9% of the time, and a bilinear probe generalised at 0.574 = chance. The features had been shaped to make cells look ALIKE.

WHY THE OLD REFUTATION NO LONGER SETTLES IT. a1v was deprioritised on that frozen-feature evidence. But today joint training UNFROZE the backbone and association improved (+0.0075 on held-out data, recall unchanged, so the gain was association). So "the features cannot discriminate" was a statement about FROZEN features, not about the architecture's ceiling.

THE ONE-ARCHITECTURE ALTERNATIVE: a single network emitting a per-voxel INSTANCE EMBEDDING alongside cellness, trained with a contrastive/metric objective so the same cell across frames is close and different cells are far. Association becomes embedding similarity - dense, end to end, no sparse sampling step, and the discrimination objective is explicit rather than in tension with detection. Optionally keep a small head on top for the final pairing.

WHY IT IS NOW THE BIGGEST REMAINING SWING: detection is saturated (recall 0.992, misses produce no peak at any threshold); the association wall has resisted four attacks (three frozen-head retrains and one inference-time fusion); fine-tuning improves individuals but adds no ensemble diversity (measured from both parents today). Every cheap lever is spent. This attacks a bottleneck we have MEASURED rather than one inferred.

COST/RISK: a new training objective and a new inference path, days not hours, and it forfeits the published weights' head start - our from-scratch detector caps ~0.04 below the shipped pipeline. Sequence it AFTER the cheap LB probes are exhausted, and prototype the embedding on the dense movie's known mislinks (does a contrastive embedding separate the 35 inverted cases the current features cannot?) before committing to a full retrain.

title: Train detection on duplicated windows, association on real pairs — distribution-match both heads
description:
Follows from the measured refutation of pair-context inference (duplicated 0.9334 vs real pair 0.9280).

THE INVERSION: detection is TRAINED on real-pair features and DEPLOYED on duplicated ones.

  training:  JointModel.forward stacks a REAL (t, t+1) window; detect_head is supervised on BOTH frames.
  inference: _response feeds (t, t), a duplicate, and reads slot 0.

We measured that the real neighbour HURTS detection at inference (-0.0054), because _TemporalAttention is residual and order-blind: a moved cell's features bleed into voxels where it is not yet. So the detection head is trained on the DEGRADED distribution and deployed on the clean one - the mismatch runs the opposite way to the one first assumed.

EXPERIMENT: in the joint step, compute the DETECTION loss from a duplicated window (matching inference) while keeping the ASSOCIATION loss on the real pair (which needs the genuine neighbour). Costs one extra backbone forward per step, and both heads then see the distribution they are deployed on.

WHY IT MIGHT MATTER: the joint run's gains came from association, while detection recall stayed flat (0.992 vs pilkwang's 0.993) on the test four. If the detection head is being trained through leaked features, that is a plausible reason it does not improve - and this is the cheapest way to find out.

RISK / ALTERNATIVE READING: the leak may act as a regulariser during training even though it hurts at inference, in which case matching the distributions could make detection worse. Either result is informative; the experiment is one flag plus one forward.

title: Wire MislinkSignal into training eval — the association instrument that can actually fail
description:
The joint trainer logs an edge AUC that reads exactly 1.0000 every window, for trained and untrained models alike, because it is computed over GROUND-TRUTH node pairs - the easy case, where our linker already sits at 0.9947. It is structurally incapable of failing, so association quality is currently INVISIBLE during training.

DO NOT ADD A NEW METRIC - the right instrument exists. celltrack/eval/dense_diagnosis.py MislinkSignal takes REAL detections and, for every mislinked edge, compares P(true successor) against P(the wrong target chosen), splitting the failures into:
- SIGNAL errors (p_chosen > p_true): the affinity itself ranks the wrong neighbour higher - a TRAINING problem.
- COST errors (p_true >= p_chosen): the affinity ranks correctly but the nearer wrong neighbour won on the distance term of cost = distance - bonus*P - a LINKER problem, already swept and refuted (e9b).
That split is exactly what a joint run needs to see: it says whether the association half is learning, and whether any remaining loss is even addressable by training.

WHY IT IS NEARLY FREE: ModelEvaluator already runs the full CellTracker on real detections at every eval window, so the linked graph and the per-gap affinities are already computed. The mislink analysis is post-hoc over that graph plus the ground truth - no extra forward pass.

IMPLEMENT: compute the inverted fraction (share of mislinks that are signal errors) and the mean p_true / p_chosen inside the eval, log them beside the proxy score, and either delete the GT-node AUC or rename it to what it is - a sanity check that would only move if the head collapsed entirely. Do not keep presenting it as association quality.

BASELINE for comparison: on the dense movie post-NMS-fix, 35 mislinks were 100% affinity-inverted with mean p_true 0.134 vs p_chosen 0.686. A joint run that is genuinely improving association should move those numbers.

title: T>2 needs temporal positional encoding — a wider window alone is order-blind
description:
Supersedes the framing of f5w (T>2 timeframes). Reading the backbone changes the design.

TemporalUNet3D accepts ANY T - the spatial path reshapes to (B*T, ...) and _TemporalAttention is an nn.MultiheadAttention over the T axis - so a wider window RUNS today with no retraining. But that attention has NO temporal positional encoding, which makes it PERMUTATION-INVARIANT over time: the backbone literally cannot tell which frame came first. Order enters the pipeline only later, through the edge transformer's time-fraction node feature (0.0 source / 1.0 target).

CONSEQUENCE: simply widening the window buys APPEARANCE aggregation (smoothing across frames), NOT motion. It therefore does NOT deliver the velocity signal the dense mislink needs - the documented failure is a fast mover whose true successor lands FAR while a slower neighbour sits closer, and disambiguating that requires knowing the direction of time.

THE EXPERIMENT WORTH RUNNING is T>2 WITH temporal positional encoding: add a sinusoidal or learned position over the T axis in _TemporalAttention (or generalise the edge transformer's time fraction from {0,1} to k/(T-1)), then retrain jointly with centred windows (frame n sees n-T/2 .. n+T/2). That is an architecture change plus a retrain, not a window-size flag.

WHY IT IS NOW BETTER MOTIVATED: bidirectional harmonic fusion failed because the disambiguating information is NOT IN THE PAIR - the wrong near neighbour wins in both directions. If it is not in the pair, the remaining place it can be is the motion history, which needs ordered frames. This is the one untried idea that attacks the dense mislink at its root rather than re-weighting it.

title: Train/inference mismatch: detector trained on real pairs, run on duplicated frames
description:
Training and inference feed the detector DIFFERENT distributions, and nobody checked whether it costs anything.

TRAINING (pilkwang's recipe and our JointTrainer): one backbone pass over a REAL pair (t, t+1), with detect_head applied to BOTH frames - two supervised detection losses.
INFERENCE (forward_batch default): each frame is DUPLICATED into a fake pair (t, t), and only features[:, 0] is read.

Because _TemporalAttention is a residual self-attention with no positional encoding, a duplicated pair gives it two identical tokens - it attends to a copy of itself and adds a smoothed version back - whereas a real pair mixes genuine neighbouring information. So the features the head sees at test time are not the features it was trained on.

THE OBJECTION THAT DOES NOT HOLD: "the last frame has no t+1". Slide real pairs across the video and every frame is covered - the final frame as position 1 of the last pair. The model already emits detections for BOTH frames; the shipped path computes the second and throws it away. So the current scheme has two wastes: a discarded output AND a degenerate input, to avoid a problem that does not exist.

EXPERIMENT (free - the shipped path already computes a two-frame window): read out detections from real consecutive pairs instead of duplicates, taking each frame's map from whichever window position covers it, and compare on the proxy. Watch node recall and node count, not just the score.
close_reason: REFUTED - the duplicated frame is DELIBERATE and better. A/B with identical weights: duplicated 0.9334 vs real pair 0.9280 (-0.0054). Backbone temporal attention is residual and has no positional encoding, so a real neighbour smears cellness into the wrong voxels; duplication sharpens. Detection is a per-frame question. The surviving idea (duplicated windows for detection, real pairs for association) lives on w26p.

title: BUG: edge AUC reads 1.0000 always — measured on GT nodes, the easy case
description:
JointTrainer._edge_auc prints exactly 1.0000 at EVERY window, including the init eval of an UNMODIFIED warm-start model. That is not a perfect association head; it is the wrong population.

CAUSE: the val pairs come from PairTarget.enumerate(graph, ...), so the source/target positions are GROUND-TRUTH cell centres. Associating GT nodes is the easy case - our own measurements put the linker at 0.9947 on GT nodes versus ~0.89 on real detections, and the dense-ceiling work located the entire difficulty in the DETECTIONS (crowding, false positives, 60k+ candidates per movie). A ranking metric over ~1200 well-separated annotated nodes is saturated by construction, so it can only ever confirm.

WHY IT MATTERS: it was added precisely to make the association half visible during training, and instead it is a metric that reads 1.0 for a model that has learned nothing. A metric that cannot fail is worse than no metric - it looks like evidence.

OPTIONS: (a) compute the AUC over REAL detections matched to GT (what dense_diagnosis/MislinkSignal already do) - the honest substrate, but it needs a detector pass per eval; (b) drop it, since ModelEvaluator's pipeline score already captures association quality end to end through the real linker; (c) keep it but rename and document it as a GT-node sanity check, valuable only for catching a catastrophic regression (it WOULD fall off 1.0 if the head broke).

LEANING: (c) then (a). It is cheap and it does catch total collapse, but it must stop being presented as "association quality" - that is what the pipeline score measures. Do NOT read the current 1.0000 as evidence the association head is fine.
close_reason: NOT A BUG — resolved by reading the code and its consumer. The AUC reads 1.0000 because it ranks the affinity over GROUND-TRUTH node pairs, where the base rate is ~0.98 and there is ~0.99 candidate per source, so there are no rivals to rank; that is the population trap, and the trainer already documents the metric as a COLLAPSE ALARM rather than an association measure (joint_detector.py:153, EvalResult.edge_auc docstring). The informative instrument it was going to be replaced by ALREADY EXISTS and already runs every window: MislinkSignal reports mislink count, inverted fraction and P_true vs P_chosen on REAL detections through the shipped tracker, riding the eval pass for free. It is measured to move where the AUC cannot (this session: mislinks 64 -> 58, P_true 0.191 -> 0.220 across one window). So the alarm is cheap and covered, and repointing it at detected val pairs would buy a second forward pass per window for a signal we already have. Deleting it would remove a real collapse net. Closed as won't-fix, deliberately.

title: LB arm: flow(boundary=3) + bidirectional — the pairing the coupling evidence points at
description:
CANDIDATE, pending the runtime probe. Today's best proxy number came from a pairing never submitted:

  assignment (shipped)          forward 0.9334
  flow (global, boundary=3)     forward 0.9349
  flow (global, boundary=3)     + bidirectional 0.9353   <- best of the day

All gaps are UNDER the 0.01-0.02 noise floor, so this is not a proxy win and must not be shipped as a default. It earns a SLOT for two reasons that are about class, not magnitude:
1. It is a DECISION-RULE change - the only class that has ever transferred for us (greedy -> global AssignmentLinker was +0.005 on the LB) while every recall-side proxy gain died (NMS flat, smooth anti, node-count anti -0.007).
2. The coupling cross-test says the bidirectional fusion needs a GLOBAL consumer to pay off: the same affinity is -0.0027 under the per-frame assignment linker and +0.0004 under flow. Submitting flow+bidirectional tests the pairing the evidence actually points at, rather than either half alone.

BLOCKER BEING PROBED: FlowLinker imports networkx (pure-Python min-cost flow via network simplex), which is in NEITHER the kit's offline wheels NOR anything verified on the Kaggle image. celltrack-gpu-probe now reports it. If MISSING, add the wheel to the kit before submitting - do not discover it in a submission.
COST: network simplex is ~90s on the 65k-node dense movie, so roughly +6 min of CPU across four videos. Irrelevant next to the 24.5 min the run now takes.
CONFIG: linker.name=flow, linker.disappearance_cost=3, bidirectional_edges=true, on the confirmed base (thr0.97, gate10, bonus20, min7+rescue, smooth0.8).
notes:
WON — LB 0.895, NEW BEST (submission 55407412, kernel v23), beating the previous best 0.892 and +0.004 over its own min7+rescue base (0.891).

This closes the coupling argument with a leaderboard result. Bidirectional fusion ALONE under the per-frame assignment linker measured -0.0027 pooled and -0.0010 on the dense movie it targets — it looked refuted. The claim was that our EdgeTransformerScorer softmaxes over SOURCES, encoding "one parent per target" into the probability itself, so a SYMMETRIC mutual-consistency affinity re-states a constraint the assignment cost already imposes while blunting the directional sharpness it depends on — whereas a GLOBAL solver imposes that constraint explicitly and therefore wants the symmetric affinity. Proxy showed the predicted sign flip (assignment -0.0027 vs flow +0.0004, differential ~0.0031); the LB confirmed it at +0.004.

NOTE the proxy gain was +0.0019, UNDER the noise floor, yet it transferred as +0.004 — consistent with the transfer law that DECISION-RULE changes transfer even when the proxy cannot resolve them (greedy->global was +0.005 while every recall-side proxy gain died).

FOLLOW-UP BUILT (kernel v24, pushed, NOT submitted — last slot of the day held): the same flow+fusion configuration on the CONFIRMED-BEST base (min6, no rescue) instead of min7+rescue, removing a measured -0.001 handicap. Single variable off the 0.895 config.
close_reason: WON: LB 0.895 (55407412) + confirmed on min6 base (55415448). Shipped.

title: BUG: nn/motion/ilp/division linkers silently discard the affinity and its bonus
description:
In celltrack/linkers/linkers.py, _BUILDERS passes `affinity` to every builder, but the builders for nn / motion / ilp / division accept it and DISCARD it, and they never read config.affinity_bonus. Consequences:

- LinkerConfig(name="motion", affinity_bonus=20) is a no-op that reports nothing. Someone sweeping the bonus under those linkers gets a flat curve and would reasonably conclude the bonus does not matter.
- The tracker mounts and COMPUTES the edge affinity (~33% of inference) before handing it to a linker that throws it away - silent wasted work, not just a silent setting.

This is the same class as the three silent-inertness failures found the same day (an invalid machineShape degrading to a P100, mlflow inert since the day it was wired, CellTracker.with_config reusing a stale scorer). Every one type-checked, tested green, and did nothing.

FIX (two different wrongs, two different responses):
1. build(): if an affinity is supplied and the chosen linker does not consume one, log a WARNING naming the linker. Ignoring a mounted affinity is a LEGITIMATE configuration ("use motion, ignore the learned head"), so it must be loud rather than fatal.
2. A validator: if affinity_bonus is EXPLICITLY set (not None) on a linker that cannot read an affinity, RAISE. The user asked for something that cannot happen, and silence there is a lie.

Keep the affinity-reading set beside _BUILDERS so the two cannot drift apart.
close_reason: Fixed: per-knob reader frozensets (_BONUS/_RANKER/_AGREEMENT/_MUTUAL/_MOTION_DISTANCE/_APPEARANCE_READERS) beside _BUILDERS; explicit knob on a non-reading linker now raises.

title: Phase coupling: affinity FORM is chosen by the scorer but determined by the linker
description:
The strategy/interface/implementations/factory pattern for linking ALREADY EXISTS - Linker Protocol (linkers/linking.py), six implementations one per file (assignment, nn, motion, ilp, division, flow), a _BUILDERS name->builder registry, and LinkerConfig(name=) validated against LINKER_NAMES. Do NOT rebuild it. The real gap is different and today's bidirectional experiment exposed it.

(1) SILENT DISCARD - a concrete bug, same class as the three silent-inertness failures found today. In _BUILDERS, the builders for nn / motion / ilp / division accept the `affinity` argument and THROW IT AWAY, and they ignore config.affinity_bonus. So LinkerConfig(name="motion", affinity_bonus=20) is a no-op that reports nothing. Anyone sweeping affinity_bonus under those linkers gets a flat curve and would reasonably conclude the bonus does not matter. Either those linkers should reject an affinity they cannot consume, or the config should refuse the combination - silence is the one option that is wrong.

(2) THE PHASE COUPLING (the architectural point). The affinity's NORMALISATION is chosen in the scorer but presumes the CONSUMER's cost shape:
- Our EdgeTransformerScorer softmaxes over SOURCES, which encodes "one parent per target" into the probability itself, and AssignmentLinker's cost (distance - bonus*P) is built around that asymmetry.
- A constrained lineage ILP imposes one-parent/one-child as explicit global constraints, so it wants a SYMMETRIC, calibrated per-pair affinity and has no use for directional normalisation.
- Bidirectional harmonic fusion produces exactly that symmetric form. Under our assignment linker it measured -0.0027 pooled and -0.0010 on the dense movie it targets; the LB-0.915 bundle that uses it pairs it with an ILP.
So a legal config can pair an affinity FORM with a linker that wants a different one, and nothing in the types says so - you discover it as a small negative number.

PROPOSAL (not yet built): make the coupling explicit rather than adding another factory. Either (a) a linker declares the affinity form it consumes (softmax-over-sources / symmetric / raw) and the scorer produces that form, with a mismatch refused at config time; or (b) the affinity+linker pair is selected TOGETHER as one composite strategy, since they co-vary. (a) is the smaller change and keeps both halves independently swappable; (b) is more honest if it turns out the pairings are few and fixed.

EVIDENCE STILL PENDING: does bidirectional HELP a genuinely global linker? Note FlowLinker at disappearance_cost=0 reduces to AssignmentLinker edge-for-edge (verified again today: flow+forward = 0.9334 = the assignment baseline), so that comparison must be run at a NON-ZERO boundary cost (measured peak 3) or it tests nothing.

title: RESULT: joint warm-start fine-tune (3000 steps, lr 1e-4) does not beat pilkwang
description:
FIRST REAL JOINT RUN, CONTROLLED. Command: python -m celltrack.training.joint_detector --warm-start --steps 3000 --eval-threshold 0.97, on the honest split (191 train / 4 validation / 4 test), selected through the shipped CellTracker.

RESULT - NO IMPROVEMENT:
- init eval (warm-start, untrained) on the VALIDATION four = 0.8474.
- No window of 3000 steps ever beat it. EarlyStop fired at step 2500 (patience 5).
- save-best therefore kept the INIT weights: joint_warm_v1.pt is byte-identical to the pilkwang pack (verified by tensor comparison), while joint_warm_v1.resume.pt holds the step-2500 trained weights (max weight delta 8.9e-3 on unet.encoder_blocks.0.0.weight, so training did move the model - it just moved it the wrong way).
- Cross-check: scoring the checkpoint and a freshly mounted pilkwang pack gave IDENTICAL numbers (0.9100 on the test four, recall 0.993, ratio -0.05), which is how the identity was noticed.

VERDICT: joint warm-start fine-tuning at lr 1e-4, det_weight 1.0, 3000 steps does NOT improve on pilkwang. Consistent with every prior warm-start fine-tune in this campaign (they erode - the published weights already fit these frames, so the gradient pulls away from their optimum). The machinery worked correctly: early stop halted a losing run and save-best preserved the better model.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REFUTE (do not over-generalise from one configuration):
- FROM-SCRATCH joint training (never run) - the warm-start optimum is what is being fought here.
- A much lower learning rate (1e-5/1e-6), which is the standard fix when fine-tuning a converged model degrades it.
- det_weight sweeps - the detection term may be dominating and dragging the association head.
- Longer schedules with cosine decay.

CALIBRATION NOTE worth keeping: the same untrained weights score 0.8474 on the DENSER validation four and 0.9100 on the test four. The denser set is harsher and closer to the true LB (0.892) - more evidence the sparse test four flatter a pipeline via the node-count bonus.
notes:
SUPERSEDED 2026-08-10 — the title states a conclusion that is now FALSE and must not be read alone. "Joint warm-start does not beat pilkwang" is true ONLY at lr 1e-4. The rate was the problem, not the method.
AT lr 1e-5 WITH COSINE DECAY, 3000 steps: validation 0.8414 -> 0.8646 (best at step 2000, node recall 0.966 -> 0.981 with node ratio -0.01, so a genuine detection gain and NOT node-count bonus farming), and on the UNTOUCHED test four 0.9175 vs the 0.9100 the model started from = +0.0075, with recall unchanged, i.e. the gain is ASSOCIATION.
Flat 1e-5 without a schedule reached 0.9085 on the test four - BELOW pilkwang - so the schedule mattered, not merely the lower rate.
WHY 1e-4 FAILED: fine-tuning a CONVERGED model at its original training rate walks off the optimum it already sits in; the run never beat its own init and early stop correctly kept the untrained weights.
STILL TRUE from this bead: the machinery worked (early stop, save-best), and the run was properly controlled.
SEE ALSO: the gain does NOT transfer into the ensemble - fine-tuned models add no diversity from either parent (memory finetuning-adds-no-ensemble-value-2026-08-10).
close_reason: RESULT bead - finding recorded in memory + interpretations, nothing left to do.

title: Synthetic dataset: re-open as an asset, one refutation is not dead
description:
USER DIRECTIVE 2026-08-10: do not infer the synthetic dataset is useless from a single try - least of all one we built ourselves. What was actually refuted, and what was NOT:

REFUTED with mechanism, do not repeat as-is:
(a) lna - fine-tuning the pilkwang EDGE transformer on synthetic pairs with the UNet FROZEN: monotonic dose-damage (20 steps 0.9195, 600 steps 0.9105, vs 0.9270 baseline), worse on every movie, so the synthetic-learned gradient points away from real-optimal.
(b) curriculum synth then real for that same head: 0.9058.
(c) du3 detector-pretrain PRE-GATE: pilkwang already recalls synthetic densely (0.952 at thr 0.99, 0.990 at 0.5), so the cells we miss on real data are real-specific.

WHAT THOSE DO NOT RULE OUT:
1. The JOINT trainer did not exist when (a) and (b) ran. Every refuted arm trained ONE head with the backbone FROZEN, so the features could not adapt. Joint training on synthetic - both heads, real pairs - is a different experiment, and joint is the one retrain axis never refuted.
2. Synthetic carries DENSE edges AND divisions, which is precisely what our real supervision lacks (~1-2 percent of cells annotated). The division term is detection-limited on real data (div_jac 0.0114 vs 0.4468 on GT nodes), and synthetic is the only dense division supervision we have.
3. It is 100 percent labelled, so it can MEASURE what the sparse real annotation cannot: recall vs density, the boundary-truncation bias, association under known crowding. That is an instrument, not only training data - and instruments do not care about domain gap the way trained weights do.
4. The domain gap was diagnosed in the learned TASK (motion calibration: synthetic median 1.86um/frame, persistence 0.3) and NOT in the features (node and background L2 norms matched). Domain-adapting the motion statistics is therefore an untried fix rather than a wall.

DATA: D:/data/volumetric/microscopy/synthetic/biohub_synthetic/{sequences,static}/*.npz - sequences carry volumes (6,64,64,64) uint16, nodes (N,5) as t,z,y,x,id, edges (M,2), divisions, voxel_um_pooled.
GOTCHA that cost a wrong run once: volumes are POOLED to 64^3 but nodes stay in the RAW (64,256,256) grid - divide node y and x by 4, or recall reads as 0.025.

title: docs/architecture/graph.json is missing real import edges at HEAD
description:
FOUND 2026-08-10 while building tools/reachability. The committed architecture record is INACCURATE: at HEAD (0f2331b) graph.json contains edges FROM celltrack.training.tunet_detector but NOT the edge tunet_detector -> celltrack.eval.model_evaluator, although that import plainly exists in the source. Other genuinely-live modules (celltrack.precision, celltrack.eval.model_evaluator, celltrack.data.tunet_dataset, celltrack.detectors.pipeline, celltrack.edges.blended_edge_scoring) also come out unreachable when walking that graph, which contradicts the code.

WHY IT MATTERS: graph.json is described in CLAUDE.md as "the committed, diffable architecture" and "the architecture-erosion record" - a diff we are supposed to review per commit. If it silently omits edges, that record is misleading and any tooling built on it inherits the error (this cost a wrong orphan list twice: first 4 modules, then 18, both wrong). CI runs archmap --check only ADVISORY, so a stale/incomplete graph never fails anything.

SUSPECTS (not yet diagnosed): the pre-commit hook regenerating on commit may race the actual edit; archmap may have run before the final edits of the fold-0 change; or the generator may drop edges under some import form (e.g. a from-import of a symbol rather than a module, or an import inside a TYPE_CHECKING block).

NEXT: reproduce by regenerating (nox -s archmap) on a clean tree and diffing against the committed file - if regeneration ADDS the missing edges, the committed artifact was simply stale and the pre-commit/CI flow needs to be trusted less (consider graduating archmap --check from advisory to enforced). If regeneration STILL omits them, it is a generator bug in the scaffold (devtools is template-owned - fix upstream in sdlc-scaffold, do not hand-edit).

WORKAROUND ALREADY IN PLACE: tools/reachability parses imports from the AST instead of reading graph.json, precisely so a stale artifact cannot produce a confident wrong answer.

title: Observability taxonomy: Obs (live) vs Tracker (cross-run) — both layers were orphaned
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-10 (prompted by the user asking where non-mlflow logging belongs: phase timings for bottlenecks, tqdm, plots, captum). FINDING: the repo already HAS the right two-layer design, fully built and unit-tested, and BOTH layers were wired into nothing.

THE TAXONOMY (one home per concern):
(1) core/obs.py Obs = the LIVE view of THIS run. Obs.setup(logfile) gives console + a PER-EMIT file handler that survives logging.basicConfig(force=True) (torch calls that mid-run and silently kills a normal FileHandler) and writes straight to disk so a long run is TAIL-ABLE - subprocess/uv wrappers buffer child stdout, so a backgrounded run is otherwise invisible until it exits (this cost a 10-minute blind benchmark today). Obs.timed(log,msg) = START/DONE + elapsed, the repo own "basic bottleneck probe". Obs.progress = tqdm with mininterval so file logs stay readable.
(2) core/tracking.py Tracker = the DURABLE CROSS-RUN record. Params, scalar metrics at a step, tags, small artifacts, mlflow UI comparison. Resume-aware: track_run(dir) persists .mlflow_run_id so a resumed run continues the SAME mlflow run.
(3) NEITHER: multi-hundred-MB weights (log the PATH as a tag/param, never artifact them); future figures/attribution (captum bead 5zg, plots) go on disk under the run dir, artifact only if small.

ORPHANS FOUND IN THE SAME AUDIT (all three from the same superseded epoch-loop design):
- celltrack/training/tracked_run.py: a generic EPOCH-loop driver duplicating control flow both step-windowed trainers already implement more richly (resume, heartbeat, ETA). Being deleted.
- core/obs.py Obs: only consumer was tracked_run. Being wired into both trainers instead.
- core/hparams.py RunConfig/DataCfg/AugCfg/OptimCfg/EvalCfg: only remaining production mention is a DOCSTRING in linkers.py. Its DataCfg.fold and two subset fields describe the fold-0 concept just deleted from the repo.

LESSON: an orphan cluster hides in the gap between "built" and "wired" - the repo standing rule (build-and-wire or do not build) needs a periodic grep, because these passed every gate (tests, coverage, vulture at min_confidence 80) while serving nothing.
notes: TRUSTWORTHY ORPHAN LIST (2026-08-10, via the committed tools/reachability, AST-based): 6 unreached modules - celltrack.data.crops, celltrack.data.targets, celltrack.training.tracked_run, core.data.split, core.hparams, core.metrics.recall. Two earlier lists (4 and 18) were WRONG because they trusted docs/architecture/graph.json, which is missing real edges at HEAD (separate bead). NOTE core.data.split: the fold-0 rip kept Acquisitions on the grounds that by_prefix is "still used by StratifiedSplit and the dataset_facts E2E" - but StratifiedSplit lives INSIDE that same module (self-reference, not external demand) and dataset_facts is a TEST. So it is production-dead by the honest definition; that self-referential justification is exactly the trap the tool exists to catch. Also celltrack.data.targets is orphaned only BECAUSE crops is - it is imported by crops alone, so its fate follows that judgement. Each of the 6 needs the KEEP / CONSOLIDATE / DELETE judgement (consolidate-before-deleting rule), NOT an automatic delete.

title: ORPHAN: TrackedRun + mlflow built and tested but wired into NO trainer
description: FOUND 2026-08-10 by grep: celltrack/training/tracked_run.py (TrackedRun) and core/tracking.py (the mlflow backend, with a CELLTRACK_NO_MLFLOW opt-out) exist, are unit-tested, and are imported by NOTHING in the production path — grep count of 'TrackedRun|mlflow' in celltrack/training/tunet_detector.py = 0 and in joint_detector.py = 0. mlflow is a DECLARED runtime dependency serving nothing. Built in 4aa6452 ('EarlyStop + TrackedRun — the tracked epoch-loop core'); EarlyStop from that same commit WAS wired into both trainers, TrackedRun was not. This is the exact anti-pattern the repo has a standing rule against (memory feedback-build-and-wire-or-dont: an abstraction's value is realised only when the shipped path uses it; never leave a better layer unwired 'for later'). CONSEQUENCE (this is the real cost, not tidiness): every run's numbers live in stdout and die with the terminal. There is no queryable cross-run record in a campaign whose entire method is comparing runs — no way to ask 'what did the joint run at det_weight=2 score vs 1', no param/metric history, no artifact link to the saved weights. WIRE IT: both trainers' train() should open a TrackedRun, log the config as params and each eval window's metrics (proxy score, node recall, node ratio, edge AUC, train loss terms, it/s), and record the saved checkpoint path. Do it BEFORE the next long run — an unrecorded run wastes the wall-clock it costs. Check first whether TrackedRun's RunConfig/loop shape actually fits a step-windowed trainer (it was written for an epoch loop) and adapt rather than bolt on. If it genuinely does not fit, either reshape it or delete it + drop the mlflow dep — orphan or wired, not both.
notes: LARGELY RESOLVED 2026-08-10. Tracker (mlflow) and Obs are now WIRED into both trainers and proxy_eval: TrainingRun logs params/metrics/tags per eval window at step=done, Obs.setup gives a tail-able per-run log beside the weights, Obs.timed wraps the coarse phases, Obs.progress the 191-video walk. Two silent failures fixed en route - mlflow had been INERT since the day it was written (enable_system_metrics_logging sets a flag, then every start_run raised because psutil is absent, swallowed by the never-break-a-run guard), and the __main__ logger sat outside the celltrack tree so every 'python -m' entrypoint logged into the void. Tracker._disabled now warns once instead of vanishing. REMAINING under this title: TrackedRun itself is still unwired - deliberately KEPT, not deleted, because it is a generic loop driver the two hand-rolled trainer loops duplicate; consolidating them onto it is the DRY-correct end state and is tracked in yoz9 (orphan judgements).

title: Kernel v20 pushed: first run with fp16 autocast + multi-GPU T4x2 dispatch
description: Kernel celltrack-dualseed-assign-affinity-stlf6 v20 pushed 2026-08-10. CONFIG (forward, not a revert): thr0.97 gate10 bonus20 min_track_length=7 + ShortTrackRescueConfig + smooth0.8 — same probe as the still-PENDING v18/55398573, now carrying the new infra. INFRA UNDER TEST (both expected score-NEUTRAL): (1) fp16 autocast on BOTH GPU stages (proxy-verified 0.9334 vs 0.9334, dscore -0.0000; bf16 REJECTED at 0.9309 — inference wants mantissa, training wants range); (2) MultiGpuSubmission over Kaggle's T4x2 (exact by construction: one device per video, identical code) — machine_shape had to be fixed from NvidiaTeslaT4 to NvidiaTeslaT4x2 or it would have been silently INERT. WHAT TO READ FROM THE RUN: (a) the dispatch log line 'dispatching N videos over [devices]' confirms it actually got 2 GPUs; (b) per-video stage timings (detect/affinity/link+post) now logged; (c) total runtime vs the ~6-7h baseline (expect ~2x from dispatch, plus the T4 fp16 tensor-core gain on the 88% that is GPU work); (d) score should land at the min7+rescue number, NOT a new one — a score change indicts the infra. SUBMIT WHEN COMPLETE: .venv/Scripts/kaggle.exe competitions submit -c biohub-cell-tracking-during-development -k dimiturnt/celltrack-dualseed-assign-affinity-stlf6 -v 20 -f submission.csv -m 'min7+rescue on fp16 + T4x2 dispatch'. DO NOT WAIT on Kaggle (hours).
notes:
ARM-DESIGN CAVEAT, recorded honestly (2026-08-10). The base for v21/v22/v23 is min7+rescue, which has now scored LB 0.891 - BELOW the confirmed-best 0.892 (min6, no rescue). So all three arms measure their deltas on a slightly worse foundation than necessary. They remain interpretable as single-variable deltas AGAINST v21 (same base), which is what they were built for, but a positive result on any of them would need re-testing on the min6 base before shipping as a default.

THE MISTAKE: I anchored on the NEWEST config rather than the BEST-MEASURED one, at a moment when the newest was still pending and therefore unproven. Anchor an arm on a number you already have, not on one you are waiting for - otherwise a pending result silently becomes a dependency of every arm built after it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LAST SLOT: hold it until v21/v22 land. If boundary rescue shows a gain on the min7 base, the follow-up is boundary rescue on the min6 base (isolating it on the confirmed-best config). Spending the slot before those land would be a guess, and the directive is measured submissions.
close_reason: ANSWERED 2026-08-10. The question this tracked - does fp16 + multi-GPU dispatch change the score - is settled on the HIDDEN SET, not the proxy: 55398573 (min7+rescue, pre-infra) and 55405539 (identical config + fp16 + 2xT4) both scored 0.891. The infra is score-neutral and the ~2x speed work is free. Kernel log confirmed both devices in use ('dispatching 4 videos over [cuda:0, cuda:1]', 2 videos each) at 24.5 min total. En route: machine_shape 'NvidiaTeslaT4x2' is INVALID and degrades silently to a P100 (sm_60), which the base torch refuses hours later - 'NvidiaTeslaT4' already provisions both T4s. Arm-anchoring lesson recorded: these arms were built on the min7+rescue base, which then scored 0.891, BELOW the confirmed 0.892 - anchor on a number you already have, not one you are waiting for.

title: Wire joint trainer eval to ModelEvaluator (both heads) + log edge-AUC
description: DEPENDS ON: the ModelEvaluator (agent A, LB-aligned CellTracker eval on the 4-movie proxy) + edge_auc metric (agent B). The joint trainer (celltrack/training/joint_detector.py) currently selects checkpoints on VAL-LOSS - a different bias than the detector trainer's motion-linker (both non-shipped-metric). Once ModelEvaluator lands: wire the JOINT model's eval to score BOTH trained heads through a CellTracker (mount the trained detector AS the BlendDetectorScorer AND the trained edge transformer AS the BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer, not pilkwang's) on the 4-movie proxy = the full own-model LB-aligned score, replacing val-loss selection. Also log edge-AUC (agent B's metric) per window so association quality is visible. This is the joint-trainer half of the training<->eval unification (agent A does the detector half). Result: both trainers select on the metric that transfers.
close_reason: DONE 2026-08-10: JointTrainer now selects on ModelEvaluator's LB-aligned pipeline score with BOTH trained heads mounted (TemporalUNetDetector.of + EdgeTransformerScorer.of, wrapped as a one-member logit blend), EarlyStop direction flipped to higher-is-better, and edge AUC logged per window. Caveat recorded separately: that AUC is measured on GT-node pairs and reads 1.0000 always - bead jpy8 wires MislinkSignal, the instrument that can actually fail.

title: Unify training-eval with the real CellTracker pipeline (common code, LB-aligned selector)
description: User: training + eval should share more code. THEY DIVERGE: the detector trainer's in-loop eval (_FoldEval in tunet_detector.py) scores with LinkerConfig(name='motion') + ShortTrackFilter + LinefitSmoother - a MOTION linker + simple postproc. The real/proxy pipeline (proxy_eval -> CellTracker) uses the AssignmentLinker + edge affinity + bridge + rescue + smooth. So the training checkpoint SELECTOR is NOT the shipped pipeline -> it under-reflects the detector (cdg's 0.837 motion-fold-eval vs 0.893 real-pipeline 4-movie proxy for the SAME weights). FIX: make the training eval score the detector through the SAME CellTracker (mount trained detector as BlendDetectorScorer + edge affinity + AssignmentLinker, like scratchpad/cdg_proxy_eval.py did) = common code with proxy_eval + an LB-ALIGNED selector (picks the checkpoint that's best on the metric that transfers). TRADEOFF: full-pipeline eval per window is slower than the motion linker + needs the edge affinity mounted; make eval_every coarse. This is the 'training and eval common code' + fixes a real bias (selecting detectors on a non-shipped metric).

title: Speed the Kaggle T4 eval kernel (6-7h, compute-bound): batched inference + inference-compile
description: The submission kernel takes 6-7 HOURS on T4 = compute-bound (NOT just scoring-queue lag). ~10 UNet forwards/frame: dual-seed detection (2 seeds x 4-fold TTA=8) + edge affinity (2 seeds forward each consecutive pair), all FRAME-BY-FRAME (detectors/tunet.py _response loops one frame). T4 starved by batch=1. LEVERS (apply our training work to inference): (1) BATCHED INFERENCE - stack N frames per forward in _response (+ the edge-affinity pair forwards). NUMERICALLY IDENTICAL (batch=same per-frame forward) -> LB-safe, verify bitwise locally. Biggest win, T4 even more starved than 5090 was (3.6x-class). (2) INFERENCE-COMPILE on T4: Kaggle=Linux=stock triton, inference=no backward so the SDPA-backward bug doesn't apply, static 64^3 -> clean compile ~1.3-1.8x. Needs numerical-equiv check. Both STACK -> 6-7h -> ~2-3h. RISKY (separate A/B, don't default): TTA 4->2/0 halves detection forwards but TTA is a recall lever -> may cost score. channels_last+fp16 already in kernel. Rebuild kit + push to test on real T4. Supersedes the inference-compile note on the compile-followup bead.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-10 (per-stage timing now in CellTracker.run, commit): 5090, dual-seed thr0.97, fresh forward (EphemeralResponseStore = the kernel path). DENSE 6bba_05db0fb1 (74340 nodes): detect 11.4s (55%) | affinity 6.9s (33%) | link+post 2.3s (11%) | TOTAL 20.6s. SPARSE 44b6_0113de3b (25828 nodes): 11.3 / 6.4 / 0.3 | TOTAL 18.0s. CONCLUSIONS: (1) ~88% of inference is GPU work (detection 2 seeds x 4-fold TTA + affinity 2 seeds), videos are INDEPENDENT -> MULTI-GPU VIDEO DISPATCH is THE lever (Kaggle offers T4 x2 -> ~2x, 6-7h -> ~3-3.5h). Building now: one worker process per device, each rebuilds CellTracker.ephemeral(pack1,pack2,device,config) on its shard, parent merges to one CSV; device list is a PARAM (1 local / 2 Kaggle / N). (2) GPU COST-MATRIX OFFLOAD REFUTED BEFORE BUILDING: linking is NOT slow - 11% of the worst movie, 1.7% of sparse - so moving the cdist/cost-matrix build to GPU has a <=11% ceiling even if linking went to ZERO. Not worth the VRAM-budget complexity (would also need free-VRAM probing since PC 32GB is often training, T4/laptop smaller). The Hungarian solve (scipy linear_sum_assignment) is sequential = bad GPU fit anyway. (3) Batched inference ALSO refuted earlier (0.70x, non-bitwise). REMAINING after multi-GPU: inference-compile on T4 (Linux stock triton, no backward, static shape, ~1.3-1.8x on the 88%) - stacks with multi-GPU. TTA-reduction stays risky (recall lever, A/B only).
close_reason: DONE + MEASURED 2026-08-10. Kernel now runs 24.5 min with fp16 autocast on both GPU stages and MultiGpuSubmission over both T4s (log: dispatching 4 videos over ['cuda:0','cuda:1']). Score-neutrality PROVEN on the hidden set, not assumed: 55398573 (pre-infra) and 55405539 (same config + fp16 + 2xT4) both scored 0.891. Two proposals refuted en route: batched inference (0.70x SLOWER, non-bitwise) and GPU cost-matrix offload (<=11% ceiling - linking is 11% of a video, not the bottleneck). Remaining unexploited: inference-compile on the T4 (filed in the interpretation doc).

title: Weight registry: structured layout + training-setup tag + MLflow (traceability)
description: Today weights save to the data root (gitignored, correct) but FLAT with ad-hoc names (detector_tunet_scratch_fast.pt etc), no structure, no SETUP tag. save_checkpoint records arch shape + recipe (downsample/tta) but NOT the training setup (detection-only vs joint, T=2 vs single-frame) -> a detection-only detector could be misgrafted where a joint one is expected (the 'wrong-architecture course-correction' risk). DECISIONS/PLAN: (1) keep weights in data root NOT repo (binaries out of git); (2) structured layout weights/<setup>/<run-id>/best.pt + a manifest (config, setup, metric, git-SHA) for traceability + pruning; (3) tag checkpoint with training setup so from_pack/graft can CHECK compatibility before use; (4) unify the trainer with TrackedRun for MLflow experiment+artifact registry (proper 'connected to architecture', metadata not physical adjacency). Conditions today: save-best on score>=best + .resume.pt every window (both fine, keep). Do with the joint trainer (which needs MLflow anyway).

title: Gradient checkpointing — bigger batch/model on the 5090 (enables T>2 + bigger nets)
description: torch.utils.checkpoint on the U-Net blocks: recompute activations in backward instead of storing -> training VRAM drops (currently ~30/32GB at batch8) -> bigger batch OR bigger model. Nuance: the T4 is the INFERENCE/eval GPU (no backward) so checkpointing is a TRAINING-side lever; but it lets us TRAIN a bigger model on the 5090, whose INFERENCE (forward-only, smaller) usually still fits T4 16GB. Pairs with the T>2 temporal-window bead (T inflates activation memory ~linearly). Trade: ~20-30% slower training for the memory. Wire as an opt-in --grad-checkpoint flag on the trainer.
notes: MEASURED 2026-08-10 - REFUTED FOR SPEED, REFRAMED FOR CAPACITY. Batch/VRAM/throughput curve (5090, bf16, single_frame, 64^3): 8=5.0GB/62.9fps, 16=10.0GB/64.8, 32=20.0GB/65.6, 48=27.7GB/66.9, 64=thrash 15.7. Throughput FLAT (+6% over a 6x batch increase) while VRAM scales linearly 0.62GB/sample -> COMPUTE-BOUND not memory-bound. Gradient checkpointing costs ~30% compute to buy memory that buys <=6% -> net LOSS for speed. ALSO: checkpointing is training-only (recomputes activations in backward) so it does nothing for T4 INFERENCE - the original 'bigger models on the T4 we use for eval' rationale is void. WHAT REMAINS VALID: checkpointing to fit a BIGGER MODEL (capacity = a score lever, untested). Rescope this bead to that, or close it. Practical takeaways landed: keep batch_size=8, cap at ~32 (48 sits at 87% VRAM, one step from a 4x thrash cliff).

title: Training speed: cheap wins (bf16 autocast, TF32, eval cadence)
description: Main detector trainer tunet_detector.py runs batch=1 single-frame at ~5.3 it/s. Land safe speed/correctness wins: (1) autocast dtype=bfloat16 (currently defaults fp16 with NO GradScaler = latent underflow bug; Blackwell 5090 prefers bf16); (2) torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('high') for TF32 matmuls; (3) eval_every default 250->500 (full-frame+TTA subset eval runs synchronous with training, can be ~half wall-time). channels_last_3d skipped (channel=1 outer dim, needs care inside temporal forward).
close_reason: bf16+TF32+eval-cadence landed, ruff+10 tests green

title: Wire or consolidate orphaned detectors.py (DetectorConfig factory) — threshold-baked mismatch with CellTracker
description: ORPHAN SCAN (2026-08-05): celltrack/detectors.py (DetectorConfig registry: pilktunet/ourstunet/unetaug/dog, bp3) has ZERO non-test importers — no kernel, no eval, nothing constructs through it. Built-not-wired anti-pattern. ROOT MISMATCH diagnosed: DetectorConfig.build returns a _ScorerDetector whose Detector contract BAKES the threshold (nodes(video_key, path)), but the shipped CellTracker sweeps threshold as an operating point (detector.nodes(video_key, path, threshold), varied by with_config without rebuilding/re-caching). Also DetectorConfig._blend hardcodes ResponseCache (disk) so it can't serve the kernel's EphemeralResponseStore (no-disk) path. RESOLUTION (recommended = WIRE, it DRYs 4 inline BlendDetectorScorer constructions in tracker.from_packs/kernel/edge_finetune + generalizes detector as a strategy like the linker): refactor DetectorConfig to (a) NOT bake threshold — return the scorer, threshold applied at nodes() call time, matching CellTracker; (b) accept a ResponseStore (or store factory) so both the disk-cache local path and the ephemeral kernel path construct through it. Then CellTracker.from_packs + kernel + edge_finetune build the detector via DetectorConfig(name='pilktunet'). Keep the dog/unetaug/ourstunet builders as available registry options (like the linker family). ALTERNATIVE if wiring proves unjustified: consolidate the pilktunet builder into tracker construction + delete the speculative alt-detector builders (they serve detectors the edge-coupled CellTracker can't use). Do NOT leave it orphaned.
close_reason: Consolidated (removed): 0 importers, pilktunet builder duplicated CellTracker.from_packs, alt-detector builders were speculative-unused (every underlying detector is directly constructible). Deleted detectors.py + test; the only unique capability (config-driven detector name-dispatch) had no consumer = speculation. Resolves the built-not-wired orphan.

title: Check bridge_reach_um vs linker gate self-consistency (possible under-reach bias)
description: DensityGapBridge reach_um=bridge_reach_um defaults 10 = the linker gate_um (max SINGLE-frame displacement, i0a-derived 9.96um). But the gap bridge reconnects a 1-frame GAP = a cell traveling across TWO frames (t-1 -> t+1, the dropout at t), so its reach should be ~2x single-frame max (~20um), not 1x. If 10um is too short, real 2-frame-gap reconnections are being missed = a subtle recall bias on the bridge stage. Measured test: sweep bridge_reach_um {10,14,20} on the proxy (per-movie, watch dense + sparse 44b6 where dropouts matter). If 20 helps without over-bridging, derive reach = 2*gate (self-balancing, removes the magic 10). If flat, document 10 as physically-argued and keep. Cheap proxy arm.
close_reason: Refuted by reading (observe-before-change): DensityGapBridge predicts end+2*velocity (full 2-frame motion); reach_um caps the PREDICTION ERROR not the span, and is further capped by the Voronoi half-spacing (dominates in crowding). 10um = one-frame motion gate = correct max prediction error. Raising it admits false bridges, not recall. Not a bias.

title: Test divaug tophat 2-UNet detector for no-response cell recovery (only untested detection lever)
description: Data analysis 2026-08-04 proved the ~1.3-2.6% detection recall gap on harder videos (6bba_fc83837d 0.9739, 969618f6 0.9867) is IRREDUCIBLE no-response cells - flat across threshold 0.95-0.995, detector gives NO peak at any threshold (crowd-buried at (1,4,4) res). pilkwang-family detectors (slw DeepCenter, ksv retrain, fcd TTA, 884 cellpose) all refuted for recall - same family/response. The ONE untested lever with a DIFFERENT mechanism: xiaoleilian/biohub-ct-mix-divaug's 2-UNet ensemble unet3d_bright.pt (raw) + unet3d_traintophat.pt (TOPHAT morphological preproc). Tophat responds to different structures than raw intensity -> MIGHT fire on cells raw-intensity pilkwang misses. Weights public in 'biohub-unet3d-weights' Kaggle dataset (mountable). TEST: download weights, port their UNet3D arch + tophat preproc (model code in scratchpad/kaggle_nb/xiaoleilian_biohub-ct-mix-divaug), run on the 4 hard CV videos, measure COMPLEMENTARY GT recall vs pilkwang blend@0.99 (like slw/ksv probes, now via ChampionPipeline). GATE: if it recovers no-response GT cells the pilkwang detector misses (comp>0 on fc83837d) -> real detection lever, union into ensemble; else confirms detection ceiling is resolution-limited (pack needs assets we lack). Medium integration (~30-45min: their model class + tophat + mount). This is the last detection avenue before concluding pilkwang-detector + threshold caps us at ~0.908-tier and 0.93+ pack needs higher-res/better detector we don't have.
notes: BLOCKED (external asset, 2026-08-04): the divaug weights unet3d_bright.pt + unet3d_traintophat.pt live in xiaoleilian's PRIVATE 'biohub-unet3d-weights' dataset — kaggle datasets files/download both 403 (kernels pull of the notebook itself works, so it's private-dataset gating not auth).
