PORT-READY though: extracted their full recipe from the pulled notebook (scratchpad/kaggle_nb/xiaoleilian_divaug/biohub-ct-mix-divaug.ipynb): UNet3D(base=24, 3-level, _block=2x[Conv3d3p1+BN+ReLU], out=Conv3d(base,1,1)); preproc pool_xy(POOL=4 XY-mean) then optional tophat p-=grey_opening(size=(1,7,7)) clip>=0, then percentile-norm 50/99.5 clip -0.5..6.0 (SAME as pilkwang); peak UNET_THRESH=0.15 + physical NMS 4.0um + centroid _refine; SCALE=[1.625,.40625,.40625], (1,4,4) downsample. Two models averaged. REMAINING PATH = train this arch+tophat on OUR data ourselves (a retrain, multi-hour, uncertain, loses their division-aug advantage) = a different heavier task, not this cheap probe. fql-as-probe is dead until the weights become public.

title: Test Ultrack global-over-time tracker on dense (the un-refuted linker lever)
description: e9b lever 2 (track-level global-over-time optimization) is the ONLY un-refuted dense lever after slw/ksv/fcd/e9b/lna/884/trackastra all refuted detection+per-frame-linker paths. Ultrack (Nature Methods 2025, Royer lab, developmental-tested, installed as 0.7.2, uses CBC MIP not SCIP so may dodge our Kaggle-SCIP blocker) does hierarchical candidate SEGMENTATION SELECTION + global ILP — its hierarchy could split crowded touching nuclei that our fixed-detection per-frame Hungarian mislinks. PROPER feed: Tracker.track(config, foreground=detector_prob_volume, contours=1-prob or gradient), to_tracks_layer -> TrackGraph, score dense 6bba_05db0fb1 edge-jaccard vs champion 0.86. GATE: beat 0.86 by >0.02 to justify the Kaggle CBC-offline-wheel build + a submission slot. RISK/EV: dense-ceiling capstone caps global-opt at ~+1.8% dense edge-jac (40% conflict subset; 60% signal-wrong) = ~+0.005-0.008 pooled, within LB overshoot noise — but Ultrack's re-segmentation is a different mechanism that may exceed the fixed-detection estimate. Point-feed (our peaks as labels) reduces to existing global assignment (like Trackastra which LOST 0.45 on dense) — must use the foreground+contours hierarchy feed. Time-box: local dense-slice smoke first (cost-tier). Harness pattern: like the trackastra probe.
close_reason: Ultrack infeasible as drop-in: watershed hierarchy needs full-res cell-sized regions, our (1,4,4)-downsampled nuclei (~1-6 voxels) too small ('Region too small' error). Proper use = full-res instance-seg rebuild (16x compute, breaks isotropy downsample). Global-linking concept survives only as hand-rolled min-cost-flow, capstone EV ~+0.005 = not worth it.

NOTE: my earlier 'warm-start erodes' finding was CONFOUNDED (fine-tuned with detection-only objective = wrong recipe); continuing with the correct joint objective should NOT erode. CAVEAT: gains only measurable on hidden LB — our fold-0 val is 93% leaked into pilkwang train, so local fold-0 can't show warm-start improvement. Parent 80e/cdg.

title: Temporal multi-frame ourstunet trainer (the only from-scratch tier-avenue)
description: From-scratch SINGLE-frame recipe refuted at ~0.69 ceiling (ourstunet-from-scratch-ceiling memory). The measured gap to pilkwang 0.877 is architectural: their detector is TEMPORAL (multi-frame window attention), ours trains one frame at a time. A genuinely-ours tier detector needs a multi-frame trainer (window W=2 fake-pair -> real temporal batch), + cosine-lr (nan past 40k on flat lr) + more epochs. Only avenue with a mechanism to reach tier; do NOT retry single-frame.
close_reason: Superseded: we are running their ACTUAL train_unet_transformer.py (joint temporal recipe) on our fold-0-clean — no need for a separate reimpl. Tracked under cdg.

title: Train a second seed for the dual-seed logit blend
description: The frontier averages logits from two TemporalUNet3D checkpoints (50ep pack + seed314159) before the sigmoid. Once we can train or fine-tune one detector, a second seed is nearly free and is the cheapest ensemble available. Deliberately gated behind the fine-tune task: worthless until a single seed of ours reaches tier.
acceptance_criteria: Blended fold-0 measured against single-seed fold-0; kept only if it moves.

description: No documented/scripted path from D:/data/.../raw to processed OME-zarr (with image_statistics.quantiles + multiscales). tools/ has rechunk (processed->rechunked) + derive_scale only. Also document pilkwang pack provenance (reference/pilkwang was copied from a Kaggle support pack). Needed for reproducibility on a fresh machine.

description: Add gap-close (bridge a track across a 1-frame detection miss) after linefit; the 0.857 NB3 recipe has it, we do not. New S3 token stlfg. Eval dog-motion-stlfg + pilktunet-motion-stlfg fold-0.

title: Random-rectangle crop augmentation (input regularization, stride-aligned)
description: Vary crop position AND size (currently fixed (16,64,64)+jitter) so the detector cannot memorize a fixed framing = input regularization. Sizes must be stride-aligned (z%2, y%8, x%8). Batching needs same-size-per-batch (bucket by size or pad). Test vs fixed-crop baseline.

title: Tiled inference (stitch prob map, peak globally) + stride-aligned crops
description: IF a frame stops fitting VRAM (does not at w64), spatial-tile: forward cubes with halo overlap >= receptive field, write each into a full-frame probability volume (average overlaps), then NMS/peak-pick ONCE on the global map. Boundary cells detected once, in global coords; tracking is already global so unaffected. Crops/tiles MUST be stride-aligned (z%2, y%8, x%8 for strides ((1,2,2),(1,2,2),(2,2,2))).

title: Explicit 80/10/10 train/val/test split (drop fold framing)
description: Replace the single fold-0 80/20 with an explicit 3-way train/val/test partition, stratified by prefix, deterministic by filename hash. Train=random-crop pool, val=per-epoch crop metric, test=final full-pipeline tracking-score (one test script). User is fine with 80/10/10 (or 90/10); no k-fold CV.
design: test=2/prefix (4 total, mirrors competition test size, LB-predictive), val=1/prefix (2 total, both acquisitions so metric means something), train=rest (~193). Deterministic by blake2b(filename) rank — same split every run, no seed. Per-epoch val = crop metric (fast); test = full tracking-score at end.

description: Save model checkpoint each epoch (mlflow artifact + weights file); support resume/continue training from a checkpoint. Enables warm-start and interrupt-resume. Note: warm-start is only valid when input distribution is unchanged (per CLAUDE.md) — a background-crops or objective change should train fresh.

title: Operating-point sweep: N_pred/N_total against realised score
description:
The adjustment ratio is signed and uncapped above, so predicting FEWER nodes than the estimated true
count multiplies the jaccard by more than 1 (up to 1.1). Detecting every cell earns exactly 1.0.

That argument is arithmetic on the formula, not an experiment. Sweep the detector's threshold across
N_pred/N_total and measure the realised score, per prefix - the aggregation weights each video by
its own TP+FP+FN, so the bonus is worth most where annotation is densest (6bba), which is also where
N_total is smallest and the ratio moves fastest.

DONE WHEN: the sweep curve is in an interpretations/ note with the chosen operating point and the
reason, including whether the bonus survives the edge FNs that under-detection causes.
close_reason: Sweep DONE-WHEN met with learned detector + NN linker: curve recorded, operating point ~1.0, under-detection (0.5x) collapses score (0.24/0.30) so the node-count bonus does NOT survive edge FNs. Force-closed past the cdo dependency — the curve stands for the current pipeline; re-running with the learned linker after cdo is a refinement. Surfaced: learned recall beats classical but end-to-end score (~0.45-0.48) < classical floor (~0.56); recall != score. See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_operating-point-sweep.md.

title: Detection model: 3D U-Net with temporal context
description:
Per-voxel detection map over an anisotropic volume, cell centres recovered by local-maximum
suppression with an NMS radius derived from the physics (voxel spacing + measured cell scale), not
tuned by hand.

Anisotropy is 4x: an isotropic kernel in index space is an ellipsoid in the tissue. Either use
anisotropic kernels/strides or resample - decide with an argument, and record it.

DONE WHEN: detection recall against the annotated nodes beats the classical detector from the
bracket task at a matched node count, on the held-out prefix split.
close_reason: Learned anisotropy-aware 3D U-Net beats the classical floor's recall at matched node count on held-out fold 0, both prefixes: 44b6 0.656->0.766, 6bba 0.664->0.742. Trained 40 videos/2000 steps, masked MSE 0.040->0.006, no tuning. Single-run/2-videos-per-prefix; direction credible (both acquisitions agree). See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_detection-beats-floor.md.

title: Linking model: candidate generation plus learned scoring
description:
Candidates are generated with a radius that covers the measured motion tail (median 1.82 um/frame,
p99 8.38, max 60.8) - deliberately WIDER than the 7 um matching cutoff, so the scorer has real
competitors to discriminate rather than a single obvious partner. Then a learned pairwise score over
consecutive frames, resolved into a one-to-one assignment (plus the two-child case at divisions).

DONE WHEN: it beats nearest-neighbour linking on ground-truth nodes - i.e. it exceeds the ceiling
from the bracket task, which is exactly the number nearest-neighbour cannot pass.
close_reason: Division-aware linker beats NN on GT nodes: edge Jaccard 0.9980 > 0.9976, and decisively on full score 1.1222 > 1.0884 via the division term (NN div_jaccard=0, structural; division-aware 0.333). Composes NN one-to-one then attaches unmatched daughters to nearest matched parent within a tight 7um division radius (=matching cutoff; wider gates add false divisions). Exceeds the bracket ceiling = DONE-WHEN. Note: real score bottleneck is detection jitter, not GT-node linking (see operating-point-sweep). See interpretations/tracking/2026-07-23_division-linking.md.

title: Training harness: crop sampling, masked supervision, tracking
description:
The data loader and run scaffolding both models sit on. Samples (T, Z, Y, X) crops from the zarr
stores (one timepoint per chunk, so temporal windows are the natural read unit), applies the
quantile normalisation the stores ship, and carries the annotation mask.

The masked supervision is the load-bearing part: ground truth is hand-followed lineages covering
~6% of cells, so an unlabelled bright blob is a real cell, not background. Unlabelled positives must
be excluded from the loss rather than scored as negatives.

DONE WHEN: a smoke run trains for a few hundred steps on a handful of videos, logs to MLflow, and
the mask demonstrably zeroes the gradient on unannotated regions (asserted in a test).
close_reason: Training harness complete: CropSampler + DetectionTarget (masked supervision: positive near centres, negative in dark tissue, EXCLUDED for bright-unlabelled) + MaskedDetectionLoss + DetectionUNet + DetectionTrainer. DONE-WHEN met: smoke run 300 steps/4 real videos on GPU, loss 0.052->0.004, logged to MLflow; mask-zeroes-gradient pinned in a unit test. 14 tests, gates green.

title: Daughter-persistence fork ranking REFUTED — long-lived daughters are worse division candidates, not better
description:
Built SurvivingDaughterRanking: a decorator penalising a proposed daughter that does not survive as a track, normalised by the tracker's own min_track_length over the reachable span (1 to L). Rationale: a real mitosis leaves two lineages that persist, a false fork grafts a fragment.

MEASURED at IDENTICAL gates and identical fork counts (1072 forks both arms, so only WHICH forks changed), test four, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional, v26 division config:
  symmetry only          edge 0.9243  div 0.0294  clamped 0.9259
  symmetry + persistence edge 0.9212  div 0.0263  clamped 0.9225
BOTH terms fell. Refuted.

MECHANISM, visible in the edge column and the opposite of my prior: preferring a long-lived daughter means grafting a track that survives ON ITS OWN — a real independent cell the linker correctly left unparented (it entered the field or appeared) — onto a parent. That costs edge jaccard AND finds fewer true divisions. A SHORT-lived orphan is the better division candidate.

NOT chasing the sign flip: inverting the term is a post-hoc fit to a proxy holding three annotated divisions, and it would amount to performing the component-merge rescue deliberately, which measured ~free (0.0006 for 157 forks) rather than positive.

Code KEPT: default off, byte-identical when off, composes with any ranking as a decorator rather than a fourth ranking. What is refuted is the USE.
close_reason: Refuted and documented in full: both the edge and division terms fell at identical fork counts (0.9259 -> 0.9225 clamped), with the mechanism identified (a long-lived daughter is an independently real cell the linker correctly left unparented; a SHORT-lived orphan is the better candidate). Code kept default-off as a composable decorator. Nothing left to do — the sign flip is deliberately not being chased, since it would be a post-hoc fit to a proxy holding three annotated divisions.

title: Orphan judgements: all six are KEEP or CONSOLIDATE, none delete
description:
Judgements for the six modules tools/reachability reports as unreached, under the consolidate-before-deleting rule. NONE is a delete. Recording WHY, because unwired code without a recorded reason decays into either cargo or an accidental deletion.

KEEP - celltrack/data/crops.py (CropSampler, TrainingCrop). Offers anchored sub-volume sampling, anchor jitter, flips, multi-timepoint windows. Unused because the live FrameDataset trains on WHOLE 64^3 frames, where anchoring solves nothing (a full frame contains all its annotations, so there is no empty-crop problem). But that is true ONLY because of the (1,4,4) downsample. The campaign's own conclusion is that the remaining gap is RESOLUTION, and finer-resolution training is exactly where a full frame stops fitting and anchored cropping becomes mandatory. Deleting it means rebuilding it the moment we act on our own diagnosis.

KEEP - celltrack/data/targets.py (DetectionTarget, _gaussian_peaks, supervised_fraction). Builds GAUSSIAN HEATMAP supervision; the live path uses hard voxel targets under BalancedBCE. That is a genuinely different supervision form we have never tested, and it is NOT the label smoothing we refuted (smoothing capped the positive target at 0.95 and destroyed peak sharpness; a Gaussian peak keeps a sharp maximum with a soft skirt). supervised_fraction is also the only thing that measures how much of a volume carries supervision. Orphaned only because crops.py is - it has no other importer.

KEEP/CONSOLIDATE - celltrack/training/tracked_run.py (TrackedRun). A generic loop driver duplicating control flow BOTH step-windowed trainers hand-roll. The DRY-correct end state is to extend it (resume, heartbeat/ETA, step-windowed indexing) and drive both trainers through it - a control-flow rewrite of two loops, deliberately not attempted next to a GPU run.

KEEP/CONSOLIDATE - core/hparams.py (RunConfig et al.). A validated pydantic hierarchy with bound constraints, dotted --set overrides and JSON round-trip, against the trainers' unvalidated frozen dataclasses. The repo's stated direction is "hierarchical configuration" and "config objects over long arg lists", so this may be what the trainers should ADOPT. The three fold-describing fields were already removed.

KEEP - core/metrics/recall.py. Recall at a MATCHED NODE COUNT, which NodeCounts.recall (recall at whatever count the detector produced) cannot express. That control matters precisely because node count is itself a scoring lever here - comparing two detectors at different counts confounds "where it looks" with "how much it predicts".

KEEP - core/data/split.py (Acquisitions). Production-dead by the reachability walk, but its by_prefix/prefix_of/rank_of are the acquisition-structure vocabulary the dataset-facts E2E asserts against (71/128). Note the earlier justification for keeping it was CIRCULAR (StratifiedSplit lives in the same module, and dataset_facts is a test) - the honest reason is the E2E, not internal self-reference.

title: Eval cadence: the LB-aligned selector made eval a large share of training wall-clock
description: ModelEvaluator replaced a cheap motion-linker fold eval with a full CellTracker run over 4 movies (mount edge affinity + forward + link + postproc per eval). Measured context: a training window of eval_every=500 steps x batch 8 = 4000 frames at ~63 frames/s = ~64s of TRAINING, while a 4-movie pipeline eval costs tens of seconds (the dual-seed TTA proxy run measured ~80s; the selector is single-seed + tta=False so cheaper, but same order). So eval is plausibly 30-50% of wall-clock at the default cadence - a real throughput regression that arrived with a better selector. IMMEDIATE MITIGATION: pass a larger --eval-every (~2000-2500 keeps eval ~10-15%). PROPER FIX (self-balancing, per the standing directive - eval_every in STEPS is machine- and model-dependent): make the cadence adaptive - time the first eval and the window rate, then choose eval_every so eval stays under a declared FRACTION of wall-clock (e.g. 10%). That replaces a magic step count with a stated intent. Cheap to implement inside the existing window loop (it already measures steps/s and can time the eval). Do it when a long run makes the overhead bite.

title: Kernel duplication: 10 kernels repeat the dual-seed mounting block
description: Every kernel under kaggle/kernels/ hand-rolls the same mount: TemporalUNetDetector.from_pack x2 -> BlendDetectorScorer((det1,Ephemeral),(det2,Ephemeral)) -> BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer.from_packs -> CellTracker. That block is duplicated 10x and drifts (the kernel-marker bug + the KernelRuntime staticmethod import bug both had to be fixed across all 10). FIX IN FLIGHT (partial): CellTracker.ephemeral(pack1,pack2,device,config) classmethod = the shared mount (same as from_packs but EphemeralResponseStore, no disk cache - the bounded /kaggle/working disk). The multi-GPU dispatcher work wires ONE kernel (celltrack-dualseed-assign-affinity-stlf6) to it as proof. REMAINING: migrate the other 9 kernels to CellTracker.ephemeral + the dispatcher, so a kernel is only its _CONFIG + one call. Batch with the next kit rebuild. Relates to bead iye (kernel_runtime -> kaggle/).

title: Metric: edge PRC-AUC for association quality (joint-trainer selector)
description: The joint trainer (celltrack/training/joint_detector.py) selects checkpoints on VAL LOSS only — that hides whether the ASSOCIATION (edge model) is actually improving vs the detection term. Add an edge PRC-AUC metric (core/metrics/, beside edges.py): rank the source->target affinities against the GT edge matrix, PRC-AUC (better than ROC for the sparse-positive edge problem). The campaign computed this by hand (crowd-AUC 0.986 proved the affinity was at ceiling). Wire it into the joint eval so a window logs edge-AUC alongside val-loss. Meaningful gap; the one metric worth adding. Optional companion: Brier/calibration on matched-peak probs (detector over-detection signal) - lower priority.

title: Move kernel_runtime.py out of celltrack/ into kaggle/
description: celltrack/kernel_runtime.py is Kaggle SUBMISSION glue (mount kit, install offline wheels, glob packs/test videos, write submission CSV) — NOT tracking logic. It sits oddly at celltrack/ root beside tracker.py/affinity.py. Move to kaggle/ (e.g. kaggle/kernel_runtime.py). KERNEL-TOUCHING + KIT-STRUCTURE: every kernel script does 'from celltrack.kernel_runtime import KernelRuntime' after bootstrapping sys.path to the mounted celltrack_src; if it moves to kaggle/ the kit must ship it (or the kernels import it from a kaggle_src the kit includes). Design the kit-ship path + update all 10 kernel scripts + build_kit.py. Batch with the next kit rebuild (Phase B already forces one).

title: captum attribution entrypoint (edge-transformer + detector)
description: Opt-in 'attribution' extra (captum 0.9.0) added + uv-lock validated. Build a 'python -m celltrack.eval.attribution' entrypoint (after GPU frees): (1) EDGE-TRANSFORMER attribution — IntegratedGradients on the BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer's input feature vectors (the UNet features at the two cell positions) for a chosen dense mislink -> which feature dims drive the WRONG link. Formalizes a1v/zni (we did feature separability by hand: cosine 0.229, bilinear probe ~chance). (2) DETECTOR saliency — attribution of a detection peak w.r.t. input voxels. Portfolio/interpretability value; NOT a new score lever (dense-mislink refuted every angle). Keep it a proper eval sub-entrypoint, wired (not orphaned). Needs GPU to run; build+test end-to-end when the cdg training frees it.

title: single_frame train/eval consistency — wire T=1 into _score_fold detection
description: --single-frame trains the detector on T=1 windows, but the trainer's eval (_score_fold -> detector.detections -> forward, T=2) and shipped inference use T=2. A T=1-TRAINED detector evaluated/inferred at T=2 is unvalidated (the g50 99.98% match was frozen pilkwang weights, not our-trained). To USE single-frame for a real cdg run: make detection (detections/logit_volumes/_response) honor single_frame so train+eval+infer all match T=1. Then single-frame (1.6x) can join the training stack. Until then, cdg runs use compile+channels_last+batched only (no single-frame).

title: Compile follow-ups: inference-compile + default-on for long runs
description: training-compile works (xgf, 1.7x). Follow-ups: (1) test INFERENCE compile (detector._response / eval path, no_grad — no backward, so likely works without the SDPA-math dance; would speed local eval + proxy_eval); (2) decide whether to auto-enable --compile-backbone for runs above N steps (warmup ~30-60s amortizes past ~a few hundred steps); (3) Kaggle submission kernel could compile on its Linux T4 (stock triton) to cut runtime. All lower priority than g50 (2x, env-independent).

title: uv: add triton + triton-windows as OS-markered opt-in 'compile' extra
description: torch.compile inductor needs Triton. Add both packages platform-conditionally so each OS auto-selects: 'triton-windows ; sys_platform==win32' + 'triton ; sys_platform==linux', as an OPT-IN [project.optional-dependencies] compile extra (not base deps, so a bleeding-edge Triton never breaks uv sync). Gated on researcher confirming triton-windows supports torch 2.10 + Blackwell sm_120 (RTX 5090). If Windows build lags sm_120, the same extra still works on Linux/WSL. Enables the compile-backbone flag (xgf).

title: Fix kernel_runtime import drift across remaining 9 kernels
description: The arch gate class-wrapped kernel_runtime funcs into KernelRuntime staticmethods + the restructure moved motion_linking.py to linkers/; the shipped kernel (celltrack-dualseed-assign-affinity-stlf6) is fixed (marker->tracker.py, KernelRuntime aliases) but the other 9 kernels still import free functions install_wheels/pack_source/etc and would ImportError on run. They are mostly superseded but should be fixed or pruned for correctness (user: dont forget restructure references). Root cause: kaggle/ is gate-excluded so kernel consumers arent checked against celltrack renames. Consider a lightweight import-smoke gate for kernel scripts.
close_reason: all 9 kernels aliased to KernelRuntime + py_compile verified, committed

title: Training speed: eliminate fake-pair 2x conv waste (detection-only)
description: temporal_unet.py:122 reshapes (B,T=2,...) -> (B*T,...) and runs EVERY spatial conv on both frames, but tunet.py forward_batch feeds a DUPLICATED pair (stack([frames,frames])) and the detect head reads only frame[0] (features[:,0]). So ~half the spatial-conv FLOPs compute the thrown-away duplicate = the biggest structural cost. BLOCKED: _TemporalAttention couples the frames at downsampled levels (full-res temporal is Identity, skip_fullres_temporal=True) so frame[0] deep features depend on frame[1]; and the fake-pair matches the pilkwang inference recipe. HIGH risk (changes trained distribution). Theoretical up-to-2x forward. Also frees VRAM (batch8 already 30.9/32GB, so batch cannot grow until this is fixed). Investigate: can detection-only train a T=1 path natively + still graft/infer with the pair recipe?
notes: VALIDATED (node-set gate PASSED): 20 dense frames of 6bba_05db0fb1 (hardest), thr0.97 tta-off. T=1 vs T=2-duplicated detected peaks: node count IDENTICAL (16269=16269, delta 0, +0.00%), 99.98% peak match both ways (16265/16269, only 4 differ). So T=1 is near-lossless at HALF the conv work. ADOPTING as opt-in: single_frame flag on forward_batch (default False=shipped T=2, LB-safe), trainer --single-frame uses it. Inference stays T=2 until an LB A/B confirms no drift. scratchpad/g50_nodeset.py.
close_reason: single_frame T=1 window implemented + VALIDATED near-lossless (dense 16269 nodes identical, 99.98% peak match) + MEASURED 1.6x eager (T2 5 -> T1 8 it/s). Trainer --single-frame; inference stays T=2 (LB-safe). Combined single-frame+compile = ~18 it/s = 3.6x over eager-T2 batch8.

title: Training speed: channels_last_3d memory format in training
description: Inference already uses channels_last_3d (febd89f); training does not. Apply detector.to(memory_format=channels_last_3d) + frames to same, feeds tensor cores better on the 3D convs (~1.1-1.3x). Skipped in the batched-forward change (channel=1 outer dim + temporal T reshape in forward_batch need care). Static 64^3 shape makes it safe. Measure real gain.
notes: BUILT --channels-last flag (detector.to(channels_last_3d)). Runs clean, ~3.7 it/s in smoke = no obvious gain (C=1 conv input, temporal reshape). Needs a proper matched A/B on a real run to keep/kill.
close_reason: channels_last A/B: ~1.2x measured (5.15->6.3 it/s marginal), lossless. Made unconditional-on-CUDA, flag removed (self-balancing, not a knob).

title: Training speed: trim eval overhead (drop TTA + eval-every up)
description: _score_fold runs detector.detections with recipe.tta=True = 4x flip-TTA forward per video, purely for a checkpoint-selector proxy that does not need TTA. ~14% of the 2h run (15 evals x 69s/4-videos). Fix: pass a tta=False recipe for training-eval + raise eval_every 1000->2000. Saves ~0.2h, trivial + safe. Measured: init eval 69s for 4 videos.
close_reason: eval-trim (TTA off, 17s->6s/video measured) + heartbeat/ETA/frames-s logging landed, smoke-verified

title: Training speed: torch.compile the detector (static 64^3 shape)
description: Batched forward (o0g) landed 3.6x. Next: torch.compile now that input shape is static (B,64,64,64). Complication: we call detector.forward_batch directly, but torch.compile(module) wraps forward/__call__ — need to compile forward_batch specifically (e.g. self._compiled=torch.compile(self.forward_batch)) or route the batched train path through __call__. Also the backbone lives in external/ (tracking_cellmot TemporalUNet3D) — may hit graph breaks; measure real gain vs warmup cost before committing. Guard behind a config.compile flag default off. Secondary: batched INFERENCE (_response forwards frame-by-frame; could batch the whole video's frames since same shape) — but inference is response-cached (run once) so lower priority.
notes: UNBLOCKED on Triton: triton-windows 3.7.1.post27 (compile extra) gets past TritonMissing, sm_120 codegen works. NEW blocker: SDPA-backward meta-kernel stride assert in _TemporalAttention (BACKWARD only). NEXT: (1) test INFERENCE compile (no backward -> likely works, speeds submission kernel + eval _response); (2) for training, make attention inputs contiguous or exclude attention from compile or bump torch. See compile-windows-triton-2026-08-10.
close_reason: torch.compile WORKS: triton-windows + dynamic=False (static-shape collapse) + sdpa_kernel(MATH) context. Measured 1.7x (eager 4.8 -> compile 8 it/s, batch8 warm-start steady-state). Eval score unchanged. Flag opt-in.

title: Training speed: batched forward (static 64^3 shape -> no buckets needed) + torch.compile
description: _step in tunet_detector.py forwards ONE (z,y,x) volume per optimiser step = GPU underfed (the dominant cost, ~5.3 it/s). Frames differ in shape per video so cannot naive-stack. Fix: bucket annotated frames by shape, stack same-shape into (B,z,y,x), one forward. Then torch.compile(detector) stops recompiling per-shape and torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True stops re-benchmarking. Highest-ceiling training-speed lever. Also enables pre-downsampled zarr store (kills 16x decompress from strided ::4 reads in FrameDataset.__getitem__). Note: benefits own-weights research arm (80e) + edge_finetune probes, NOT the shipped pilkwang-graft LB number.
notes: MEASURED: all 158 fold-0 train videos share ONE post-downsample frame shape (64,64,64). So the shape-bucketing premise is moot — frames stack directly into (B,64,64,64). Plain batching + static-shape torch.compile + cudnn.benchmark=True are all safe. Need: batched forward on TemporalUNetDetector, batched detection loss (ragged coords), collated batch stream, config.batch_size.

title: Half-precision the response cache via fp16 logits (not probs, never bf16)
description:
ResponseCache is fp32 because the equality-NMS (volume==max_pool) breaks under fp16-of-PROBABILITIES: probs saturate near 1.0 where fp16 ULP~0.0005, so distinct peaks (0.99998 vs 0.99991) round equal -> false plateau -> merged detection -> replay 0.8160 vs live 0.9090 (see commit 24a8f15).

FIX (normalization, per user insight): cache LOGITS (pre-sigmoid), not probabilities. sigmoid is monotonic so max_pool equality NMS yields identical peaks; logits DON'T saturate (peaks land at logit~9-11, fp16 ULP~0.008 there = resolvable). Threshold t remaps to logit(t) e.g. 0.99->4.595; background very-negative logits filtered by the >floor cut. Result: fp16 storage + faithful NMS + half disk.

bf16 is EXCLUDED: 8-bit mantissa, ULP near 1.0 ~0.004 (8x coarser than fp16) — corrupts MORE.

PRIORITY LOW: payoff is disk only. Cache-replay bottleneck is CPU peak-extract+link (~1.4s/video), not disk load; fp32->fp16 saves ~1-2s on a ~57s replay. Storage precision is NOT the experimentation-speed lever (the cache EXISTING is). Do this only if the cache becomes disk/load-bound. Acceptance: fp16-logit cache reproduces 0.9090 local fold-0 exactly (bit-faithful peaks vs fp32).

title: Contrastive per-cell embedding (metric learning) for crowded-cell discrimination
description:
IDEA (user): a contrastive/metric-learning objective on per-cell intermediate embeddings — different cells in the SAME frame repel (spatial push), the SAME cell across frames attracts (temporal pull). This is the SOTA dense-association direction (research 66g: triplet/contrastive + hard-negative mining + parental softmax) and targets the ONE open lever: the dense mislink is 100pct AFFINITY-INVERTED (zni) — the edge transformer confidently scores the wrong NEAR neighbour above the true FAR successor.

WHY THIS IS DIFFERENT from the refuted retrains: lna(synth), lna(real), zni(hard-neg) all fine-tuned the edge HEAD with the pilkwang UNet FROZEN, and all crushed P_true along with P_chosen because the frozen (1,4,4)-res features genuinely favour the near cell (dense-ceiling capstone). A contrastive loss on INTERMEDIATE EMBEDDINGS trains the FEATURES to be cell-discriminative — attacking the root cause (feature indiscriminability) the frozen-UNet retrains could not. Connects to appearance-linker (4pz, +0.0075 proxy but CAPPED because hand-crafted intensity descriptors barely separate crowded nuclei) — a LEARNED embedding could exceed that cap.

SETUP OPTIONS (user unsure — evaluate): (a) add a contrastive head to the existing detector/edge model (joint), embeddings feed the linker cost as an appearance term; (b) a THIRD standalone model (like DeepCenter/center_prior is mounted separately) producing a per-detection descriptor consumed by the linker; (c) fold into a from-scratch tunet_detector retrain. Loss: InfoNCE/triplet over (anchor cell t, positive same-cell t+1, negatives = other cells same frame + hard spatial neighbours). GATE before big build (cost-tiered): on the dense movie, does a contrastive embedding SEPARATE the 35 inverted mislink pairs (P_true vs P_chosen) better than the current transformer? If the embedding distance ranks true>chosen on those cases, build; else the (1,4,4) resolution caps it too (dense-ceiling) and it needs finer res. RISK: same resolution wall as every dense-affinity attempt; but this is the untried axis (train features, not head). Portfolio: a clean metric-learning model is a strong artifact regardless. softmax-mass-leaks-outside-the-gate-2026-08-11: MEASURED on the dense movie at the shipped operating point (python -m celltrack.eval.softmax_population, 69164 target columns): sources/gap 700 = the deployed softmax denominator, in-gate competitors mean 3.8, and the IN-GATE SHARE OF THE PARENT-PROBABILITY MASS is mean 0.7796, median 0.9174, p25 0.7289, p5 0.0861.

TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second is the bigger one.

(1) FOR TRAINING (bead jxah): the head is trained normalising over ~3 competitors (DetectionPairs supplies 2.87 decidable sources per pair; the annotated corpus ~12 per frame) and deployed normalising over 700. Widening the corpus to the IN-GATE neighbourhood would reproduce ~78% of the deployed denominator on average but only ~9% for the worst 5% of targets, so it is a real improvement and NOT a faithful reproduction. Do not claim the mismatch is closed by that route.

(2) FOR INFERENCE, needing no training at all: EdgeTransformerScorer.affinities applies torch.softmax(logits, dim=0) over EVERY source in the frame, and the linker then forbids all but the in-gate ones. So the P fed into cost = distance - bonus*P is normalised over a choice set the solver does not have. The correct quantity given the constraint is the probability CONDITIONED on the admissible parents, i.e. renormalised over the in-gate sources. We currently feed an unconditioned one that is deflated by ~22% on average — and deflated MOST exactly where the mass leaks, which is the crowded targets where the mislinks live.

NOT THE REFUTED RENORMALISATION: e9b tested normalising over SOURCES vs TARGETS vs raw vs bidirectional (all noise, 0.868 flat) — a change of AXIS. This is a change of POPULATION on the same axis, restricting the denominator to the parents the assignment may actually pick. Different quantity, and it is the only one of the two that corresponds to a constraint the solver imposes.

CAVEAT before believing it pays: the linker cost is distance - bonus*P with bonus 20, so a uniform inflation of P is partly absorbed by the bonus scale; what can move the score is the NON-UNIFORM part (p5 0.086 vs median 0.917), which is exactly the crowded tail. subvoxel-refuted-but-mislink-endpoints-are-off-2026-08-11 (MY MECHANISM REFUTED by three independent numbers - and the residue is more interesting than the hypothesis):
THE HYPOTHESIS: detections are quantised to a 1.625um isotropic lattice while the median annotated step is 1.675um, so quantisation noise could invert a near-wrong candidate against a far-true one - in the linker s distance AND in the head s relative-displacement input.
REFUTED THREE WAYS (dense movie, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional, reproduces exactly 38 mislinks):
 1. IN-PLANE ERROR IS A QUARTER OF THE STEP, NOT HALF. Median |offset| over 1224 matched detections is 1.675um in 3D but y/x median is 0.406um = ONE full-res voxel, with 83% inside the +-2-voxel half-block the 4x read-out can round by. The +-0.81um figure is the BOUND; the median is 0.41um.
 2. ZERO DISPLACEMENT COLLISIONS, and structurally so. Over 38 mislinks and 1102 correct-edge controls, the true and rival quantised voxel deltas were IDENTICAL in 0 cases and one-voxel-apart in 0 cases (median L1 separation 7 voxels in BOTH sets). The NMS suppression radius IS a cell radius, so two surviving detections can never occupy the same lattice cell - a collision is impossible by construction. The head always had geometrically distinguishable input.
 3. THE MARGIN IS TOO WIDE TO FLIP. On the 38 mislinks the chosen rival is nearer by a median of +6.474um (IQR +4.35 to +7.86), rival-nearer in 97.4% of cases, and only 7.9% have |gap| < 2.369um (= sqrt(2) x the measured median offset, i.e. localisation noise propagated through a difference of two positions). Control on correct edges: median -6.200um, rival nearer 0.1%. The wrong target wins by a wide REAL margin.
PREMISE CORRECTION worth keeping: GEFF stores t,z,y,x as INT64 - our GT annotations are integer full-res voxel indices, NOT sub-voxel. And z is not downsampled, so the z column cannot see sub-voxel z error at all.
THE RESIDUE, which is a real and unmeasured finding: MISLINK ENDPOINTS CARRY 2.1x THE LOCALISATION ERROR of the population (3.495um vs 1.675um median), and it is NOT quantisation - only 27-46% of their per-axis offsets fall inside the grid-explainable half-block against 74-83% for the population. At the 38 failures the peak is genuinely 2-4 voxels off the annotated cell. A crowding control kills the obvious confound: detections with a rival inside the 7um matching radius read 1.675um, IDENTICAL to the population, so it is not a density effect.
THE CONFOUND THAT MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE READING ANYTHING INTO THAT: the offset may be large because the CORRECT detection was MISSING and the 7um matcher paired a NEIGHBOUR instead. The control tests density, not absence. If that is what is happening, those are ENDPOINT_MISSING cases wearing a MISLINK label, and the dense fate decomposition is mis-attributing them. Cheap to separate and it is the next measurement.
ALSO OPEN: 49.8% of matched detections sit a whole 1.625um z-plane or more from the annotated z. z is not downsampled so no read-out refinement addresses it, and an integer GT cannot say whether it is our peak or the annotator s rounding. Needs a different instrument.
STANDING POINT: the detector has been judged by RECALL alone (0.988-0.997, saturated, seven refuted levers) and recall is blind to this - it only asks whether a peak lands within 7um. Position accuracy AT THE NODES THAT FAIL is a different question and nobody had asked it. Tool: celltrack/eval/localisation.py. THE ENTROPY GUARD CAUGHT THE THING IT WAS BUILT FOR, on its first real run. From-scratch, 8 epochs, lr 3e-4 cosine, masked loss, difficulty sampling ON:

  epoch 2.5  coverage 1.000  entropy 0.235  recall 0.201  sel 0.1734   train loss 0.0014, EDGE LOSS EXACTLY 0.0000  <- killed
MECHANISM: coverage reaches 1.000 at 1.5 epochs (vs 1-e^-1.5 = 0.777 for i.i.d. with replacement - the optimistic-init half WORKS and was kept). But once every pair has been seen, sampling becomes PURELY difficulty-weighted, most pairs fall to difficulty ~0, and the mass concentrates permanently on the crowd-ambiguous pairs a1v measured as NOT separable from these features at this resolution. The model memorised the shrinking set it was still shown while held-out recall collapsed.
THE ASSUMPTION THAT FAILED was in the original docstring: "staleness self-corrects, because an improved model makes an old estimate read too high, so that pair is redrawn and refreshed". That holds only while every pair keeps a NONZERO draw probability - and a pair measured at 0.0 is never redrawn.
THE FIX (shipped): p = (1-a)/n + a*(d/sum d) with a = 1/2, a floor on the DISTRIBUTION rather than on difficulty, preserving the difficulty ratios exactly. The adaptive entropy-controlled form was implemented and REFUTED: entropy is an aggregate and one frozen pair among 18024 moves it by ~1e-4, so it cannot see the failure until thousands have frozen. Entropy stays the ACCEPTANCE TEST, never the controller.
A CONTROL RUN with uniform sampling led at 2 of 3 matched epochs (0.2763/0.5345 vs 0.2163/0.4234), so the unmixed sampler was net harmful throughout, not only at the end. UNVERIFIED: that the mixture restores held-out quality past the 1.5-epoch peak - entropy sitting near 0.57 instead of falling is the read to watch.

false-positives-are-a-double-count-2026-08-11 (RE-PRICES THE WHOLE CAMPAIGN: the association lever is worth ~3x its bookkeeping, and two of my readings were refuted by the counts):
THE GAP: our fate diagnosis is per-GT-EDGE, so it accounts for every FALSE NEGATIVE and is structurally blind to a predicted edge with no GT edge to attach to. About half the false positives had never been classified, on a metric where jaccard = TP/(TP+FP+FN) charges an FP exactly as much as an FN.
COUNTS (prediction-centric decomposition, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional):
  dense 6bba_05db0fb1  TP 1132 FP 71 FN 51  MISLINK 38 (53.5%)  TARGET_ORPHAN 33 (46.5%)
  6bba_05b6850b        TP  837 FP 11 FN  8  MISLINK  6          TARGET_ORPHAN  5
  44b6_0113de3b        TP   48 FP  0 FN  2  all zero
  44b6_0b24845f        TP   49 FP  0 FN  0  all zero
  SOURCE_ENDS = SYNTHETIC = EXTRA_CHILD = 0 everywhere.
THE FPs ARE ONE EVENT COUNTED TWICE. All 38 MISLINK targets are UNANNOTATED - the wrong partner is never another annotated cell. All 33 TARGET_ORPHANs stole a LOST target: the target s own annotated in-edge is one we already failed to reproduce, so each is the SECOND charge on a false negative we already knew about. 71 FPs / 38 mislinks = 1.87 charges per mislink.
SO FIXING ONE MISLINK PAYS ~2.9 POINTS (-1 FN, -1.87 FP, +1 TP), NOT 1. The campaign s spend on association was not misallocated, it was UNDERPRICED ~3x. Re-read every association arm s expected value with this multiplier.
TWO OF MY READINGS REFUTED BY THE COUNTS:
 1. I suspected sparse annotation created phantom FPs and could not square that with the proxy OVERSHOOTING the leaderboard. Resolved the other way: linking on past a track end into unannotated tissue is UNCOUNTABLE - FREE - so a sparse annotation charges FEWER FPs than a dense one, which PREDICTS overshoot. Gradient confirms: 0 FPs at 0.16-0.2% annotation, 11 at 13.5%, 71 at 1.8% dense. FP structure is a CROWDING phenomenon, not a sparsity one.
 2. I claimed the boundary sweep (0.9351 -> 0.9313 -> 0.9282 above cost 3) was "over-linking priced from the other side". SOURCE_ENDS = 0 STRUCTURALLY, so it cannot be. Higher disappearance forces the flow to continue tracks, so it accepts lower-affinity partners - it MANUFACTURES mislinks. Same curve, different mechanism.
A BRIEF ERROR THAT WOULD HAVE HIDDEN THE ANSWER: I specified "edges whose BOTH endpoints match GT". EdgeCounts._countable is an OR (source has an annotated out-edge OR target has an annotated in-edge). Both-matched would have excluded TARGET_ORPHAN entirely - i.e. excluded the class that IS the finding.
INSTRUMENT DISAGREEMENT, diagnosed: MISLINK reconciles exactly on the dense movie (38 = 28+10) and differs by +1 on 6bba_05b6850b. The SIGN names the cause - Fate is per-GT-edge, Charge is per-emitted-link, so one source emitting TWO wrong links loses one true edge but is charged twice. Charge < Fate would instead mean a repair dropped a mislink s wrong half.
NET: the lever is unchanged - the affinity, 97.4% inverted on the mislinks with the wrong partner always an UNANNOTATED detection outranking the true one - but it is worth three times what we thought. consolidate-before-deleting-2026-08-10 (USER FEEDBACK, standing rule): before deleting ANY module, check whether the OLD design is BETTER than the current one and should be CONSOLIDATED INTO — always. Never assume newer means better, and never treat "nothing imports it" as sufficient grounds: unused often means the BETTER design was left unwired, which is a reason to WIRE it, not to bin it. WHY: deleting the superior design silently locks in the inferior one, and the duplication that motivated the delete stays. HOW TO APPLY: for each orphan, list its capabilities against the thing that supposedly replaced it; if the orphan has a capability the current design lacks, either merge that capability first or adopt the orphan as the canonical home. Report KEEP / CONSOLIDATE (into what, what merged) / DELETE (with a capability-by-capability argument that nothing is lost). LIVE EXAMPLE that triggered this: I told an agent to delete celltrack/training/tracked_run.py as "a duplicate of the trainers loops". That was backwards-ish - TrackedRun is a GENERIC reusable driver (fit(train, evaluate, save) owning eval cadence + EarlyStop + save-best + metric emit) while the repo now has TWO hand-rolled step-window loops duplicating that control flow. The DRY-correct outcome may be to EXTEND TrackedRun (resume, heartbeat/ETA, step-windowed indexing) and have both trainers drive it. Likewise core/hparams.py was deleted for being unimported, but it is a validated pydantic config HIERARCHY (Field constraints, JSON round-trip against config.json files already written under the data root, nesting) and the repo direction is explicitly "hierarchical configuration" + "config objects over long arg lists" - so it may be what the trainers should ADOPT. threshold-couples-to-the-linker-2026-08-10 (decides the held submission slot; and a THIRD validation of the clamped instrument): detection threshold does NOT have a config-independent optimum - it couples to the linker consuming the detections.
ISOLATED LADDER (assignment linker, clamped): 0.97 = 0.9295, 0.96 = 0.9304 MAX, 0.95 = 0.9303, 0.94 = 0.9300, 0.92 = 0.9301. Reads as "0.96 is best", by +0.0009 = about ONE edge on ~1200, then a flat plateau.
OUR ACTUAL CONFIG (global flow linker at boundary 2 + bidirectional fusion, clamped): 0.97 = 0.9357, 0.96 = 0.9340. The ORDER REVERSES and the margin is larger (+0.0017). More detections change what a WHOLE-VIDEO optimiser has to work with, so the threshold that suits a per-frame matcher is not the one that suits a global solver - the same consumer-coupling that made bidirectional fusion flip sign.
CONSEQUENCE: keep 0.97. Had I trusted the isolated sweep I would have shipped 0.96 into the flow config and lost. RULE: sweep a knob in the CONFIG IT WILL SHIP IN, never in isolation, whenever a downstream stage can reinterpret it.
ALSO A THIRD INSTRUMENT VALIDATION: flow+fusion reads +0.0062 clamped over plain-0.97 and measured +0.003 on the leaderboard - right direction and right order of magnitude, after threshold rank (4/4 correct) and the live selector A/B.
THRESHOLD LEVER IS EXHAUSTED either way: the ladder flattens below 0.97 and the LB ladder was already decelerating (+0.005 then +0.001). Do not spend a submission on threshold. [[clamped-proxy-predicts-lb-threshold-2026-08-10]] [[new-best-0895-flow-bidirectional-2026-08-10]]

divisions-pay-first-lb-win-2026-08-11 (NEW BEST 0.899, and the axis was structurally zero all campaign):

SUBMISSION 55433641 (kernel v26) = 0.899 PUBLIC, against a standing best of 0.895. Config: the shipped
flow+fusion recipe plus symmetry-ranked division recovery — ranking = parent_dist/parent_gate +
|u+v|/(|u|+|v|) over the two daughter displacements, probability floors OFF (min_second_prob and
min_kept_prob both 0.0), gates 7.0/14.0, absolute cap 300 forks.

WHY IT WAS AVAILABLE AT ALL: score = adjusted_edge_jaccard + 0.1 * division_jaccard, and we had banked
exactly ZERO of the second term for the whole campaign. Not from a measured limit — the flow solver's
capacity-1 node split makes dividing_rows() empty, so division_jaccard was 0 BY CONSTRUCTION. The term was
never contested, which is why the first serious attempt paid.

PROXY VS LEADERBOARD, worth keeping: the proxy said 0.9434 vs a 0.9353 control, but the proxy holds THREE
annotated divisions and cannot arbitrate this axis — its FP:TP ratio is 30-50x worse than the hidden set's,
where a fully annotated dense movie would hold ~79-170 divisions rather than 3. The readable proxy signals
were the FORK COUNT (490) and whether the one recoverable division survived, not div_jac. The LB agreed with
the direction anyway: +0.004.

HONEST CHARACTERISATION, because half of this is not science. The SYMMETRY RANKING is principled — the
half-angle form is real mitosis geometry (cytokinesis pushes daughters apart along the division axis), it is
dimensionless, it has no fitted weight, and it beat the frontier's parent + 0.15*sister at identical gates
and identical candidates. The FLOORS-OFF + CAP is closer to gaming: min_kept_prob was set to 0.0 because the
true divider scores below 0.5, so we emit forks the model does NOT believe are divisions, ranked by geometry,
and cap the count to bound the damage. It is attractive because of an asymmetry in the METRIC, not in the
biology — a false fork costs the edge term ~nothing (-0.0019 at 490 forks) while a true one pays 0.1 * div,
and the metric credits a fork that merely REACHES two daughter lineages within a +-2 generation window.

WHAT PRINCIPLED WOULD LOOK LIKE: a mitotic classifier that identifies actually-dividing cells. Static 3D
appearance is measured dead on our data (clean null, brightness confound controlled). The live candidate is
the Hirsch/Linajea learned cell-state head — five-frame 3D patch stack, 7.5x fewer FP divisions on
light-sheet, MIT licence — which the appearance null does not touch because it reads temporal context.

two-noise-floors-and-headroom-2026-08-10 (USER CORRECTION, methodological): I had been applying ONE noise floor to TWO different questions. Separate them.
(1) "Is this change real?" -> the SELECTOR REPEATABILITY floor. Measured at ~0.0017 (two evals of identical untrained weights gave 0.8474 vs 0.8457, caused by cudnn.benchmark timing-dependent kernel choice under fp16); now ~0 after ModelEvaluator disables autotuning for the scoring pass. By THIS standard the low-lr joint gain (+0.0137) is 6-8x noise and clearly real.
(2) "Will it transfer to the leaderboard?" -> the TRANSFER floor, 0.01-0.02, from historical proxy->LB divergence. This governs SHIPPING decisions, not "did training help".
Using (2) to judge an in-run A/B under-sells real improvements, which is what I did.

NEAR A CEILING, JUDGE RELATIVE TO REMAINING HEADROOM, not absolute delta. Node recall 0.968 -> 0.975 reads as a trivial +0.007 but closes 22% of the remaining miss (0.032 -> 0.025). Small absolute increments matter MORE the closer you are, and they are exactly what a coarse floor hides.
CAVEAT specific to this competition: the SCORE has no clean ceiling of 1.0 to normalise against - the adjusted metric is jaccard*(1-0.1*ratio), so UNDER-detecting pushes it ABOVE 1 (measured per-movie 1.018 and 1.026). Node RECALL does have a real ceiling (1.0), which is why it is the more interpretable of the two numbers. Do not compute "percent of headroom closed" on the adjusted score without stating which ceiling you mean.

mount-time-knobs-are-the-ones-that-break-2026-08-11 (the taxonomy that PREDICTS which config knobs can silently do nothing — derived after the edge_blend bug, then used to audit the rest):

TWO KINDS OF KNOB in this pipeline, and only one kind can silently fail:
 - RUN-TIME: read out of `self.config` inside CellTracker.run/_stages every time a video is scored. Changing the config changes behaviour automatically, because nothing was precomputed from the old value. Examples: threshold, min_track_length, smooth_strength, detector_blend, division, rescue, bridge, reuse, topology, keep_boundary_tracks, and every linker field (the linker is BUILT per run from config.linker).
 - MOUNT-TIME: consumed once inside CellTracker._mounted to construct a long-lived object, then never consulted again. Changing the config does NOT change behaviour unless with_config explicitly re-points the constructed object. These are exactly the knobs that can read as "inert" while never arriving.

THE COMPLETE MOUNT-TIME SET is small — the three arguments of BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer.from_packs:
   edge_blend      -> was NOT re-pointed. This is the bug: `--set edge_blend=…` moved the config and nothing else,
                      and the resulting flat sweep was recorded as "the constant is fake".
   bidirectional   -> re-pointed via with_bidirectional (correct all along)
   edge_options    -> re-pointed via with_options (correct, and its config-path test already existed)
Now all three are re-pointed (with_weights added) and each has a test asserting it arrives THROUGH the config.

THE AUDIT THIS PREDICTED AND CONFIRMED: detector_blend looked like a fourth candidate — it is a blend weight and it sits beside a mounted BlendDetectorScorer — but it is read per run (tracker.py: `seed1 = self.config.detector_blend`, passed into detector.nodes) so it connects. No other knob is mount-time. The class is closed, not merely patched.

THE RULE FOR NEW KNOBS: if a value is consumed while CONSTRUCTING something that outlives one run, either re-point it in with_config and pin that with a config-path test, or do not precompute from it. Prefer reading it at use time — a knob that cannot be stale cannot be a lie.

WHY THE TEST SHAPE MATTERS: a unit test that constructs the scorer directly with weights (0.5, 0.5) proves the object mixes correctly and says NOTHING about whether any caller can reach it. Only a test that goes through with_config catches this. That distinction is the same one recorded in built-but-unreachable-is-my-brief-defect. [[edge-blend-sweep-never-reached-the-scorer-2026-08-11]] [[built-but-unreachable-is-my-brief-defect-2026-08-11]]

new-best-0895-flow-bidirectional-2026-08-10 (NEW BEST PUBLIC LB): submission 55407412 (kernel v23) = 0.895, beating the previous best 0.892. Config: GLOBAL flow linker (FlowLinker, disappearance/boundary_cost=3) + BIDIRECTIONAL HARMONIC edge fusion, on the min7+rescue base (thr0.97, gate10, bonus20, smooth0.8, min_track_length=7 + ShortTrackRescue). Since that base alone scored 0.891, the flow+fusion change is +0.004 relative to its own base and +0.003 over our overall best.

THIS VALIDATES THE COUPLING HYPOTHESIS, which made a falsifiable prediction and paid off twice. Bidirectional fusion ALONE under the per-frame AssignmentLinker measured -0.0027 pooled and -0.0010 on the dense movie it targets. The argument: our EdgeTransformerScorer softmaxes over SOURCES, encoding "one parent per target" into the probability, and the assignment cost (distance - bonus*P) is built around that asymmetry - so a SYMMETRIC mutual-consistency affinity re-states a constraint the linker already imposes while blunting the directional sharpness it needs. A GLOBAL solver imposes one-parent/one-child as explicit constraints and therefore wants the symmetric, calibrated affinity. Prediction: the fusion should stop hurting once the consumer is global. Proxy showed the sign flip (assignment -0.0027 vs flow +0.0004); the LB now confirms it at +0.004.

LESSONS: (1) a component that "fails" may have been paired with the wrong consumer - keeping bidirectional opt-in rather than reverting it is what made this possible; (2) PORT BUNDLES, NOT PARTS - the frontier pairs this fusion with an ILP, and our five prior cherry-picks failed alone; (3) the proxy gain was +0.0019, UNDER the noise floor, yet transferred as +0.004 - decision-rule changes transfer even when the proxy cannot resolve them, consistent with the transfer law (greedy->global was +0.005 while every recall-side proxy gain died).

NEXT: v23 sits on the min7+rescue base, which is 0.001 WORSE than the min6 base. Re-run flow+bidirectional on the CONFIRMED-BEST base (min6, no rescue) - the same anchor-on-the-best-measured-config lesson - which plausibly reads ~0.896. backbone-temporal-attention-is-order-blind-2026-08-10 (ARCHITECTURE FACT, read from source, corrects two earlier claims): external tracking_cellmot TemporalUNet3D takes (B, T, C, Z, Y, X) with T ARBITRARY - the spatial path reshapes to (B*T, ...) so convs are per-frame, and _TemporalAttention is a per-voxel nn.MultiheadAttention over the T axis with a LayerNorm and a residual (x + h). CRITICALLY: there is NO temporal positional encoding of any kind (grep for pos/embed/sin/cos finds nothing). CONSEQUENCES: (1) the backbone attention is PERMUTATION-INVARIANT over time - unet([t, t1]) and unet([t1, t]) give the same features up to swapping, so the backbone CANNOT tell which frame came first; (2) order enters the pipeline ONLY via the edge transformer s time-fraction node feature (0.0 for the source frame, 1.0 for the target). CORRECTION 1: my bidirectional-harmonic implementation recomputes the UNet for the reverse pass, justified in the code comment by "the backbone has temporal attention so frame order is material". That is FALSE - the reverse pass could reuse the forward features and merely swap the time fractions, so the 2x affinity cost was unnecessary, and "bidirectional" is much closer to the affinity RENORMALISATION we already refuted than I claimed (which plausibly explains why it behaved like one). The interpretation doc 2026-08-10_affinity-form-is-coupled-to-its-linker.md needs this correction. CORRECTION 2: T>2 (bead f5w) would RUN unchanged (any T is accepted), but order-blind attention can only aggregate APPEARANCE across frames - it cannot represent motion, so a wider window does NOT deliver the velocity signal the dense fast-mover mislink needs. The experiment that would is T>2 WITH temporal positional encoding = architecture change + retrain, a different and better-motivated bead than f5w as filed.

finetuning-adds-no-ensemble-value-2026-08-10 (CLOSES the own-weights-into-the-ensemble line, measured from BOTH parents): our joint fine-tune improves a model INDIVIDUALLY but contributes NOTHING to the two-seed blend, whichever seed it started from.
FROM SEED1 (joint_warm_cos3k, +0.0075 solo on the test four, 0.9175 vs 0.9100): added as a THIRD edge scorer 0.9315 (0.55/0.15/0.30) and 0.9320 (0.4/0.1/0.5) vs shipped 0.9334; REPLACING seed2 with it 0.9325.
FROM SEED2 (joint_seed2_cos3k, best 0.8591 validation): replacing seed2 with it gives EXACTLY 0.9334 at the shipped 0.8/0.2 weighting - i.e. no measurable change, because the 0.2-weighted logit shift flips no assignment on these movies (the score is a discrete function of the matching) - and 0.9329 at 0.5/0.5, i.e. worse when given more say.
CONCLUSION: diversity comes from INDEPENDENT training, not from fine-tuning a copy. Same data, same objective, same schedule pulls any starting point toward the same solution, so fine-tuned variants agree with each other and with their parents more than two independently initialised seeds do. Ensembles pay for DISAGREEMENT; our recipe improves quality while destroying (or never creating) diversity. This is why frontier pipelines ship independently trained seeds rather than fine-tuned variants.
CONSEQUENCE: to use our own weights in a submission we would need either (a) genuine diversity - a different architecture, objective, or data regime, not a different parent - or (b) to replace the ENTIRE ensemble with our own models, which needs them to beat 0.9334 collectively, not individually. Both are larger than a fine-tune. [[own-weights-beat-pilkwang-2026-08-10]]

training-never-saw-the-failure-cases-2026-08-11 (STRUCTURAL FINDING that reframes the whole association campaign - the population trap, in the TRAINING DATA this time):
THE MEASUREMENT that produced it. Hard-negative mining with the backbone UNFROZEN, under a margin form built specifically against zni s flattening failure (pairwise-logistic RankNet on raw logits, invariant to adding a constant to a row, so "push the decoy down and take the truth with it" is an unreachable minimum - pinned by a test). Warm start, lr 1e-5 cosine, masked detection, 1000 steps, weights MATCHED to the edge term (edge 0.2104 vs hn 0.0176 at window 1, so parity ~12; arms w=3 and w=12):
  arm       peak sel  dense jac  mislinks  P_true  P_chosen  recall   test-4 clamped
  control    0.8759    0.8807       38     0.192    0.760    0.9878     0.9136
  w=3        0.8534    0.8734       42     0.225    0.820    0.9862     0.8991
  w=12       0.8554    0.8703       43     0.214    0.830    0.9878     0.8917
Control REPRODUCES joint_short_masked (0.9141 vs 0.9147), so the harness is sound.
THE FORM WORKED, THE OBJECTIVE DID NOT. P_true ROSE (0.192 -> 0.225) where zni s collapsed - the anti-flattening design did its job. But P_chosen rose MORE (0.760 -> 0.830), inversion stayed 100%, mislinks 38 -> 42/43 monotone in the weight.
THE MECHANISM, and it is the finding: the term is supervised on ANNOTATED GT-NODE PAIRS, where the truth already wins by ~4 logits (hn = 0.017 at init). Its gradient lands on already-solved cases and sharpens the head GLOBALLY, including on the real-detection decoys that cause our mislinks - which NO GT-PAIR BATCH EVER CONTAINS. Unfreezing the backbone did not rescue it because the substrate was never the binding constraint. THE CANDIDATE SET WAS.
OUR ASSOCIATION TRAINING HAS NEVER SEEN THE FAILURE CASES. The joint trainer s pair corpus is GT-node-only; the mislinks happen among ~74k real detections of which ~1.8% are annotated. This is the SAME population trap that gave a meaningless AUC of 1.0000 on GT pairs, an inverted threshold ranking on the sparse proxy, and a base rate of 0.9807 in the shortcut probe - but in the TRAINING DATA rather than in a measurement, where it is far harder to see.
THE 2x2x2 THAT NAMES THE UNTRIED CELL:
  zni        = right POPULATION (real detections + mined decoys), wrong OBJECTIVE (absolute suppression), FROZEN backbone  -> flattened
  this arm   = right OBJECTIVE (margin), UNFROZEN backbone, wrong POPULATION (GT-node pairs)                              -> sharpened the wrong cases
  UNTRIED    = real detections + margin form + unfrozen backbone
The joint trainer cannot express that today: its pair corpus is GT-node-only and it has no detection-matched pair source. Building one is the best-motivated association experiment we have, and it is the FIRST time in the campaign that all three axes would be right at once.
ALSO SHIPPED: celltrack/eval/joint_eval.py, which was missing and needed - dense_diagnosis and proxy_eval both mount the PUBLISHED packs, so neither could diagnose one of OUR trained checkpoints. affinity-calibration-is-population-dependent-2026-08-11 (GATE for the likelihood-cost bead - it does NOT pass where it matters):
RELIABILITY CURVE on GT node pairs, dense movie, 40 frames, 5726 candidate pairs, base rate 0.078:
  P<0.05     n=5199  mean 0.001  true 0.000  gap +0.001
  [0.10,0.20) n=24   mean 0.146  true 0.000  gap +0.146
  [0.20,0.40) n=16   mean 0.293  true 0.000  gap +0.293
  [0.40,0.60) n=6    mean 0.458  true 0.167  gap +0.291
  [0.80,0.95) n=23   mean 0.904  true 0.913  gap -0.009
  [0.95,1.00) n=423  mean 0.995  true 0.993  gap +0.002
  CONFIDENT (P>=0.6): n=452, mean 0.987, actually true 0.985.
So on GT PAIRS the affinity is WELL CALIBRATED where it commits (+0.002 at P>=0.6), with mild over-confidence only in the sparsely-populated middle bins (n=6-24).
BUT THAT CONTRADICTS THE HARD POPULATION. The mislink diagnosis measures the SAME model assigning P=0.686 to edges that are wrong essentially 100% of the time on REAL detections in crowding (P_true 0.134 vs P_chosen 0.686, 35/35 inverted). A calibrated model cannot do both. Calibration is POPULATION-DEPENDENT: fine on uncrowded GT pairs, badly over-confident exactly where the score is lost.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE LIKELIHOOD-CORRECT COST (filed P1, removes affinity_bonus AND boundary_cost): -log P blows up precisely where it matters - a confidently-wrong 0.686 edge takes a SMALL penalty while the true 0.134 edge takes a LARGE one, which is worse than the current linear cost, not better. DO NOT build it on the GT-pair calibration. Measure calibration on REAL DETECTIONS (bin the affinity over detected candidate pairs, truth by matching) and recalibrate there (temperature/isotonic on real pairs) BEFORE the log form is safe.
THIRD INSTANCE TODAY OF THE EASY POPULATION LYING: edge AUC reads 1.0000 on GT pairs (structurally cannot fail), the sparse-annotation proxy INVERTS the threshold ranking against the LB, and now calibration looks excellent on GT pairs while the model is confidently wrong on real ones. Each looked like a property of the MODEL and was a property of WHERE IT WAS MEASURED. Standing rule: state the population before quoting any model-quality number.

association-prize-is-0086-on-dense-2026-08-11 (THE HEADROOM, computable for the first time now that the FP term is decomposed):
THE ARITHMETIC. Dense movie 6bba_05db0fb1 at the shipped config: TP 1132, FP 71, FN 51, jaccard = 1132/1254 = 0.9027. Every one of the 71 FPs traces to the 38 mislink EVENTS (38 MISLINK + 33 TARGET_ORPHAN, the second charge on the same event), and 38 of the 51 FNs are those same events. So repairing the mislinks and nothing else gives TP 1170, FP 0, FN 13 (the residual skips and endpoint-missing) = 1170/1183 = 0.9890.
PERFECT ASSOCIATION ON THE DENSE MOVIE IS WORTH +0.086 THERE - more than four times the whole 0.020 gap to the reproducible frontier. That settles a question the campaign never actually computed: the association wall is not a marginal lever we are scraping at, it is by far the largest quantity on the board, and the frontier gap is a small fraction of it.
PER-MISLINK PRICE, useful for sizing any future arm: one repaired mislink moves the dense jaccard by about 2.9/1254 = 0.0023. Our proxy noise floor of ~0.002 is therefore ABOUT ONE MISLINK. Consequences for experiment design: a method that fixes a single mislink is indistinguishable from noise and must not be read as a win; a method must fix ~5 to be clearly detectable; and a "tie at the noise floor" genuinely means "fixed at most one".
THIS ALSO SIZES THE REFUTATIONS HONESTLY. The arms we killed (ranker at b=3 = -0.0007, evidence ramp k=0.5 = -0.0014, seed alignment = -0.0001, bidirectional-alone = -0.0027) were not "small positives we could not resolve" - at ~0.0023 per mislink they each moved on the order of zero-to-one mislink, and the ramp arm s own mislink count confirmed it directly (38 -> 39, unmoved). The instrument was adequate; the methods did nothing.
WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: that 0.086 is REACHABLE. All 38 are affinity-inverted with the wrong partner an unannotated detection outranking the true one, and seven independent axes have failed to move that. contrastive-is-a-trade-not-a-warmup-2026-08-10 (ONE FULL EPOCH, four monotone reads - supersedes both the premature kill and its withdrawal): InfoNCE at weight 0.1 on the SHARED backbone features degrades the model monotonically, and the reason it is a trade rather than a warm-up dip is visible in the loss terms.
CURVE (dense validation four, thr 0.97): init 0.8414 R 0.966 ratio +0.01 -> step 9000 (half epoch) 0.7430 R 0.887 ratio -0.16 -> step 18000 (ONE FULL EPOCH) 0.7292 R 0.867 ratio -0.22.
THE DECIDING EVIDENCE IS NOT THE SCORE. The contrastive term itself CONVERGES over the same span - nce 0.8770 -> 0.4276, edge 0.2479 -> 0.1605 - so the objective is being learned successfully while node recall falls 0.966 -> 0.867. A warm-up dip recovers AS the new term settles; here the term settles and detection keeps degrading. The model is buying discrimination and paying for it in detection, which is exactly what the invariance-vs-discrimination argument predicts when both heads read ONE representation.
ALSO NOTE the proxy understates the damage: ratio -0.22 means heavy UNDER-detection, and the node-count bonus (adjusted = jaccard * (1 - 0.1*ratio)) pays for that, so 0.7292 flatters a detector that lost a tenth of its recall. Read node RECALL, not the adjusted score, when a change can move detection.
THE FIX IS PLACEMENT, NOT PATIENCE AND NOT WEIGHT. Untried variants, in order of prior: (a) a SEPARATE embedding head off the backbone, so the contrastive gradient never reshapes the detection features directly; (b) stop-gradient from the contrastive term into the shared trunk; (c) a magnitude-matched weight (<=0.01) chosen by matching the term to the edge loss rather than guessed. The loss stays committed at default 0.0, computed as a free diagnostic.
PROCESS NOTE: this is the THIRD reading of the same experiment. First kill at step 2500 was premature (user corrected: more objective = slower learning, not no learning). The withdrawal was right. What makes THIS call different is a full epoch, four monotone points, and a converging auxiliary loss - a mechanism, not an extrapolation. [[joint-cosine-3k-best-2026-08-10]]

zero-init-features-are-untestable-here-2026-08-11 (A REGIME LIMIT, not a property of any one feature - check this BEFORE building a third):
THE PATTERN. To warm-start published weights safely, a new input must contribute EXACTLY NOTHING at step 0 - so we zero-initialise it (PriorVelocity.widen_linear_inputs expands the projection with zero columns; the relative-position attention bias is a zero-initialised per-head weighting of a fixed radial basis). That is correct and it is what makes the pretrained model loadable unchanged. It also means the model must LEARN to use the feature before the feature can help.
THE PROBLEM: our warm-start fine-tune peaks at 250-750 steps and degrades after (measured repeatedly; joint_short_masked peaked at step 250, cos3k at 2000 of 3000). So we are asking a converged model to learn a brand-new input inside a window shorter than learning one plausibly takes. A null in that setting does not distinguish "the feature is useless" from "the feature never got a chance".
ALREADY BITTEN ONCE: prior velocity measured +0.0001 held out - identical to its control - with a validation curve swinging 0.8332 -> 0.8627 between ADJACENT windows. That is not evidence against velocity; it is evidence the test could not resolve it.
APPLIES NEXT TO: the relative-position attention bias (built, zero-init, deliberately identity-preserving at step 0, currently unwired). Wiring it into a warm-start fine-tune would reproduce the same uninformative null.
WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED, and the distinction matters: a feature is untestable here only if it starts INERT and must be learned. An active OBJECTIVE (the contrastive term - its head is randomly initialised but the loss applies from step 0) is testable in a short run, and so is anything that acts at INFERENCE with no training at all (the JS log-pool edge TTA, seed moment alignment, every linker cost term). Those can be measured today.
WHAT TO DO INSTEAD, for a zero-init feature: test it FROM SCRATCH with the feature present from step 0, or in a long run with the detection term frozen so only the consuming head is learning. Do not spend a warm-start arm on it and do not record the resulting null as a refutation.
BUDGETING CONSEQUENCE: prefer inference-time and active-objective experiments while the fine-tune regime is what we have. Two of our four staged builds (velocity, relative-position) are in the untestable class; the other two (log-pool TTA, contrastive-detached) are measurable now. [[velocity-null-in-finetune-regime-2026-08-11]] [[longer-training-is-worse-held-out-2026-08-10]]

training-sees-one-candidate-per-source-2026-08-11 (THE NUMBER that turns "training never saw the failure cases" from an inference into a measurement - and it kills the synthetic fix while sharpening the real one):

MEAN CANDIDATES INSIDE THE SHIPPED 10um LINKER GATE, PER SOURCE (python -m celltrack.training.corpus_audit):
  population                                    sources/frame  mean in-gate  median  p90  contested
  synthetic GT (complete labels)                     296           2.79        3      5     77.8%
  real GT annotated - WHAT TRAINING SEES TODAY      12.3           0.99        1      1      1.9%
  real DETECTED, dense movie - what we choose among  744           3.80        4      6     95.4%

OUR ASSOCIATION HEAD IS TRAINED ON UNCONTESTED CHOICES AND DEPLOYED ON CONTESTED ONES. 1.9% of training sources face a rival at all; 95.4% of inference sources do. One candidate per source means most training steps ask "is this the successor?" when there is no alternative to reject - the discrimination the score depends on is never exercised.

THE SYNTHETIC ARM IS A CLEAN NULL, and it refutes the premise not the build. Fixed-fraction mixing 0/25/50%: peak clamped 0.8598 -> 0.8456 -> 0.8320 (the 50% arm never improved on its init at all), dense mislinks 41 -> 42 -> 43, monotone in the dose. It differed from the prior lna refutation on ALL FOUR counts (UNet unfrozen, masked detection loss, MIXED rather than synth-only, complete-candidate framing rather than teach-the-task) and still reproduced it.

THE MECHANISM, which is the real finding: synthetic edge loss ran 0.0041-0.0095 against 0.20-0.53 on real pairs, AT EVERY WINDOW OF BOTH ARMS. The warm-started head ALREADY SOLVES the complete-candidate synthetic pairs. So the complete candidate set supplied almost no association gradient and 25-50% of the step budget went to an already-solved task - dilution, which predicts the monotone damage exactly.

CRUCIALLY, CROWDING WAS NOT THE MISSING INGREDIENT: synthetic carries 2.79 in-gate rivals against real inference's 3.80 - the same regime (the 225-vs-743 per-frame gap is mostly VOLUME, not density). So my pre-registered kill-check (that synthetic candidate sets might be far SMALLER, making completeness worthless) did NOT fire; the arm failed for a different reason than the one I guarded against.

COMPLETENESS IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT - THE NEGATIVES MUST ALSO BE HARD. The corpus with both is our own dense movie's DETECTIONS: complete by construction (every real rival present) and hard by construction (all 38 mislinked partners are unannotated detections the features cannot separate). That is bead tv3x, now P0 with this audit folded in.

CONFOUND, stated honestly: a fixed fraction at a fixed step budget trades real steps for synthetic ones, so the 25% arm saw 750 real steps to the control's 1000. "Adding synthetic" and "fewer real steps" are not separated by this design. The mechanism (synthetic loss already at zero) is what makes dilution the better reading, not the arm ordering alone.

NOT KILLED: node recall rose 0.9902 -> 0.9959 at 25% synthetic - the detection half's only real movement in this experiment, and a hint that synthetic may be a DETECTION asset even though it is not an association one. probe-population-trap-2026-08-11 (I wrote the rule and violated it in the next probe - the lesson is about the MECHANISM, not the rule):
THE HYPOTHESIS BEING TESTED (still open): the edge head may have learned DISTANCE as a shortcut rather than appearance. It receives the candidate pair s relative displacement and true motion is small (median 1.7um), so "near = successor" is an excellent rule everywhere except the crowded fast-movers where we lose score. If true, the learned term in cost = distance - bonus*P is partly REDUNDANT with the distance term it is meant to correct, which would explain why bonus tuning plateaus over a broad optimum.
THE PROBE WAS INVALID. I scored the GT GRAPH, so rows and columns are annotated nodes only; annotated nodes are sparse, so within a 10um gate nearly every candidate pair IS a true edge - 446 true of 457 candidates, base rate 0.976. Both AUCs read ~1.0 by construction (P 1.0000, -distance 0.9969) and every matched-distance band was all-positive, so AUC was undefined. It measures nothing.
THIS IS THE THIRD-POPULATION TRAP, ONE HOUR AFTER RECORDING IT. The same day already produced: edge AUC reads 1.0000 on GT pairs and cannot fail; the sparse-annotation proxy INVERTS the threshold ranking against the LB; affinity calibration looks excellent on GT pairs while the model is confidently wrong on real detections. I recorded "state the population before quoting any model-quality number" and then built a probe on the easy population.
THE FIX IS MECHANICAL, NOT RESOLVE: any probe reporting a separability number must PRINT ITS BASE RATE FIRST and refuse to report AUC when the base rate is near 0 or 1. A rule you have to remember is one you will skip; a guard in the code is not.
TO ACTUALLY TEST THE HYPOTHESIS: score REAL DETECTIONS (~60k nodes, each source with many candidate targets, almost all false), match to GT for truth, then compare AUC(P) against AUC(-distance) and - the decisive one - AUC(P) WITHIN matched distance bands. If P cannot rank within a band it carries no appearance information beyond proximity.
Salvageable: corr(P, -distance) = +0.54 even on the easy set, consistent with the shortcut but far from sufficient. [[affinity-calibration-is-population-dependent-2026-08-11]]

seeds-fail-together-ensemble-uncertainty-closed-2026-08-11 (CLOSED with a mechanism, and a CONTROL that caught a false positive - the flat outcome is the informative one):
THE QUESTION: BlendedEdgeTransformerScorer mounts two INDEPENDENTLY-TRAINED edge heads, blends their raw logits 0.8/0.2 and soft-maxes, keeping only the weighted MEAN. The DISPERSION between them - the one thing an ensemble gives free that a single model cannot - is discarded before the linker sees it. Does it know where we fail?
MEASURED (dense movie, thr 0.97 flow boundary 3 bidirectional, warm cache, identical on two independent runs), split by the per-GT-edge Fate decomposition (Charge names the same wrong links but has NO handle on the true edge we did not emit, which is one of the three groups):
                        n     median |l1-l2|   median |p1-p2|   median blended P
  CORRECT             1132    0.5190           0.0496           0.883
  MISLINK wrong chosen  38    0.5347           0.0877           0.719
  MISLINK true missed   38    0.5322           0.0282           0.070
  AUC(logit gap) = 0.522 and 0.540 = CHANCE. Base rate 0.0325, inside the guard interval.
THE RAW LOGIT GAP IS FLAT TO THREE DECIMALS across all three fates, and that is the space the blend actually acts in, uncompressed by any softmax.
THE CONTROL IS THE PART TO REMEMBER. The PROBABILITY spread reads AUC 0.688 on the wrong-chosen half, which looks like a finding. But |p1-p2| is bounded by 4P(1-P) and the three populations sit at P = 0.88 / 0.72 / 0.07 BY CONSTRUCTION. Ranking by that headroom ALONE - never reading the seeds at all - scores 0.804, HIGHER than the spread; and on the missed-true half both fall below chance together (0.332 vs 0.403). So the probability dispersion carries strictly LESS information than the blended mean already does. Without the bound as a control this ships as "ensemble uncertainty found". Any future spread/variance/entropy statistic over a bounded quantity needs the same control.
WHAT IT ESTABLISHES: two models sharing an architecture, a recipe and a dataset but differing in INITIALISATION produce the SAME logit gap on the 38 pairs they get wrong as on the 1132 they get right. A correlated failure across independent inits is not an initialisation accident - it is much stronger evidence for a FEATURE / RESOLUTION wall than any single-model result in this campaign, because it rules out "this particular model happened to learn it badly". Nothing to build: no downweighting, gating or solver re-routing has a signal to act on.
NOT THE REFUTED AGREEMENT GATE, and the module docstring says so in a marked block: that was ONE model in TWO directions (forward/reverse mutual consistency, dead in all four linker pairings). This is TWO models in ONE direction. Different quantity, different claim.
RE-TEST CONDITION rather than "assume dead": if we ever hold seeds that do NOT share a recipe - a different architecture, objective, or data regime - the correlation argument no longer applies and the dispersion is worth re-measuring. Tool: celltrack/eval/seed_dispersion.py (python -m). [[agreement-gate-dead-all-pairings-2026-08-11]] [[finetuning-adds-no-ensemble-value-2026-08-10]]
