duplicated-frame-detection-is-deliberate-2026-08-10 (HYPOTHESIS REFUTED, mechanism found): the shipped detector read-out feeds each frame a DUPLICATE of itself (t, t) to satisfy the temporal window, while TRAINING supervises the detect head on BOTH frames of a REAL (t, t+1) window. That looked like a train/inference mismatch worth fixing - it is not. A/B on the TEST four with identical weights: duplicated (shipped) 0.9334 (control reproduced exactly) vs REAL PAIR 0.9280 = -0.0054, about 3x the selector repeatability floor. MECHANISM: TemporalUNet3D _TemporalAttention is RESIDUAL and has NO positional encoding, so it adds a mixture of the window s frames back into each frame. With a real neighbour the cells have MOVED, so a voxel holding a cell at t+1 but not at t receives borrowed cellness - the response smears and peaks appear where a cell WILL be, which the equality-NMS then reads as detections. Duplication adds the frame to ITSELF, which sharpens. So the duplicate is a DENOISING choice: detection is a per-frame question and temporal leakage hurts it, even though the same leakage is an asset for association. LESSON: "inference should match training" is a good heuristic, not a law - two heads can ask different questions of the same window. Implemented as DetectorRecipe.pair_context (default OFF, in the cache fingerprint so arms cannot contaminate each other) and kept as a documented measured finding. ALSO weakens T>2: if two real frames already leak, more frames leak more without positional encoding. [[backbone-temporal-attention-is-order-blind-2026-08-10]]

range-deflation-is-structural-in-the-softmax-2026-08-11 (MECHANISM linking two separate findings - explains WHY calibration decays with distance, and predicts a redundancy):
THE OBSERVATION: on genuinely-true pairs at >=5um the head s mean P is 0.519 (median 0.588) against 0.839 on true pairs overall. RANK survives at range (within-band AUC 0.97) but the absolute probability decays toward a coin flip.
THE LIKELY CAUSE IS NOT TRAINING, IT IS THE NORMALISATION. EdgeTransformerScorer softmaxes OVER SOURCES: for a target j, P[i,j] is normalised across the candidate sources i. A FAR true source therefore competes for its target s probability mass against NEAR false sources, and since logits correlate with proximity (corr(P,distance) = -0.893) the far true parent is handed a small share of a fixed budget. The deflation is a property of the directional normalisation plus distance-correlated logits, not evidence that the head is confused - which is exactly consistent with rank being fine and calibration not.
THIS PREDICTS A REDUNDANCY WE SHOULD CHECK BEFORE STACKING: bidirectional harmonic fusion (our only leaderboard gain, +0.004 to LB 0.895) computes the reverse pass and fuses, which PARTIALLY UNDOES the source-direction asymmetry - i.e. it attacks the same range deflation from the other side. The distance-dependent ramp now under test attacks it by reweighting. If both work for the same reason they may be substantially redundant rather than additive.
CURRENT TEST DESIGN ALREADY ACCOUNTS FOR PART OF THIS: the ramp sweep runs ON TOP of bidirectional fusion (the control config is flow(3) + bidirectional), so a ramp gain there is a gain BEYOND fusion, not a re-discovery of it. What is NOT yet measured: ramp WITHOUT fusion. If ramp-alone recovers most of fusion s +0.004, they are two implementations of one fix and we should ship the cheaper one - fusion costs a second full affinity pass per gap, the ramp costs nothing.
ALSO WORTH NOTING: this gives the affinity-form/consumer coupling a cleaner mechanism than we had. Softmax-over-sources encodes "one parent per target" INTO the probability; a per-frame assignment linker already imposes that constraint, so the encoding is redundant there and the symmetric fusion blunts the directional sharpness it relies on (measured -0.0027). A global flow linker imposes one-parent/one-child structurally and wants the calibrated symmetric affinity (measured +0.004). Same fact, both signs explained. boundary-truncation-closed-both-ways-2026-08-11 (a direction CLOSED from both directions - do not re-open without new evidence): the idea that clip-truncated tracks are being unfairly penalised is sound geometry and does NOT pay, whether applied after linking or priced into the solver.
POST-HOC (ShortTrackFilter.keep_boundary): exempt a short component touching the first/last frame from the length rule. Proxy -0.0005; LEADERBOARD 0.891 = EXACTLY its base. Neutral.
PRICED IN (BoundaryPrior on FlowLinker): charge zero for an appearance/disappearance the observation window already explains - at the volume face within one gate, or in the first/last frame - and the full cost in the interior mid-movie. A/B at MATCHED non-zero boundary cost (flow boundary 3 + bidirectional fusion, thr 0.97): flat 0.9353 clamped vs prior 0.9326 = -0.0027. WORSE. The faithful score agrees (0.9380 -> 0.9360) and the bonus rose (+0.0028 -> +0.0034), so it is not a bonus artefact.
READ: making boundary births free lets the solver start and end tracks more freely at the volume edge, and those extra track ends cost more than the truncated tracks they rescue. Consistent with the post-hoc result - the annotations simply do not reward boundary-truncated tracks, on the proxy OR the hidden set.
THE IMPLEMENTATION IS WORTH KEEPING even though the use is refuted: the margin DERIVES from the linker gate (a detection further than max_distance_um from every face cannot have been outside the volume last frame, so no admissible step reaches it - the gate IS the margin, and BoundaryPrior is handed it at call time so the two cannot diverge), distances are micrometres against (shape-1)*spacing so anisotropy falls out, and the factor is argued to 0.0 rather than tuned - there is no strength knob at all. Default off, byte-identical when off. If a likelihood-correct cost is ever built, this is the plumbing it needs. [[infra-neutral-boundary-neutral-2026-08-10]]

clamped-proxy-scope-count-knobs-only-2026-08-10 (PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, CONFIRMED - scopes the instrument, prevents an over-claim): the clamped proxy corrects knobs that change NODE COUNTS and does NOTHING for knobs that move node POSITIONS.
PREDICTED BEFORE RUNNING: smoothing does not change node counts at all (detection and linking set them; the smoother only moves positions), so the ratio and therefore the BONUS must be identical at both settings, both scores shift equally, and the clamped ranking must stay the same as the faithful one - i.e. it will still disagree with the leaderboard.
MEASURED: smooth 0.3 -> faithful 0.9412, clamped 0.9373, bonus +0.0039. smooth 0.8 -> faithful 0.9334, clamped 0.9295, bonus +0.0039. The bonus is IDENTICAL to four decimals and both scores prefer 0.3 by the same +0.0078. The LB prefers 0.8 (0.892 vs 0.889). Clamping does not fix smooth.
THE SCOPE, THEREFORE: COUNT-CHANGING knobs (threshold - validated 4/4 against LB; min_track_length; NMS window; short-track rescue) are the ones the clamp corrects, because trimming is what the bonus pays for. POSITION-MOVING knobs (smooth_strength, linefit, any de-jitter) remain proxy-blind and their anti-transfer has a DIFFERENT cause: at 0.8 the heavier de-jitter drags nodes off the 7um match radius on our SPARSE annotations (local penalty) while the DENSER hidden annotation rewards it. A matching-radius effect, not a count effect.
CONSEQUENCE: do not re-open smooth/linefit on the clamped proxy - the number will keep lying in the same direction. DO re-rank min_track_length and the rescue, which are count-changing and have LB ground truth. And when a new knob is proposed, ask first WHICH KIND it is: if it changes counts the clamped proxy can rank it locally; if it moves positions, only the leaderboard can.
METHOD NOTE: predicting the bonus would be identical, then measuring +0.0039 on both, is stronger evidence for the mechanism than the threshold result itself - it confirms WHY the correction works, not just THAT it does. batch-throughput-plateau-2026-08-10 (MEASURED, settles gradient-checkpointing for SPEED): detector train step (5090, bf16 autocast, single_frame, 64^3) batch vs peak VRAM vs throughput: 8=5.01GB(16%)/62.9 fps | 16=10.02GB(31%)/64.8 | 32=20.00GB(63%)/65.6 | 48=27.74GB(87%)/66.9 | 64=THRASH 15.7 fps (4x COLLAPSE; peak VRAM reads LOWER because it OOM-retried+freed - allocator thrash at the ceiling, this also silently HUNG an earlier benchmark for 10min at 98% VRAM). READ: THROUGHPUT IS FLAT - batch 8->48 buys only +6% while VRAM goes 16%->87% (linear ~0.62GB/sample). We are COMPUTE-BOUND, NOT memory-bound; the GPU is already saturated at batch 8. CONSEQUENCE: gradient checkpointing for SPEED is REFUTED - it spends ~30% extra compute to free memory, and the freed memory buys <=6%. Net loss. KEEP batch_size=8 (default is right); NEVER exceed ~32 (48 at 87% is one step from the thrash cliff). WHAT SURVIVES: checkpointing for MODEL CAPACITY (a wider/deeper UNet), which is a different axis and a genuine SCORE lever - at 0.62GB/sample VRAM is exactly what gates a bigger net. Also note: checkpointing is TRAINING-only (it recomputes activations in the backward), so it does NOTHING for the T4 inference/eval - the earlier 'bigger models on the T4 we use for eval' framing was wrong. selector-nondeterminism-2026-08-10 (MEASURED, previously unknown): our ModelEvaluator selector is NOT deterministic. Two joint runs evaluated the SAME untrained warm-start model on the SAME 4 validation movies at the SAME threshold and scored 0.8474 vs 0.8457 - a 0.0017 spread on identical weights. CAUSE: JointTrainer.train sets torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True, so conv algorithm selection is TIMING-dependent; under fp16 autocast a different algorithm gives slightly different numerics, which moves peak logits, which moves which maxima survive equality-NMS, which moves node counts and the score. IMPLICATIONS: (1) our own selector has a ~0.002 repeatability floor, so an in-run improvement under ~0.005 is not distinguishable from re-running the same model; (2) that is SEPARATE from and much smaller than the proxy->LB noise floor of 0.01-0.02, which is about transfer, not repeatability; (3) it does NOT undermine the low-lr result - flat +0.0137 and cosine +0.0105 are 6-8x the repeatability floor; (4) any future A/B on this selector should either fix cudnn.benchmark=False for eval or report a repeat of the SAME config as its own control. CHEAPEST HONEST FIX: evaluate with benchmark disabled (eval is a small fraction of wall-clock, and deterministic selection is worth more than its speed), or run the init eval twice and report the spread. taskstop-orphans-dataloader-workers-2026-08-11 (a resource leak I caused repeatedly today, and the kill that fixed it took out my own live run):

WHAT HAPPENS: TaskStop (and a killed background Bash) terminates the SHELL, not the python process tree under it. A joint-trainer run spawns DataLoader workers, so each killed training run leaves ~12 orphaned python processes holding GPU contexts. Across a day of "launch, watch, kill, relaunch" this accumulated to 27 GPU compute processes and 18 python processes.

THE SYMPTOM IS SLOWDOWN, NOT FAILURE, which is why it went unnoticed for hours: the eval that had been taking affinity 7.9s per movie was taking 52-61s, and detection 3s became 10s — roughly 6x, spread evenly, with nothing erroring. I only looked because a number I had seen before looked wrong. A leak that degrades instead of crashing is invisible to every gate we have.

THE FIX THAT ALSO BIT ME: I killed python processes older than 5 minutes, keeping "live" ones. My live training run was 6 MINUTES OLD and landed in the kill group. I had the per-process ages printed in front of me and chose the cutoff without checking which side the live job fell on. Age is the wrong discriminator - the right one is the COMMAND LINE (kill python processes whose command line is not the run I intend to keep), or better, capture the launched PID and kill exactly its tree.

STANDING PRACTICE:
 - After any TaskStop of a TRAINING run, check `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid --format=csv,noheader | wc -l` and clean up. Do not assume the stop was clean.
 - When a benchmark-familiar number is suddenly several times worse with no code change, suspect resource contention BEFORE re-deriving the mechanism. I nearly started explaining a 60x edge matrix as the cause of a slowdown that was mostly zombies.
 - Prefer letting a short run FINISH over killing it. Today's kills were all "I can do this cheaper" — each was right on its own and the aggregate cost more than the savings.

MEASURED on the untouched test four, same weights, same detections, only the LINKER and the fusion differing:
  checkpoint            DEFAULT (assignment, no fusion)   SHIPPED (flow b=3 + bidirectional)
  joint_warm_cos3k      0.9175 faithful / 0.9168 clamped  0.9153 / 0.9147
  joint_short_masked    0.9147 / 0.9142                   0.9192 / 0.9188

THE ARGMAX MOVES. Under the pipeline we SELECTED with, cos3k wins by +0.0028. Under the pipeline we SUBMIT, short_masked wins by +0.0039. We have been calling joint_warm_cos3k our best own-weights model all campaign; under the configuration that actually goes to the leaderboard it is the WORSE of the two.

INSTRUMENT VALIDATION, and it is what makes the result trustworthy: both DEFAULT numbers reproduce the historical figures to four decimals (0.9175 and 0.9147 were recorded on 2026-08-10 in [[longer-training-is-worse-held-out-2026-08-10]] and [[fixes-correct-but-inert-2026-08-10]]). WHY IT INVERTS, mechanism not mystery: the two checkpoints differ in node RECALL (0.9945 short_masked vs 0.9918 cos3k) and in node ratio (-0.016 vs -0.052 shipped). The global flow linker prices track boundaries, so it converts extra true detections into kept track continuations, while the per-frame assignment linker cannot - it has no channel for "this track was continuing". cos3k's more trimmed graph flatters the assignment linker (and the node-count bonus) and gives the flow solver less to work with. Consistent with threshold-couples-to-the-linker, where the same knob reversed rank between the two consumers.

CONSEQUENCE: every "best checkpoint" judgement of this campaign was made with the wrong instrument, so the own-weights results need re-reading, not just re-labelling. joint_short_masked - the 250-step masked run - is now the leading own-weights checkpoint at 0.9192 faithful, which is also ABOVE the single-seed pilkwang 0.9118 by +0.0074.

head-learned-appearance-cost-is-the-wall-2026-08-11 (THE KEY NAME IS WRONG - "cost is the wall" was REFUTED within the hour by the ramp experiment it motivated. The MEASUREMENT below stands; the INFERENCE does not. Read to the end.)
WHAT STANDS - measured on REAL DETECTIONS (dense movie, thr 0.97, 10um gate, base rate 0.1487, n=7846):
  band      AUC(P)   AUC(-distance)
  0-2um     refused - 96% of in-gate candidates ARE the true successor
  2-4um     refused - 82% positive
  4-7um     0.972    0.706
  7-10um    0.950    0.642
  5-10um    0.970    0.823
The head HAS learned appearance, not distance: with distance held near-constant it still ranks the true successor at 0.97. And the refusals are a finding - at short range there are NO distractors, which is why "near = successor" works and why the pooled shortcut AUC of 0.982 means nothing.
THE PROBE NEEDED TWO FIXES and the second is the reusable lesson: moving off the GT graph onto 74k real detections was NOT enough - judge() required BOTH endpoints matched to GT, which rebuilds the annotated graph inside the detections (base rate came back 0.9807). Judgedness must follow the endpoint the annotation REACHED (core.metrics.edge_auc s convention). The TRUTH RULE was the artifact, not the population.
WHAT WAS REFUTED - my inference, not the data. I argued the head s value RELATIVE to distance rises with range, so a CONSTANT affinity_bonus under-weights it where the mislinks are, so the COST was the bottleneck. The self-normalising ramp built to test it (bonus * max(0, 1 + k*(d/mean_gated_d - 1)), budget-preserving, byte-identical at k=0) measured:
  k=0 0.9353 (exact control) | 0.25 0.9326 | 0.5 0.9339 | 1.0 0.9113 | 2.0 0.2632 collapse
  mislinks 38 -> 39, UNMOVED
WHY IT COULD NEVER HAVE WORKED: on that config s own 38 dense mislinks, 97.4% are affinity-INVERTED, mean P_true 0.079 vs P_chosen 0.589. In 37 of 38 the head scores the WRONG neighbour far above the true successor. SIGNAL errors, not cost-weighting errors - a ramp that spends more bonus at range amplifies the wrong evidence. The k=2 collapse is the other half: near weight clamped toward 0, short links stop beating the boundary cost, tracks shatter.
THE RECONCILIATION, and the thing to remember: an AUC of 0.97 over 7846 pairs with 1167 positives is fully compatible with 38 confident inversions - that tail is far too thin to register. AGGREGATE RANKING QUALITY SAYS NOTHING ABOUT THE TAIL, AND THE TAIL IS THE WHOLE SCORE. The diagnosis said so explicitly ("a ranking AUC of 0.97 permits a handful of confident inversions") and I quoted that line in the same document where I concluded the head was fine.
NET: dense mislinks remain SIGNAL-LIMITED - seventh independent axis to reach that, and the first from the cost-weighting side rather than by retraining. Resolution/features are still not exonerated as the FIX; what is exonerated is the idea that the head carries no appearance information at all. log-pool-tta-refuted-two-ands-2026-08-11 (REFUTED WITH A MECHANISM that tonight s other finding predicts):
MEASURED (clamped, test four, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional):
  control                         0.9353
  + four-view JS log-pool edge TTA 0.9304  = -0.0049, over 2x the noise floor
  + log-pool AND seed alignment    0.9304  identical to 4 decimals, so it is the pool, not an interaction
COST: affinity wall-clock 120.3s -> 450.8s = 3.75x. So it is WORSE at 3.75x cost, not "no gain at 4x cost".
WHAT IT IS NOT: it did not inflate the graph - node counts and the node-count bonus are unchanged, because the pool sits on the EDGE head, downstream of detection. The soft-AND behaves as designed and still loses edges the single identity view got right.
THE MECHANISM, and it is predicted by the same-day finding that the head under-rewards long true steps: the logarithmic pool is a soft AND across four flip views, and it runs ON TOP of bidirectional_edges, which is ALREADY a mutual-consistency AND (harmonic fuse of the two directions). Two ANDs stacked suppress TRUE-BUT-ONE-SIDED far successors - exactly the pairs measured at mean P 0.519 on genuinely-true >=5um steps while ranking correctly (within-band AUC 0.97). We are conjoining evidence for the very edges that are already starved of it.
THE UNTESTED ARM THIS NAMES: log-pool with bidirectional_edges=FALSE. One AND instead of two. If the pool is only harmful in conjunction, that arm is neutral-or-positive and the mechanism is confirmed; if it is still negative, the soft AND is wrong for this head regardless. Not run - this sweep does not settle it.
KEEP the code: default off, byte-identical when off, now reachable from proxy_eval --set edge_options.view_tta=true. What is refuted is the USE in our current configuration, and the machinery cost nothing to keep. association-loss-degenerate-on-one-source-2026-08-11: SoftmaxFocalBCE normalises over the SOURCE axis. A pair with ONE source makes softmax(dim=0) identically 1.0 -> gradient EXACTLY ZERO and loss a constant 66.67 (clamped BCE(1,0) per rival). MEASURED over 30 train videos / 2776 GT pairs: 799 single-source = 28.8%, and 61.7% carry <=2 sources.

TWO CONSEQUENCES: (1) ~29% of association steps this whole campaign were no-ops; (2) reported edge-loss curves are polluted by that constant - the 'loss 57' on the detected corpus was blamed on the detection-centre collision, which is real but is NOT what produced the number.

A THIRD I ASSERTED AND WITHDREW, filed as a bead before reading the code: that the difficulty sampler, ranking by loss, would mine the dead pairs. FALSE. _PairOutcome.difficulty() is the fraction of annotated sources whose true successor the logits fail to rank top-1, argmax(dim=1) over RAW LOGITS, bounded [0,1] and independent of edge count - immune to the degeneracy, and its docstring says why (a loss-weighted sampler would chase label count). The correction is the better fact: that argmax is over TARGETS, so the sampler already asked 'which successor for this source' - the exact question the source-normalised LOSS could not express.

THE DEEPER FORM, present even when healthy: at 4 sources the true target gets grad -0.142 while its rivals IN THE SAME ROW get +0.0071, 20x weaker. A rival TARGET's probability can only fall if another SUPERVISED source claims its column - and all 38 measured dense mislink partners are UNANNOTATED detections that no source claims. So the axis the linker chooses along has never been directly supervised; our objective is shaped by annotation density rather than by the tracker's decision. This sits UNDERNEATH the seven flat association attacks and under training-sees-one-candidate-per-source: those said the corpus was wrong, this says the objective could not have used a better one.

FIX SHIPPED: normalise over TARGETS as well (axes=(0,1), LossCfg.symmetric_links, --symmetric-links). ZERO new parameters, default unchanged (byte-identical when off). REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: a slack row needs a SCALE - our edge logits sit near -11 so a zero-logit slack takes all the mass.

WORSE at the peak by ~0.006 though FLATTER in decay (control fell to 0.8453 by step 1000, this held 0.8516). Held-out test read pending. NOTE the fix targets the GT corpus's dead pairs; the DETECTED corpus (tv3x, 3.86 candidates/source) is where the target-axis term has rivals worth ranking, and that pairing is untested.

PROCESS LESSON: we audited the training CORPUS twice (candidate density, coverage, contestedness) and never audited the OBJECTIVE computed over it. Check a loss has a gradient on every SHAPE its data takes - SoftmaxFocalBCE had a unit test from day one and it used a 2x2 matrix. THE EXPERIMENT: re-run the recipe that produced our best own-weights checkpoint (warm start, lr 1e-5 cosine, masked detection at 0.97, 1000 steps, eval/250) with the SELECTOR finally scoring through the shipped pipeline (flow boundary 3 + bidirectional) instead of the bare-default per-frame one. CURVE on the validation four (shipped selector): init 0.8476 -> 250: 0.8654 SAVED -> 500: 0.8534 -> 750: 0.8455 -> 1000: 0.8453. Peak at step 250, matching the long-known short optimum.

  joint_hn_control  (old, wrong selector)    0.9206 / 0.9201                   recall 0.9932  mislinks 43
So the correctly-selected run is 0.0009 BELOW the best checkpoint we already had — inside noise, i.e. equivalent.

WHAT THAT MEANS, stated as pre-registered before the run: the old selector happened to pick WELL WITHIN a run even though it ranked badly ACROSS runs. The damage from the bias was confined to between-run comparisons (which model we call best), and it did not cost us a better checkpoint inside any single run. USEFUL BY-PRODUCT: two runs of nominally the same recipe scored 0.9206 and 0.9197, so ~0.001 is a reasonable estimate of run-to-run variation for this recipe on the test four. That is a tighter floor than the 0.002 selector-repeatability figure and worth using when judging future own-weights arms.

Masking removes the negative pressure that keeps detections precise, so the model over-detects, and the extra detections become crowding candidates that turn into mislinks.

resolution-is-not-the-lever-2026-08-11 (CLOSES the direction I judged most promising - decided by a cheap asset-free measurement):
MEASURED on the dense movie 6bba_05db0fb1, shipped detector at thr 0.97, whole movie: gt=1229, FOUND 1225, MISSED 4. Detection recall 99.7%.
Raw full-resolution patch statistics at GT centres: FOUND (n=150) raw_peak median 1601, local contrast median 379.5. MISSED (n=4) raw_peak median 1391.5, local contrast median 316.0. Contrast ratio missed/found = 0.833.
TWO READS, and the second dominates:
(1) The misses are NOT featureless - at 83% of the contrast of found cells they look much like cells in the raw image, so "the information is not in the image" is unsupported. But n=4 is far too small to conclude anything about resolution specifically.
(2) THERE ARE ONLY 4 MISSES IN 1229. Recovering every one is worth ~0.3% of annotated nodes. Resolution is NOT the lever - not because the signal is absent but because there is essentially NOTHING LEFT TO FIND on the axis we can measure.
THIS KILLS THE DIRECTION I RATED HIGHEST when asked where a "much bigger upside" could come from. I had argued from three earlier findings (every mounted detector added ZERO complementary recall; misses produce no response at any threshold; misses described as crowd-buried at (1,4,4)) that our REPRESENTATION was the bottleneck and finer resolution was the untried structural lever. The miss COUNT was never checked. It is 4.
HONEST BOUND: this measures recall against OUR annotations (1229 nodes among ~70k detections). The hidden evaluation annotates the same movies DENSELY, so cells we have no label for are invisible to this test - it cannot rule out that the pack is finding cells we neither detect nor annotate. But on every axis we can measure, detection is finished and the gap is association.
METHOD NOTE: an earlier version of this probe sampled 10 frames, found 75/75, and reported ZERO misses - a sample too small to contain the phenomenon. Sizing the sample to the effect (0.3%) was the whole experiment. [[dense-ceiling-quantified-2026-08-04-the-capstone]] [[threshold-recall-mechanism-closed-2026-08-04-definitive]]

the-out-of-gate-mass-is-a-none-of-the-above-2026-08-11 (REFUTED with a mechanism that inverts the premise, and it answers the slack-row question from the other side):

MEASURED (test four, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional, shipped weights, inference-only change):
  control                                    clamped 0.9353
  + AdmissibleAffinity (conditioned on gate) clamped 0.9270   = -0.0083, about 4x the noise floor
Clearly worse. The idea was that the linker prices P normalised over all ~700 sources in the frame while the gate admits ~4, so the correct quantity given the constraint is P conditioned on the ADMISSIBLE parents. The arithmetic is right and the conclusion is wrong.

WHY: conditioning asserts 'one of these four IS the parent'. That is FALSE for a target whose true parent is outside the gate or does not exist at all - a track start, an appearance, a cell entering the volume, a parent the detector missed. The leaked mass was never noise: a column with LOW in-gate mass was saying 'probably none of these', and renormalising deletes exactly that signal and then hands the solver a confidently wrong parent. Measured leak distribution (celltrack.eval.softmax_population, 69164 dense targets): in-gate mass mean 0.7796, median 0.9174, p25 0.7289, p5 0.0861 - so the 5% of targets with almost no in-gate mass are precisely the ones conditioning damages most, and they are disproportionately the true appearances.

SO THE 22% LEAK IS A FEATURE. It is an implicit 'none of the above' that the softmax provides for free, and it answers the slack-row question raised the same day from the opposite direction: at INFERENCE we already have a slack row, made of the out-of-gate sources. What TRAINING lacks is not a slack row either - it is that the training matrix contains only decidable sources, so the head never learns to spread mass onto 'no admissible parent' the way it must at inference.

THE FOLLOW-UP THIS NAMES, and it is the constructive use of the same quantity: instead of renormalising the leak away, READ it. A target whose in-gate mass is low is evidence of an APPEARANCE, and FlowLinker prices appearance with one uniform constant. Making that price read the in-gate mass is the opposite operation to the refuted one and uses the signal rather than destroying it. Untested.

KEPT: celltrack/linkers/admissible_affinity.py, default off, byte-identical when off (applied() returns the very same array), refused on a linker with no gate. What is refuted is the USE. [[softmax-mass-leaks-outside-the-gate-2026-08-11]] [[e9b-dense-costfn-exhausted-2026-08-03]]

edge-blend-plateau-at-the-shipped-point-2026-08-11 (COMPLETE re-measurement after the with_weights bug — and it separates two questions the morning's broken run had fused):

MEASURED with the knob connected, four test movies, all four arms:
  SHIPPED point (thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional fusion):
    0.8/0.2 = 0.9380 (clamped 0.9353)
    0.6/0.4 = 0.9380 (clamped 0.9352)
    0.5/0.5 = 0.9380 (clamped 0.9352)
    1.0/0.0 = 0.9336 (clamped 0.9309)   <- DROPS 0.0044

    0.8/0.2 = 0.9334   0.5/0.5 = 0.9329   1.0/0.0 = 0.9312

TWO SEPARATE ANSWERS, and conflating them is what made this confusing:
 1. THE MIX RATIO is on a broad PLATEAU at the shipped point — 0.5, 0.6 and 0.8 are identical to four decimals
    faithful and within 0.0001 clamped. So the specific value 0.8 is NOT measured; anything in 0.5-0.8 is the
    same pipeline. Under the per-frame linker the same range spans 0.0005, i.e. it matters slightly there.
 2. THE SECOND SEED IS LOAD-BEARING. Removing its edge head entirely costs -0.0044 faithful and -0.0044
    clamped at the shipped point — twice the noise floor, and the largest single-knob effect measured today.
    A plateau over how the two are mixed is NOT evidence that one of them is redundant.

DECISION: KEEP 0.8/0.2 as shipped. It is the measured best by 0.0001 (inside noise, so it wins on nothing) and
it is the value the leaderboard actually scored 0.895 with. Switching to the self-balancing 0.5/0.5 for
tidiness would change the submitted recipe for zero expected gain against an unmeasured leaderboard effect —
the same class of churn that cost 0.003 when smooth_strength was shipped on a proxy preference. What is
recorded instead: the constant sits on a plateau and therefore needs no defence, rather than being "fake".

CONSEQUENCE FOR 42x9 (our head as an ensemble seed), and it LOWERS the prior: seed 2's edge head is
load-bearing under the shipped consumer, so a third head has to BEAT it, not fill a vacancy. The optimistic
reading — that flatness across the mix meant seed 2 contributes nothing — is refuted by the 1.0/0.0 arm.

own-weights-beat-pilkwang-2026-08-10 (MILESTONE - first own-trained weights to beat the published ones on held-out data): joint_warm_cos3k.pt (warm-start, lr 1e-5, cosine, 3000 steps, best at step 2000) scored 0.9175 on the untouched TEST four vs the same-shaped single-seed pilkwang 0.9100 = +0.0075. THE MECHANISM IS ASSOCIATION, NOT DETECTION: recall 0.992 (ours) vs 0.993 (pilkwang) and node ratio -0.05 for both - identical. So the gain is neither recall nor the node-count bonus; it is EDGE JACCARD, i.e. the jointly-trained transformer links the same nodes better. That matters because four separate refutations said the association head could not be improved (lna synthetic, lna real-positives, zni hard-negatives, bidirectional fusion) - and every one of them trained the head with the BACKBONE FROZEN. clamped-proxy-predicts-lb-threshold-2026-08-10 (INSTRUMENT BREAKTHROUGH - overturns "threshold is irreducibly LB-only"): removing the node-count bonus from the proxy makes it reproduce the leaderboard s threshold ordering EXACTLY.

MEASURED on the 4-movie proxy, against LB ground truth we already paid for:
  threshold   faithful   clamped   bonus     LB
  0.995       0.9326     0.9203    +0.0123   0.880
  0.99        0.9348 MAX 0.9264    +0.0083   0.887
  0.98        0.9344     0.9291    +0.0053   0.891
  0.97        0.9334     0.9295 MAX +0.0039  0.892 MAX
FAITHFUL ranks 0.99 > 0.98 > 0.97 > 0.995 and picks the config that LOST 0.005 on the leaderboard. CLAMPED ranks 0.97 > 0.98 > 0.99 > 0.995 = the leaderboard order, all four, no inversions. The bonus column is MONOTONE in threshold (+0.0123 down to +0.0039), which is the confound made visible.

WHAT THIS OVERTURNS: threshold-recall-mechanism-CLOSED and 8-video-cv-equally-threshold-blind both concluded that NO sparse local proxy can capture the threshold lever, and that the axis is LB-only. That was the right observation with the wrong cause attributed. The proxy was not blind because our annotations are sparse; it was blind because the node-count BONUS rewards the trimming that sparse annotation hides. Remove the bonus and the sparse proxy ranks the axis correctly.

WHY IT WORKS: adjusted = jaccard * (1 - 0.1 * ratio). Raising the threshold trims true cells that are mostly UNANNOTATED locally, so jaccard barely moves while ratio goes negative and the factor climbs above 1. On the hidden set those same cells ARE annotated, so they cost real jaccard and the bonus does not compensate. Clamping the factor at 1.0 removes exactly the term the hidden set does not pay.

CONSEQUENCE: threshold becomes a LOCALLY TESTABLE axis for the first time in this campaign - a minutes-long sweep instead of a 5-per-day leaderboard resource. The same correction applies to every recall-side knob previously written off as proxy-blind (smooth, min_track_length, NMS): they should ALL be re-ranked under the clamped score before being called untestable. The clamped score is still RISING as threshold falls (0.9264 -> 0.9291 -> 0.9295), so the optimum may sit BELOW 0.97, which no submission has ever tested.

CAVEAT: this validates RANK, not level - clamped 0.9295 vs LB 0.892 still differ in absolute terms. Use it to order configs, not to predict a score. And it is validated on ONE axis with four points; re-check before trusting it on a knob of a different kind. ranker-translated-ratio-fails-2026-08-11 (FIRST measurement of the ported CC0 ranker - the frontier ratio is much WORSE in our pipeline):
  CONTROL flow(3)+fusion, a=20, no ranker   clamped 0.9353
  RANKER  same, a=3 / b=17 (their 85/15)     clamped 0.9124   = -0.0229
WHAT I DID WRONG, and it is the bundle lesson biting from a direction I did not check: I preserved their RATIO while changing what the ratio sits INSIDE. Their cost is motion_dist + 0.05*raw_dist - 0.75*(0.85*ranker + 0.15*edge); ours is distance - a*P. The ranker consumes motion_dist_um and motion_gain_um AS FEATURES, so it was trained against a candidate set and a geometry we did not reproduce - and cutting the transformer from 20 to 3 is itself a large change that requires the ranker to be at least as good just to break even.
SO THIS IS NOT YET EVIDENCE THE RANKER IS USELESS. It is evidence that transplanting the evidence term while keeping our geometry does not work. Three things differ at once: the geometry (raw distance vs motion-predicted distance), the solver (global min-cost flow vs per-frame Hungarian), and the transformer weight (3 vs 20).
NEXT, ISOLATING TEST (running): hold a=20 (transformer untouched) and add b = 2 / 5 / 10. That asks the single question "does the ranker add anything MARGINALLY", with everything else fixed. If it helps at small b, the mechanism transfers and only the split needs finding. If it hurts at every b, then either our features are off-distribution or the ranker genuinely does not transfer to a global solver.
STILL TRUE AND VALUABLE REGARDLESS: we load the artifact correctly where the public notebooks do not - their _InferredRankerMLP collects only 2-D weights and silently drops the (64,) LayerNorm the model was trained with, which our strict=True reconstruction proves is really there. Any comparison against their 0.915 is therefore against a degraded version of this asset.
IF THE ADDITIVE TEST ALSO FAILS, the next thing to check is FEATURE DISTRIBUTION, not the weight: dump our 22-feature vectors and compare their per-feature mean/std against local_association_features stats shipped in the artifact. A feature computed in the wrong units or from the wrong graph would put the whole vector off-distribution and produce exactly this shape of result. [[new-best-0895-flow-bidirectional-2026-08-10]]

THE MECHANISM: a one-source pair makes softmax(dim=0) identically 1.0, so that term has no gradient and contributes a constant 66.67. A dead axis adds zero to the numerator and still counts in the divisor. Argument independent of the accident: a target with one candidate parent carries less evidence about association than one with forty competing for it, so it should push proportionally less - and this is the only place that difference can be expressed without inventing a weight. THE QUESTION: our division recovery emits far more candidate forks than there are true divisions, and the edge probability cannot separate them. The literature says static 3D appearance can (PMC3278834: sphericity, volume, intensity, intensity-weighted-vs-geometric centroid offset, Haralick texture + weighted SVM, >90% across five cell-cycle phases in 3D developmental tissue). Does that signal exist in OUR data?
MEASURED on 6bba_05db0fb1 at the shipped config, per-mother PERCENTILE inside two controls (no AUC - three positives cannot support one):
  feature            232 (recoverable)   624 (daughter undetected)   771 (daughter claimed)
  centroid offset      82 / 73                5 / 4                     97 / 95
  intensity mean       18 / 30               75 / 86                    12 / 22
  volume               36 / 36               80 / 89                    14 / 14
  elongation           71 / 75               41 / 46                    23 / 22
  (percentile inside FALSE CANDIDATES / inside ANNOTATED NON-DIVIDING)
NO FEATURE PUTS ALL THREE IN A TAIL of either control, at either probability floor. On every feature 624 and 771 sit on OPPOSITE SIDES - that is scatter, not a class. The literature s flagship feature has 771 at the 97th percentile and 624 at the 5th.
THE ANNOTATED-VS-UNANNOTATED CONTROL FIRED, IN THE CONFOUND DIRECTION, and it is the reason to trust the null: median intensity is 1544 for false candidates, 1388 for the linked baseline, 1263 for annotated cells. BRIGHTNESS SEPARATES "IS A RECOVERY CANDIDATE" FROM "IS ANNOTATED", not "is mitotic". Any mothers-vs-candidates intensity claim would have been reading that artefact. Always carry that control when comparing annotated things to detected things in this dataset.
CORRECTION TO WHICH GATE BINDS - I had this backwards. At the SHIPPED gates the recovery proposes only 141 parents at P>=0.25 and 187 at P>=0.05; dropping the probability floor FIVE-FOLD adds 46 candidates. THE GEOMETRY GATES BIND, NOT THE PROBABILITY FLOOR. The ~800-fork figure came from a WIDER geometry, not from the floor. So the tension is sharper than I stated: reaching division 232 REQUIRES widening the geometry (it needs parent >= 6.08, sister >= 13.5), and widening the geometry IS what floods.
WHAT IS REFUTED, PRECISELY: a static-appearance discriminator computed from our detection centres. NOT refuted: the Hirsch/Linajea learned cell-state head (arXiv:2208.11467), which reads a FIVE-FRAME 3D patch STACK and a learned representation - neither of which this measures, and which cuts false-positive divisions 7.5x on isotropic 3D LIGHT-SHEET (MIT licence).
ONE CAVEAT THAT BOUNDS THE REFUTATION WITHOUT RESCUING IT: the centroid offset is computed from a centre quantised on the (1,4,4) lattice (up to 0.81um per axis in y/x) while the feature s entire range across all populations is 0.2-1.3um, and mother 232 swings from the 82nd to the 5th percentile between consecutive frames. That feature is refuted AS COMPUTED FROM THE DETECTION CENTRE; a sub-voxel-refined centre would be a different measurement. Volume and elongation carry no such caveat and are equally null.

ranker-sign-flips-with-geometry-2026-08-11 (CAUSAL CLAIM REFUTED - the flip is NOT caused by geometry. Corrected 2026-08-11 by the motion-in-flow experiment; read this whole entry, the original conclusion was wrong.)
WHAT WAS OBSERVED, and still stands as an observation: the CC0 ranker at the frontier s 85/15 split measures +0.0032 inside MotionHungarianLinker s cost and -0.0229 inside our raw-distance FLOW cost. I attributed the ~0.026 swing to the GEOMETRY - "its motion_dist_um and motion_gain_um features are in-distribution only under a motion-predicted cost".
THAT HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and on its own terms. Putting a motion-predicted distance INTO the flow cost and re-running the split (clamped, test four, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional):
  raw distance, no ranker   0.9353   control
  MOTION distance, no ranker 0.9331  -0.0022
  MOTION distance, 3/17      0.9274  -0.0079
  MOTION distance, 17/3      0.9325  -0.0028
Inside motion-predicted flow the ranker is STILL monotone-negative and 85/15 is again the worst cell. Motion geometry recovers only ~0.0022 of the penalty and does NOT reproduce the +0.0032.
THE REASON MY STORY COULD NOT HAVE BEEN TRUE: AssociationRanker computes motion_dist_um and motion_gain_um from the CONTEXT GRAPH, never from the linker s cost geometry. Changing the cost geometry does not change the ranker s features at all, so it could never have fixed a feature distribution. I should have caught that by reading the feature computation I had already commissioned.
WHAT THE +0.0032 IS ACTUALLY ATTRIBUTABLE TO: the whole per-frame linker - its tight-then-loose two-pass commitment, and a baseline 0.045 weaker (0.8932) with far more room to move. Not geometry. And it is unpurchasable regardless, since that linker is 0.045 below flow+fusion.
ALSO REFUTED IN THE SAME EXPERIMENT: motion-predicted geometry for a GLOBAL solver (-0.0022, arm 2). Mechanism - a per-frame matcher has NO channel for history, so prediction is the only way a previous step reaches its cost; the flow linker already couples gaps through the boundary price and recovers "this track was continuing" structurally. Worse, our velocity is derived from the SAME affinity the cost already prices, so it is the affinity re-entering as geometry rather than new evidence.
NET: the frontier s ranker is not available to us in any configuration we can run - refuted in flow at raw geometry, in flow at motion geometry, and unpurchasable in the per-frame linker where it does help. [[ranker-does-not-transfer-to-our-cost-2026-08-11]]

dont-commit-while-agents-hold-the-tree-2026-08-11 (a sharper, RISKIER version of a rule I had already learned once):

I knew "the test suite is only meaningful when the tree is mine" (32 phantom failures on 2026-08-11 from in-flight agent state). The commit path is WORSE, and I found out by trying it while two agents held ~28 files.

TWO THINGS BIT, and only the second is dangerous:
 1. pre-commit gates run REPO-WIDE, not on the staged set. Staging only .beads/issues.jsonl did NOT narrow them - pyrefly still type-checked celltrack/training/pair_split.py mid-edit and failed on attributes the agent had not added to DataCfg yet. So there is no "commit just my file" escape hatch while someone else's half-finished module is on disk.
 2. pre-commit STASHES UNSTAGED FILES to a patch, runs the gates, then restores. That means it moved an actively-being-written agent's work out from under it and put it back. It restored cleanly here (git stash list empty, all 28 files intact, mtimes preserved) - but if an agent had WRITTEN during that window the restore would have conflicted, and the failure mode is losing an agent's in-flight work, not a red gate.

RULE: while any agent holds files, do not run git commit at all - not even for a file the agent does not touch. Queue the commit, or wait for the agent to land. The gates cannot be scoped and the stash is a race.

WHAT IS SAFE MEANWHILE: bd close/create/update (writes .beads/issues.jsonl, no hooks), reading, measuring on a warm cache, and drafting the commit message. The board audit that triggered this was fully done - only the commit had to wait.

symmetry-ranking-recovers-the-division-2026-08-11 (FIRST division result of the campaign, and it refutes two parts of my own brief):

MEASURED (test-four proxy, thr 0.97, flow boundary 3, bidirectional):
  arm                                          forks  clamped  division 232?
  control, no division                             0  0.9353   -
  probability ranking, shipped gates 4.7/7.2     239  0.9314   missed
  frontier geometry (parent + 0.15*sister)       464  0.9313   missed
  SYMMETRY, gates 7/14, floors 0.0, cap 300      490  0.9434   RECOVERED
  symmetry, same, cap 50                         174  0.9331   missed
  uncapped variants                        4370-7356  0.88-0.91

REFUTATION 1 - THE BLOCKER WAS min_kept_prob, NOT THE GATES AND NOT THE CAP. I diagnosed the geometry gates as what excluded division 232 and filed the tension as "we cannot reach the reachable division without opening the gate that floods". Wrong: with gates open and NO cap, 232 is still never PROPOSED at min_kept_prob=0.5 - under this pipeline the true divider's kept-child probability sits below 0.5. The clean A/B is the uncapped pair at 4370 vs 4611 forks, identical but for that floor.

REFUTATION 2 - THE ANGLE TERM DOES THE WORK, NOT THE DISTANCES. Same gates, same candidacy, same 490 forks: symmetry ranking lifts 232 into the kept set and the frontier's parent + 0.15*sister does not. Edge-term damage at EQUAL fork count: symmetry -0.0019, frontier geometry -0.0036, probability -0.0039. So the frontier's own ranking is not the best available even on their own axis.

THE COST FUNCTION, with no fitted weight: parent_dist/parent_gate + |u+v|/(|u|+|v|) over the two daughter displacements. The second term is the half-angle form (0 for a clean opposite split, 1 for two cells leaving together), it is dimensionless, and BOTH terms are normalised by the constraint that decides their own admissibility - so both live in [0,1] over the admitted set and equal weighting is the only unfitted choice. Sister distance stays a GATE and never a score: as a score its sign is wrong, since a true mitosis pushes daughters apart (232's sisters are 13.5um).

SUBMITTED as kernel v26 (4 slots left today). The proxy CANNOT arbitrate this axis - it holds three annotated divisions, so div_jac is meaningless here; the readable signals are the fork count, 232's survival, and the edge-term cost. Upside is the 0.1*div_jac term we have never banked (ceiling ~0.045); measured downside is -0.0019 on the transferring term, though on the DENSER hidden annotation more wrong forks are countable, so the real edge cost is plausibly 2-5x that.

contrastive-early-regression-2026-08-10 (NOT a refutation - I killed it too early, and had already recorded that exact mistake). An InfoNCE term on the shared backbone features caused an EARLY regression; I called it refuted at step 2500 of 18000 (14% in). That conclusion is withdrawn.

Adding a NEW loss term reshapes the representation; a transient regression while features reorganise is the expected shape of the curve, not the verdict. More objective = slower learning, not no learning (user correction).
WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED. Weight 1.0: nce 1.8074 against edge 0.3057 / det 0.2028 - 6x the edge loss - proxy 0.8414 -> 0.7904. Weight 0.1: proxy 0.8414 -> 0.7765 (2000) -> 0.7375 (2500), node RECALL 0.966 -> 0.947 -> 0.925.
THE RECALL DROP REMAINS THE INTERESTING SIGNAL regardless of outcome: the contrastive objective moved DETECTION, which is what the invariance-vs-discrimination argument predicts - detection wants every cell to look like "a cell", association wants each to look distinct, and both read the SAME features. Whether that is a transient cost paid on the way to a better representation, or a standing tax, is exactly what a full-length run answers.
RERUN IN FLIGHT: weight 0.1, 18000 steps (one full pass over the 18024 pairs), cosine over the whole horizon, patience 99 so nothing early-stops during a dip. FALSIFIER: if it is still below the 0.8414 init at ~step 8000-10000 with recall still falling, the standing-tax reading is supported and the fix is PLACEMENT (separate embedding head, stop-gradient into detection, or a magnitude-matched weight), not patience.

detection-loss-punishes-good-detectors-2026-08-10 (MECHANISM, read from source - a single explanation for the campaigns whole "our retrains lose to the mounted pack" pattern): BalancedBCE builds target = torch.zeros_like(logits) with ones only at ANNOTATED centres. Our annotations cover ~1-2% of the cells in a frame, so ~98% of REAL cells are supervised as BACKGROUND. The detection objective teaches the detector to stop firing on real, unannotated cells.
SYMPTOM, reproducible in every warm-start run: node recall drifts DOWN and node ratio goes negative. The plain 15-epoch joint baseline with NO auxiliary loss: recall 0.966 -> 0.936, ratio -0.15, within HALF an epoch. The contrastive arm showed the same slide, so the drift is the RECIPE, not the extra term - which also means my "contrastive is a trade" reading was partly measuring THIS.
THE ASYMMETRY IS THE KEY. From scratch the loss works (pilkwang reached 0.993 with it) because false-negative pressure is DIFFUSE and positives teach cellness faster than mislabelled negatives unteach it. Fine-tuning a SATURATED detector inverts it: the model already fires on thousands of unannotated true cells and each emits a confident wrong-answer gradient aimed exactly at its CORRECT detections. The better the detector, the harder this loss pushes it down. That is one mechanism for lna, ksv, tms all-199, the joint 1e-4 failure, and every prior "warm-start fine-tune degrades" result - they may have been measuring this artefact rather than the method under test.
FIX (in flight): do not supervise the undecidable. Where the model responds strongly and there is no annotation, the voxel is either an unannotated true cell or a false positive and our labels cannot say which - so it must contribute ZERO loss instead of asserting "false positive". One masking rule in BalancedBCE, threshold DERIVED from the inference operating point (0.97) not swept, negative normalisation over the SUPERVISED count so masking does not silently rescale the loss. Self-balancing: the masked fraction shrinks as the model sharpens.
VALIDATION: rerun the warm-start joint baseline with the mask and watch node RECALL (not the adjusted score - the node-count bonus hides recall loss). Recall holding near 0.966 instead of sliding to 0.936 confirms it.
STAKES: this is the difference between "our own weights cannot beat the pack" and "our loss punishes any detector better than our labels". The own-weights goal depends on it. ignore-threshold-bracketed-097-2026-08-10 (cheap two-sided test, one branch REFUTED - closes the ignore-threshold question): masking undecidable detection negatives helps, but LOWERING the threshold does not fix the residual recall slide - it breaks precision instead.
MEASURED at the same point (epoch 0.25, warm-start, lr 1e-5, cosine):
  mask 0.97 -> clamped 0.8476, recall 0.954, ratio -0.06, SAVED
  mask 0.50 -> clamped 0.8381, recall 0.945, ratio -0.03, not saved
READ THEM TOGETHER: at 0.5 the model detects MORE nodes (ratio -0.03 vs -0.06) yet hits FEWER annotated cells (0.945 vs 0.954). More firing, less hitting - masking most negatives removed the supervision that keeps detections PRECISE. That is the "too aggressive" branch of the pre-registered two-sided prediction, and it refutes lowering the threshold.
SO 0.97 STANDS (it is also the derived value - the shipped tracker s operating point, above which the pipeline would already call the voxel a cell). The 0.97 arm remains the campaign s best own-weights result on an unbiased selector: clamped 0.8513 at epoch 0.5 vs a 0.8398 init, saving at every window up to that point.
THE RESIDUAL SLIDE IS NOT A THRESHOLD PROBLEM. With 0.97 masking, recall still went 0.966 -> 0.954 -> 0.940 -> 0.933 and the clamped score peaked at epoch 0.5 then declined. Masking shifted the curve up and later WITHOUT changing its shape. Next lever, never swept since the joint trainer was built: DET_WEIGHT. Detection is saturated (0.992 recall at inference) and its loss is the biased one, so weight it DOWN and let association - where the score gap actually lives - dominate the shared trunk. Running at det_weight 0.1.
METHOD NOTE: the two-sided prediction is what made this cheap. Naming BOTH failure modes in advance (slide continues = too permissive; ratio goes positive / precision drops = too aggressive) meant a single 9-minute window could decide it, and the answer was the branch I thought less likely. selector-ranks-under-a-pipeline-we-dont-ship-2026-08-11 (READ FROM SOURCE, not measured - a standing bias in every checkpoint we have ever selected):

THE CHAIN: TrackerConfig.linker defaults to LinkerConfig() = name "assignment", disappearance_cost 0.0; TrackerConfig.bidirectional_edges defaults to False. So a bare TrackerConfig() IS the 0.892 pipeline. Our 0.895 pipeline (flow linker at boundary 3 + bidirectional harmonic fusion) exists ONLY as four literals inside the Kaggle kernel file. And BOTH trainers build the selector's tracker as TrackerConfig(threshold=<eval threshold>) - grafting the shipped THRESHOLD onto otherwise-default everything (joint_detector.py:711, tunet_detector.py:404).

SO EVERY CHECKPOINT THIS CAMPAIGN SELECTED WAS RANKED UNDER A LINKER WE DO NOT DEPLOY.

WHY IT IS A REAL BIAS, not bookkeeping: we have PROVEN the sign of an affinity-side change depends on its consumer - bidirectional fusion is -0.0027 under the per-frame assignment linker and +0.004 on the LEADERBOARD under the global flow linker. Checkpoint selection IS an affinity-side judgement (it ranks edge heads). A head that is better under flow can therefore LOSE selection under assignment, by the exact documented mechanism: softmax-over-sources bakes one-parent-per-target into the probability, which the assignment cost already imposes and a global solver does not.

THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE INSTRUMENT ERROR: (1) an isolated threshold ladder picked 0.96 while the shipped flow config prefers 0.97, order REVERSED; (2) the ranker measured +0.0032 in MotionHungarianLinker and negative in flow; (3) this. SWEEPING OR SELECTING IN A CONFIGURATION YOU DO NOT SHIP is the recurring error, and the selector is its widest instance because it silently shapes which WEIGHTS survive rather than which knob wins.

ALSO CHECK BEFORE QUOTING: dense_diagnosis, localisation, mitotic_appearance, seed_dispersion, corpus_audit all construct a bare TrackerConfig(). Runs where I passed --set linker.name=flow --set linker.disappearance_cost=3 --set bidirectional_edges=true are sound (the mislink and FP decompositions were); any diagnostic run WITHOUT those flags describes the 0.892 pipeline. The candidate-density audit is unaffected (reads gate_um, 10 in both).

FIX IS ARCHITECTURAL: give the shipped recipe ONE home - a named operating point in celltrack/operating_point.py that the kernel MOUNTS rather than restates, and that EvalCfg carries WHOLE instead of reducing to a single threshold field. EvalCfg already derives its threshold from TrackerConfig().threshold, which is the right instinct applied to one field out of fourteen.

TIMING RULE LEARNED ALONGSIDE: do NOT edit a shipped default while an arm is running - it silently changes what a running experiment measures. Sequence config changes after agents land. [[threshold-couples-to-the-linker-2026-08-10]] [[defaults-must-be-the-measured-best-2026-08-10]]

argued-constant-vs-noise-peak-2026-08-11 (AUDIT of our shipped constants after edge_blend turned out to be noise - and the distinction that stops the wrong one being removed):
TWO KINDS OF CONSTANT, and only one is a defect.
 (a) ARGUED, sitting on a plateau - fine. affinity_bonus = 2*gate = 20. Its sweeps are broad and flat: early 10/15/20/25/30/40/60 -> 0.9154/0.9196/0.9227/0.9216/0.9236/0.9207/0.9197 (30 actually reads ABOVE 20 by 0.0009), later 15/20/25/30 -> 0.9365/0.9412/0.9390/0.9397. So MEASUREMENT does not pick 20 - the spread across 15-40 is at or under the noise floor. What picks it is the ARGUMENT: in dense crowding the nearest-distance prior is anti-informative (the true successor is often NOT nearest), so the learned term needs fixed over-weighting beyond a scale match, and 2x the physical gate is the statement of that. The autobalance alternative was refuted for a mechanism reason (median-scale-match undershoots ~2.5x and hands the LOWEST weight to the most crowded movie). A constant chosen by argument and merely NOT CONTRADICTED by a flat sweep is legitimate.
 (b) UNARGUED, set from a peak inside the noise - a defect. edge_blend 0.8/0.2. The sweep that set it read 1.0/0.9/0.8/0.7/0.6/0.5/0.4 -> 0.9134/0.9146/0.9154/0.9140/0.9135/0.9136/0.9149: a +0.0018 "peak" over 0.5, below our 0.002 floor, and not monotone on either side (0.4 sits above 0.6 and 0.7). Re-measured today in the shipped config, 0.5/0.5 scores 0.9353 - IDENTICAL to 0.8/0.2 to four decimals. We carried noise shaped like a peak AND told a story about it ("seed1 s edge head is better, which is why only the EDGE blend is tilted, while the DETECTOR blend is self-balancing"). That story has no evidence: both blends are indifferent.
THE TEST TO APPLY to any shipped constant: can you state WHY this value, without pointing at a sweep? If yes, a flat sweep is corroboration and the constant stays. If the only justification IS the sweep, check the peak against the CURRENT noise floor - and if it does not clear it, the value is arbitrary, so prefer the SELF-BALANCING or symmetric choice (equal weights, no tilt) which needs no justification at all.
STATUS OF THE OTHERS, unchanged and still argued: gate_um 10 = max observed inter-frame displacement (9.96um, physical). threshold 0.97 / min_track 6 / smooth 0.8 = arbitrated by the LEADERBOARD, not the proxy, with A/B ladders on file. detector_blend None = equal, measured self-balancing. affinity_bonus None = 2*gate.
